articleTitle: Wideband Millimeter-wave AoD Design on the TFE of an OLED Display for 5G and B5G Handsets
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a leading and practical wideband millimeter-wave (mmw) antenna-on-display (AoD) design on the thin-film encapsulation (TFE) of an organic light-emitting diode (OLED) display for handsets of the 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> generation mobile communications (5G) and beyond 5G (B5G) to support all licensed mmw bands (i.e., n258, n257, n261, n260, n259, and n262) in the 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> generation partnership project (3GPP) for better wireless communication capabilities and promising for integrated sensing and communications (ISAC). Also, owing to the on-TFE design, multiple merits of thinner display modules, lower manufacturing complexity and costs, higher compatibility of touch sensors, and better visual performance can be achieved.

articleTitle: Structural Design and Preparation of a Star-Borne Passive Multi-Channel Waveguide Cavity Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: According to the electromagnetic simulation results, this paper presents the structural design of a 24-channel passive waveguide cavity filter, and provides the process realization path. The specific design and preparation process include layered design, independent processing, vacuum brazing, and final processing for a 24 channel passive waveguide cavity filter. The realization path of this technology work provides a new method for the integrated design and preparation of the subsequent multi-channel waveguide filter.

articleTitle: Experimental Research on Millimeter Wave Scattering Characteristics of Small UAV
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In view of the weak echo and low detectability of low, small and slow targets, this paper takes a typical small UAV as the target, carries out low-altitude flight detection and Ka-band scattering imaging experiments based on the turntable model, and obtains its dynamic scattering characteristics and high-resolution two-dimensional scattering imaging. The results can provide basic data support for subsequent target detection and recognition.

articleTitle: MATLAB-Based Decoding of NOAA Satellite Images Using V-Dipole Antenna and RTL-SDR
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper present design and build a low-cost and portable ground station to receive NOAA satellite APT images. Many believe that building a ground station requires expensive and special equipment like large parabolic dish antennas and specialized radio receivers. This project shows that it can be done with cheaper and simpler tools. NOAA satellites are continuously transfer weather data that helps in meteorology and disaster management. These satellites transmit Automatic Picture Transmission (APT) signals with global weather images at about 137.5 MHz. Each satellite uses a different frequency. We used SDR technology with an RTL-SDR receiver and a homemade V-Dipole antenna. The ground station tracks NOAA satellites and receives their signals. We use SDRSharp for tuning the frequency and record the signals. MATLAB processes and decodes the recorded signals to turn audio into high-resolution APT pictures. Our V-Dipole antenna performed best at 137.5 MHz, with a VSWR of 1.036 and a resistance of 42.095 ohms. This setup provide an excellent signal reception. The system successfully received and processed images from NOAA 15, 18, and 19 satellites. It shows that a low-cost ground station can work well and be efficient.

articleTitle: Path Loss Prediction Model Based on Enhanced Environment Characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Accurate wireless channel model is important for the assessment and optimal preparation of wireless communication systems, which raises the need for the accuracy of channel modeling. In order to solve the problems of incomplete feature extraction and insufficient model accuracy of the existing image-based regression prediction methods, a double-branch parallel neural network model is constructed by combining convolution and back propagation neural network. A path loss prediction method is proposed by integrating the characteristics of spatial environment. Based on the measured channels of campus scene, 11 geographic information features related to the receiver and transmitter are used as the traditional input feature vector, and the gray map image between them is extracted as the feature image input. The simulation results show that the proposed network model achieves good result on the test channel set through training and validation, the root-mean-square error between the measured and predicted value is 6.71 dB, which has high prediction accuracy for path loss.

articleTitle: Study of Shooting and Bouncing Ray Method Based on BVH Tree and GPU Acceleration
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To improve the computational efficiency of the shooting and bouncing ray (SBR) method, a graphics processing unit (GPU) parallel accelerated computation using the C++AMP platform was implemented in this paper. Using Morton code to convert the triangle data into a one-dimensional linear space maintains the spatial proximity of each triangle. This optimization enhances the efficiency of spatial retrieval and data querying, as well as improves the efficiency of constructing bounding volume hierarchies (BVH) trees and collision detection. By comparing with the ray launching geometrical optics (RL-GO) method, this paper to enhance the computational efficiency of the SBR method, and the radar cross section (RCS) results are in agreement with RL-GO. Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) images of an aircraft target were calculated, and the imaging results demonstrate that this paper can correctly reflect the target's structural information, highlighting the effectiveness of the method in this paper.

articleTitle: An OTFS Waveform Based Delay-Doppler Domain Channel Sounding Method for High-Mobility Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Channel measurements are the prerequisite for the design of communication systems in high-mobility scenarios. Conventional channel sounding methods cannot directly obtain Doppler characteristics in such scenarios, making the development of new methods highly attractive. In this paper, we propose a delay-Doppler (DD) domain channel sounding method that utilizes an orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) waveform as the excitation signal to extract the channel spreading function (CSF). Additionally, a practical fractional delay-Doppler estimation algorithm is proposed to enhance the precision of channel measurements. This method is implemented by a DD domain channel sounding system, which includes the entire process of transmitting, receiving and processing the OTFS signal. Based on this system, channel measurements are conducted for vehicle-to-everything (V2X) scenarios in urban areas. Statistical results, involving root-mean-square (RMS) delay spread and RMS Doppler spread are derived, which validate the effectiveness of the proposed method and provide realistic references for research on V2X communications.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Scattering Model of Three-Layer Vegetation
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aiming at the three-layer vegetation scattering model, this paper uses Monte-Carlo to study and calculate the canopy of the three-layer model, randomly generate discrete particles (ellipsoids) to simulate the canopy, and perform coherent superposition on the scattering field calculated by Rayleigh-Gans (GRG) method for each particle. The scattering field of the dielectric cylinder can be approximated by the internal field of the dielectric cylinder of limited length under the same physical condition. Compared with the traditional three-layer vegetation scattering model, the coupling between scattering particles in the canopy layer and the ground, the high-order scattering effect between adjacent tree trunk scatters, the attenuation and absorption of electromagnetic waves in the canopy layer and trunk layer, as well as the contribution of direct scattering from the ground to the total scattering are considered. In particular, the electromagnetic scattering model of ground trees based on Monte Carlo method is established by modifying the reflection coefficient to calculate the ground reflection field and considering the influence of ground tilt and trunk tilt on scattering.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic Wireless Power and Data Transmission Technology Across Conical Metal Shell
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aiming to address the issue of wireless power and data transmission in closed conical metal shell, the ultrasonic transducer is introduced into the system. The system for ultrasonic transmission is constructed with a pair of radially polarized circular tube transducers, a metal spacer block attached to one of the transducers, and a conical shell. The finite element analysis software COMSOL is utilized to investigate the modal changes in the system during power transmission, while also analyzing the impact of receiving transducer height and relative position on power transmission. Ultrasonic data communication experimental results demonstrate that reliable data can be transmitted across the conical shell using binary frequency shift keying modulation and demodulation techniques at a communication rate reaching 1kbps.

articleTitle: Design of Ka-Band Chip-to-Antenna Transition Structure Based on Glass Packaging Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The Ka-band millimeter-wave chip and its advanced packaging technology have important application value in high-speed satellite communications, 5G mobile communication, phased-array radar and other fields. In order to improve the electromagnetic transmission performance and thermal stability of the millimeter-wave on-chip integration system, and at the same time reduce the cost of process, this article proposes a ka-band chip-to-antenna transition structure based on glass packaging technology to achieve the low-loss transmission characteristics of 35 ~ 45 GHz electromagnetic signal. The results of the three-dimensional electromagnetic simulation indicate that the proposed transition structure can achieve good impedance matching in Ka band, the transmission loss is as low as 0.22 dB at 40 GHz, and it shows good impedance matching at different frequencies by regulating single structure parameter. The ka-band transition structure based on glass process in this article processing the good electromagnetic performances, good thermal stability, low process cost, and adjustable operating frequency, has rich application prospects.

articleTitle: The Application of a Novel Ray-Splitting Dual-Port SBR Algorithm in Aircraft Inlet*
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The conventional SBR algorithm is realized in this paper and the validation study is conducted firstly. Then, a novel ray-splitting dual-port SBR (DP-SBR) algorithm is proposed and the basic implementation of improvement of this algorithm is demonstrated. The proposed algorithm is able to simulate RCS of aircraft inlet with dielectric grilles installed. The algorithm is utilized on rectangular inlet with dielectric grilles and the results present that capability of DP-SBR in engineering applications of aircraft engine design.

articleTitle: An RF Signal Amplification and Power Detection 3D System-in-Package (SIP) Design Based on HDI Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a 3D SIP (system in package) design of four-channel power detection and signal amplification. It used HDI(High-Density Interconnect) technology to vertically interconnect different MMIC(monolithic microwave integrated circuits), which has been validated to have minimum impact on its performance. The proposed 3D-SIP has been highly integrated into a volume of 2.05mm × 1.6mm × 0.4mm with BGA(ball grid array) output and input, the maximum receive gain is 11.3 dB at 16Ghz.

articleTitle: Parallel Electromagnetic Simulations based on Novel Refinement Templates of AMR
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A new adaptive refinement method and its parallel implementation of adaptive mesh refinement is developed by regrouping the tetrahedra into 7 refinement templates. In the parallel refinement process, our method only transfers nonconformity messages and refining requirements between corresponding submeshes. The communication algorithm is utilized to update shared information, eliminating the need for a global index in the refinement process. Numerical experiments of a printed dipole antenna, patch antenna, and printed circuit board are presented to validate the accuracy of our new parallel refinement method.

articleTitle: Low Complexity Time Domain Channel Equalizer for CP-OTFS Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: As an important component of signal demodulation, efficient channel equalization is required for stable data reception in Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) systems. The key to channel equalization design is to strike a balance between complexity and decoding performance with known channel characteristics and the performance of the equalization algorithm. Based on this, we present a channel equalization algorithm called Least Square Minimum Residual based on Successive Interference Cancellation (LSMR-SIC). It fully takes advantage of the sparsity of the Cyclic Prefix-OTFS (CP-OTFS) channel matrix and the resilience of the least squares minimum residual to achieve fast convergence and low complexity with good Bit Error Rate (BER) performance.

articleTitle: The Influence of Jungle Background on the Dispersal Pattern of Fuze Explosion Points
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To address the poor adaptability of guided suppression fuzes in jungle backgrounds and enhance radio fuzes' target detection, identification, and anti-jamming capabilities, a study was conducted on the impact of jungle background on fuze burst point control accuracy. Based on the measured data of the backward scattering characteristics of the jungle collected by the fuze, the distribution characteristics of fuze burst points under different wavebands and pitch angles in the jungle background were obtained. The study analyzed the effects of the jungle environment on the fuze's distance-setting accuracy. The findings indicate a strong correlation between the distribution of burst points and the electromagnetic scattering characteristics of the jungle. The dispersion of burst points follows a Gaussian distribution. At a test distance of 30 m, with fuze wavebands in the K, Ka, and V bands and HH polarization, and pitch angles between 30° and 60°, the impact of the jungle background on burst point deviation is within the range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm \mathbf{5} \mathbf{m}$</tex>. The distance distribution of the fuze is 33.5-34.5 m on asphalt surfaces, while it significantly increases to 32–41 m in jungle backgrounds, with a dispersion increase rate of 77%.

articleTitle: The Influence of Raw Data Selection on the Rain Attenuation Forecast of Grey System
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this study, the application of grey system theory in short-term prediction of rain attenuation is explored, with the objective of enhancing the accuracy and reliability of rain attenuation forecasting in the field of wireless communications. Based on the measured data from a rainfall event in 2021 at Qingdao Station, the GM(l,l) model within grey system theory is employed to forecast rain attenuation at the next 30s mark. Through systematic analysis of the influence of varying numbers of raw data on prediction results, it is found that selecting an appropriate number of raw data is crucial for improving prediction accuracy. Experimental results indicate that during periods of significant variation in rain attenuation, increasing the number of raw data can lead to abnormal values in prediction outcomes, thereby magnifying prediction errors. Consequently, using a smaller dataset for prediction effectively mitigates errors. By optimizing the program and eliminating outliers, the predicted values of rain attenuation at the next 30s mark generated by the grey system theory align closely with the actual values, validating the effectiveness and practicality of this method.

articleTitle: Improved Matrix Mapping Method for Rectangular Planar Array Beampattern Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes an improved approach for synthesizing sparse planar arrays using the improved matrix mapping method. By converting the optimization of array element positions into the optimization of increments in the x and y directions, the proposed method effectively addresses the challenges of designing sparse planar arrays under multiple constraints. These constraints include array aperture, element count, and minimum spacing between adjacent elements, while also avoiding infeasible solutions. Compared to existing matrix mapping methods, this approach affords greater flexibility in the allocation of the number of elements and their positional distribution. Numerical and full-wave simulations have validated the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed method, demonstrating its superior performance over existing solutions.

articleTitle: Design of the In-Situ Measurement System for Electromagnetic Radiation Characteristics Based on Spatial Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With the increasing number of electronic equipment loaded by large equipment and platforms, large equipment and platforms are facing more and more serious electromagnetic compatibility problems. This paper proposes the in-situ measurement system for electromagnetic radiation characteristics based on spatial filtering, which can detect the electromagnetic radiation performance of large equipment and platform with large volume and many equipment that cannot be transported to the standard open field or standard indoor field for measurement. The system consists of hardware and software, which can effectively filter out the environmental electromagnetic interference in the field test. Compared to conventional electromagnetic compatibility test systems, the system provides greater real-time capability, mainly in the frequency range from 300 MHz to 6 GHz. The measurement results show that the system can quickly and accurately extract useful signals in the presence of broadband width, high dynamic and transient signals, and can effectively suppress many types of interference such as narrow band and broadband, with the interference suppression capacity of more than 20 dB.

articleTitle: Design of a Planar Ultra- Wideband Modular Array for UHF Band
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To decrease the profile of ultra-wideband antenna array at UHF -band, a modular designed PUMA array is presented in this paper. With the use of FSS WAIM, profile of the element is decreased to 0.347 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</inf>. The array is fed by a novel SSMP balun connector, which obtain a wide operating bandwidth performance over 0.4GHz~2GHz for broadside scanning active VSWR <3. Simulated radiation patterns indicate that the proposed UHF -band element exhibits a well cross polarization below -15dB.

articleTitle: A Single Feed Wide Axial Ratio Circularly Polarized Dielectric Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A single feed circularly polarized dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is proposed in this paper. The DRA integrated an eight-arm Archimedean spiral (EAAS). A cross slot is placed in the middle of the ground for feeding the antenna. The EAAS DRA has a wide impedance bandwidth of 40.4% (1.46-2.20 GHz) and axial ratio bandwidth of 39.1% (1.46-2.17 GHz).

articleTitle: A New Synchronization Estimation Algorithm for MIL-SOQPSK
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A New Synchronous Estimation Algorithm for SOQPSK signal without data assistance is put forward. The algorithm first estimates the frequency of residual carrier after down conversion, and then estimates the carrier phase and symbol synchronization parameters. The algorithm is simulated and compared with MCRB. The results show that the estimation algorithm performance is close to MCRB.

articleTitle: Improved Air-Stripline Using PCB Technology And Research on Its Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents an improved air-stripline using PCB technology for low loss and easy assembly. Compared with traditional stripline based on two layers of substrates, the insertion loss of the design herein is lower, while compared with traditional air-stripline based on suspended transmission line, the improved stripline in this paper is easier to be fabricated and assembled due to the absence of the nylon screw. The proposed air-stripline is simulated and discussed. Furthermore, a 1:8 power divider and a linear array with 8 units are designed based on the proposed stripline to clarify its application. Measured results show that the maximum insertion loss of the power divider over 4.5GHz-6.5GHz is better than 9.3dB, which is 0.3dB higher than the theoretical value, and the realized peak gain of the linear array is 13.1dB at the center frequency 5.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Improvement of Radiation Pattern Roundness of Patch Antennas for Radar Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A patch antenna with enhanced pattern roundness achieved through ground slot loading is proposed. By incorporating radiation from the slots, the pattern roundness is significantly improved. This paper discusses the principle behind the slots' effect on the antenna pattern and examines the impact of slots of varying sizes on the improvement of roundness. Measured results demonstrate that the roundness of the antenna radiation pattern is improved by 5.5 dB within the operating band of the microwave radar sensor.

articleTitle: Measurements and Characteristics Analysis of Millimeter Wave Channel Trough the Over-the-Horizon Marine Evaporation Duct
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This study investigates the propagation characteristics of 25 GHz millimeter wave (mmWave) signals in maritime evaporation ducts through fixed-to-fixed point maritime channel measurements in the South China Sea. Utilizing high-performance equipment such as USRP X310 and 25 GHz converters, the research aimed to understand the impact of environmental factors on signal propagation. Key findings include slightly higher path loss (PL) values in the evaporation duct compared to line-of-sight (LOS) free space, indicating duct-enhanced signal propagation. The study also observed frequency-selective behavior and the influence of factors like water vapor absorption and sea surface roughness on PL. Continuous channel impulse response (CIR) snapshots were collected under various environmental conditions. Analysis revealed stable signal power at millisecond level, The variation period of received signal power is similar to that of ocean wave spectrum, which is in the level of seconds. The study provides valuable insights for the development of future maritime communication technology.

articleTitle: Transmission Characterization of Power-Exponential Airy Beams in Complex Turbulence
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The main objective of this work is to analyze the transmission properties of power-exponential Airy beams following their propagation through air and then plasma turbulence. The study first establishes the mathematical models describing the Airy beam and the LG beam at the field source, respectively. Then, using the paraxial approximation condition of Huygens-Fresnel, the expression for the transmission of the Airy beam in the free space is derived from the polar coordinate expression of the Airy beam at the field source. The light intensity and phase distributions of Airy beams and LG beams are then compared after transmission through each turbulence using the random phase screen theory, and the analysis leads to the conclusion that Airy beams are more appropriate for transmission in more complex turbulence environments. Power-exponential Airy beams are better at reducing the effect of turbulence than ordinary laser light sources because they have numerous orbital angular momentum modes at the field source, which lessens the effect of turbulence on individual modes. The comprehension of Airy beam transmission in intricate settings and the enhancement of their efficiency in real-world uses are crucial implications of our findings.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Band Microstrip Circulator for X and Ku Bands
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With the rapid development of mobile communications, there has been a demand for wideband or dual-band capabilities in antennas and RF devices to meet the requirements of multiple communication systems, reduce interference between antennas operating at different frequencies, and lower costs. This paper presents a dual-band microstrip circulator designed for X-band (9 GHz) and Kuband (16.5 GHz) communication system. The design results are as follows: for the X-band frequency, the operational bandwidth is 3 GHz, isolation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\geq \mathbf{18\ {dB}}$</tex>, insertion loss <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq \mathbf{0.3}$</tex> dB, and VSWR <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq 1.25$</tex>. For the Ku-band frequency, the operational bandwidth is 300 MHz, isolation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\geq 18 \text{dB}$</tex>, insertion loss <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq \mathbf{0.5\ {dB}}$</tex>, and VSWR <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq \mathbf{1.25}$</tex>.

articleTitle: A Low Sidelobe Microstrip Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A low sidelobe miniaturized series feed microstrip antenna array is presented in the paper. The antenna adopts a microstrip-fed patch and sixteen microstrip antenna units arranged in a line array. By using weighted feeding method, the width of the patch elements is adjusted, so as to optimize the sidelobe level of E-plane. The designed antenna utilizes a series feed method, giving the antenna characteristics of a compact structure and low profile. The feed method can effectively reduce the cost and volume of feed network, raise the antenna radiation efficiency and space utilization. The results indicate that the gain of the antenna is above 17dB in the working band, and the sidelobe is -28dB. The half-power beamwidth in the E-plane is 7.8 degrees. The antenna can be used in 76.5GHz vehicle-mounted radar system.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Orthogonally Scanning and Dual-Polarized Multibeam Antenna Based on SIW Shared-Cavity Rotman
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A shared-cavity Rotman lens for an orthogonally scanning and dual-polarized (OSDP) multibeam array is realized using substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology. The core of the design is using two Rotman-type multibeam beam-forming networks (MBFNs) orthogonally combine, each of which is primarily shaped by a feed contour and an array contour of a traditional Rotman lens. These MBFNs share the common lens cavity, thus the compactness and integration are significantly improved. It can generate orthogonal scans and dual polarizations after connecting to the radiation portion. Using this method, an SIW OSDP multibeam array is designed, simulated, and fabricated.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Ionospheric Variations in Guangzhou During the 24th Solar Activity Cycle
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The ionosphere, as an important part of the solar-terrestrial space environment, has far-reaching significance for the design, development, production, testing and operation of radio information systems. The 24th solar activity cycle is a relatively weak activity cycle in history, and the change characteristics of the equatorial anomaly region of the ionosphere are also different from those in the past due to its influence. In this paper, the changing characteristics of the ionospheric foF2 in the hump zone solar activity week are analyzed in detail, taking the Guangzhou area as an example. The following conclusions were drawn: The number of strong ionospheric disturbances is the lowest in 2013, and the number of strong disturbances is the highest in 2009; the correlation between the fluctuation of foF2 and F10.7 from 09:00 to 20:00 LT is low; the probability of the occurrence of the spread F in the high solar activity year is low, which is less than half of that in the low solar activity year.

articleTitle: Multi-Material FDTD Modeling of Vehicle Based on CAD Model with ASE Format
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: It is necessary to distinguish the materials in the electromagnetic simulation model in addition to the accuracy of the geometry. The CAD model of a vehicle contains accurate geometric data and material information. The CAD model is transformed into an ASE format text-readable file. The triangular surfaces data of objects are read to calculate the intersection location with the grid line, and the material number of triangular surface is recorded at the location. The location and material of all the Yee cells are determined one by one, and the multi-material model is constructed. Based on the modeling practice of some vehicles, the general requirements of CAD model for FDTD method are put forward. Two examples of HEMP coupling to vehicle are compared with the software calculation results, and the validity of the multi-material FDTD modeling based on ASE format file is verified. The modeling method presented in this paper can provide reference for the construction of high precision FDTD model.

articleTitle: Sky-Ground Wave Signal Separation in Enhanced Loran Based on Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This article proposes a high-precision algorithm for ELoran signal sky-ground wave separation based on particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. The simulation results show that the performance of this algorithm is significantly better than other algorithms, especially in low signal-to-noise ratio situations. The algorithm proposed in this paper has higher accuracy and stability. For actual measured signals, this algorithm can accurately separate the sky and earth wave signals and is easy to implement in engineering.

articleTitle: A Conformal Reconfigurable Antenna Array for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{4}\times \mathbf{4}$</tex> conformal frequency reconfigurable antenna array for UAV is presented. The proposed array is tuned by varactor diodes. Simulated results show that the operating frequency of the proposed array in the bending case can vary within 4.7-5.4 GHz. A <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{4}\times \mathbf{4}$</tex> array prototype was fabricated and measured. Both simulated and measured results show that the realized gain of the prototype can reach more than 17 dBi. Moreover, the proposed array can achieve a gain of more than 10 dBi over a 20° range and the cross polarization ratios are all higher than 25 dB. The measured results preliminarily verified the expected performance of the design scheme.

articleTitle: Research on Target Quantity and Distance Identification Method for Through-Wall Radar Based on CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The deep learning technology is combined with the through wall radar imaging method, and the research is carried out through the combination of simulation and experiment. The specific contents include:gprMax based through wall radar sim-ulation. gprMax software is used to establish the detection model of through wall radar and realize the simulation. The simulation data are collected and the appropriate method is selected for clutter filtering, which lays the foundation for the radar data processing obtained from the experiment. Through wall radar experiment: use the life detector radar of the laboratory to do the actual scene experiment, and obtain the experimental data of different people at different distances in the detection area, which will be converted into pictures for later processing. Establish neural network model. The radar echo image obtained from the experiment is cut and processed and sent to the neural network for training, and the number and distance of targets in the image are correctly predicted.

articleTitle: Design of L-Band Small-Sized Cavity Filters
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces a third-order cavity filter operating at a frequency range of 1.2-1.4 GHz. The filter adopts a direct coupling topology, which is simple and easy to optimize design and process. Compared to a cross-coupling filter, the direct coupling structure is more widely used in practical industrial applications Additionally, a gradient optimization algorithm is utilized to optimize the coupling matrix, which in turn optimizes the transmission zero points. This results in the filter exhibiting better performance in terms of in-band insertion loss and out-of-band suppression.

articleTitle: A Design of Broadband Rib-Type Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a broadband antenna conformal to avian ribs. The proposed antenna consists of a symmetrical archeddipole combined with two L-shaped monopoles, allowing for a perfect fit with the avian skeletal structure, where the arched dipole and the two L-shaped monopoles each have different resonant frequencies, and can be adjusted independently by their lengths, giving the antenna a relatively wide operation bandwidth. The simulated results demonstrate that the proposed antenna achieves a 10 dB impedance bandwidth of 45.7% (0.81-1.29 GHz). It also exhibits high radiation efficiency and nearly omnidirectional radiation patterns within the operational bandwidth.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Absorption Cross Section of Chrome Sprayed Coatings in a Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the absorption cross sections of chrome sprayed coatings are measured in a reverberation chamber. Measurement results quantified the loss of chrome paintings in a reverberation chamber, results show that the loss from the thin chrome paintings is not significant when the frequency is lower than 20 GHz.

articleTitle: A Muti-Bit Flip Successive Cancellation Decoder for Polar Codes
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A decoding algorithm for polar codes based on successive cancellation is proposed in this paper, which determines the location of multiple bit errors by calculating the maximum likelihood result of successive cancellation decoding, and achieves the improvement of decoding performance by flipping the values of multiple bits. Simulation results show that the proposed multi-bit flip decoding algorithm exhibits better performance than the single-bit flip decoding algorithm with the same-order computational complexity under the additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN). In addition, as the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) increases, the complexity of the proposed algorithm approaches that of the successive cancellation decoder.

articleTitle: A Fast RCS Prediction Method for 3D Dielectric Target Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a method based on machine learning is proposed to accelerate the computation of radar cross section (RCS) for three-dimensional dielectric targets. Firstly, to construct a compact dataset, the input is changed from traditional mesh data to point cloud, and the traditional equivalent source distribution is expressed as inherent feature parameters (IFPs) with the help of characteristic mode theory. Subsequently, machine learning techniques are introduced to construct a neural network model for training the IFPs with reference to the PointNet neural network. Experiments show that the proposed method can accurately predict the RCS while significantly reducing the memory overhead and runtime compared with the method of moments (MoM), and achieves a fast and accurate end-to-end mapping from a target's structural attributes to its electromagnetic properties.

articleTitle: The Impact of the Sea on the RCS of Ship Targets at Different Incident Plane Wave Angles
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: It is crucial to choose an appropriate incident plane wave angle for accurately measuring the radar cross section (RCS) of ship targets at sea, as an unsuitable angle can significantly amplify the impact from the sea. In this paper, the impact of the sea on the RCS of ship targets at different incident plane wave angles is investigated. Firstly, a typical ship target model is selected, and a sea model composed of planar patches is simulated based on the Pierson-Moskowitz spectrum(P-M spectrum). Secondly, simulations using FEKO software are conducted to analyze the impact. The simulation results prove that the sea has minimal impact on the RCS of ship targets at an incident plane wave angle θ is approximately 30 degrees, with an average deviation of less than 3 dB.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal Prediction of Real Ocean Physical Environmental Factors and Dynamic Multi-Scale Sea Surface Geometry Modeling Based on AI
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The prediction of ocean physical environmental factors has important applications in radar detection, target recognition, remote sensing, telemetry, communication, and navigation. However, due to the extensive coverage and multiple dimensions of the ocean environment, traditional methods find it challenging to achieve accurate and real-time spatiotemporal predictions of ocean physical environmental factors. This paper utilizes models based on Deep Neural Networks (DNN) and Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTM) to achieve spatiotemporal prediction of ocean physical environmental factors in different sea areas of China. By collecting multi-source and multi-dimensional ocean spatiotemporal physical field data, we constructed prediction models for ocean environmental physical fields using LSTM and DNN. The proposed models demonstrate faster speeds, better accuracy, and greater stability compared to traditional methods in predicting various ocean physical environmental factors such as wind speed, wind direction, wave height, wave direction, wave period, and temperature. Utilizing a real ocean environmental factor database combined with high-performance GPU technology, we established dynamic multi-scale sea surface geometry models for different sea areas based on different radar electromagnetic parameters. This provides theoretical foundation and technical support for ocean environment situational awareness, radar target detection and clutter suppression, high-resolution satellite remote sensing, and over-the-horizon communication.

articleTitle: An New Leapforg-ADI-FDTD Method for Lorentzian Media
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The Lorentz model is suitable for describing the dispersion properties of biological tissues and metamaterials. In order to break through the CFL condition, the existing FDTD method adopts a two-step ADI implementation scheme for the Lorentz model, and the curl equation and the constitutive relations are solved by semi-implicit scheme. In this paper, we present a Leapfrog-ADI implementation of the FDTD method to address the Lorentz model, and the constitutive relations solved by the explicit method. The numerical results underscore the feasibility and efficiency of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Discriminating Polarimetric Backscattering Characteristics between Chaff Jamming and Ships
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the discriminating polarimetric characteristics for chaff jamming and ship targets is studied. The polarization invariant properties of chaff clouds and ships are compared, and the features with noticeable statistical differences are selected as the discriminating characteristics. The separability between chaff clouds and ships are demonstrated using support vector machine (SVM). Simulation results suggest that this set of polarization features can effectively discriminate ship targets from chaff jamming under moderate SNR, achieving a discrimination rate above 90%.

articleTitle: Review on the Innovative Structural Design of Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Array antenna, as one kind of complex electronic equipment, has been widely applied in the fields of ground, sea, air and space as the core equipment of aerospace, air defense, and early warning detection. The mechanical structure of the antenna is not only the carrier for the electromagnetic performance, but also restricts the realization of the performance. The complex service environment and multiple types of antenna platforms have raised more demands on the structure design of the array antenna. For example, the antenna for the airborne platform faces severe restrictions on space, weight, and high-density heat dissipation, and for the missile-borne platform is subjected to high temperature ablation of the radome. Moreover, with the increase of antenna frequency and the development of structural integration, these impact and constraints have become tighter, resulting in the seriously restriction of realizing the high-performance antenna. The traditional antenna structure design concept and system architecture need to undergo significant changes in order to meet the increasing demands, as array antenna has extended its important role in more fields including 5G/6G communications, meteorological observation and satellite broadcasting. Following are some new ideas and suggestions on the key technologies of future structure design of array antenna from five aspects.

articleTitle: Smoke Diffusion Feature Extraction and Concentration Prediction Method Based on Canny Edge Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In the dynamic intersection scene between laser detector and smoke interference, it is difficult to quantitatively describe the smoke state parameter information of laser detection optical path at different times due to the fluidity and randomness of smoke. This paper proposes a smoke diffusion video feature extraction and concentration prediction method based on Canny edge detection. This method extracts high-speed video of smoke diffusion, detects the edge of the video image and segments the smoke area, analyzes and obtains the corresponding relationship between the shielding effect of smoke diffusion, the number of image pixels in the transmission path and the smoke concentration, By extracting the shielding effect of 1, 2, and 4 typical smoke scenes during diffusion, and analyzing the number of image pixels of a certain transmission path of smoke diffusion, the smoke impact in the dynamic intersection scene of the laser detector and smoke interference is quantified. Subsequently, the laser detector dynamic intersection scene and detection beam parameters can be combined to quantitatively describe the relative position of the laser beam in the smoke transmission path and the concentration state estimation in different forms of smoke scenes, providing important support for the time-correspondence of the echo signal and the optimization of the smoke interference algorithm.

articleTitle: Compact Flexible Tri-Notched Patch Antenna for UWB Application
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this research, a CPW fed UWB antenna with specific notched band features has been designed. The antenna specifically filters out narrow-band signals in the frequencies utilized by WLAN, Wi-MAX, and X-band satellite communications, optimizing its function within the UWB spectrum. The triple-band-notched features of the proposed antenna are achieved by integrating nested Cshaped apertures into both the central and lower sections of the elliptical radiating patch. The experimental outcomes demonstrate that the antenna exhibits a return loss of less than or equal to -10 dB throughout the entire band, except for notched frequency bands. The antenna is flexible, lightweight, and has an ultra-thickness of 0.0508mm. This research is significant because of the increasing demand for UWB technology in various applications, including radar systems, healthcare monitoring, military communications, and home networking systems.

articleTitle: Vision Transformer-Based Passive Beamforming for RIS-Assisted Multi-User Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a geometrical cluster-based channel model is proposed for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted multi-user communications, where line-of-sight (LoS) and non-LoS components are considered in BS-RIS and RIS-Rx links. Then, a novel solution method of RIS phase is presented based on vision transformer (ViT) network, which intuitively solves RIS phase by position of multiple users and reduces solution complexity. Based on the proposed model, the impacts of RIS on CIR magnitude and coverage probability are simulated and analyzed. The results show that RIS phase generated by ViT network can achieve fairly well solution and increase channel condition, which can provide a foundation for deploying and designing RIS-assisted multi-user systems.

articleTitle: Developments of On-Chest Four Bands PLB Antenna for Maritime Search and Rescue Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel four band on-chest MLA over the seawater plane is presented. It is based on-chest vertical split monopole antenna (VSMA) achievements. Simulated results shown that the meander line antenna (MLA) with size of 95×72.1×13.6mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, can meet the requirements of advanced personal locator beacon (PLB) system of 83.7×70.1×27.6mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> in size. Its 10dB return loss bandwidth at 121.5, 162, 243 and 406 MHz are 1.4, 2.4, 13.0 and 10.0 MHz respectively. Its performance, including achieved bandwiths and beam patterns, imply its potential for maritime search and rescue applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of Over-the-Horizon Transmission in Real Land-Sea Junction Regions with Ducting
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Stable and persistent atmospheric ducting over land can potentially disrupt normal transmission and reception in TDD systems, causing long-distance interference between cities. Due to the evaporative effects, stable ducting structures are almost always present over the sea, which can impact base station communications in coastal cities. This paper determines the occurrence of ducting through meteorological station data in coastal cities and uses the WRF numerical model to simulate the ducting coverage in the coastal area around these meteorological stations. We select a coastal urban area for long-distance ducting communication analysis. The sea surface is generated based on real marine meteorological data, and the selected area's land cover type follows the IGBP global vegetation classification scheme. Considering the dielectric constant of the land cover, we analyze the long-distance ducting transmission in the land-sea interface links and compare the results with AREPS simulations.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Lightweight Dual-Polarized Waveguide Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The transmission mode of coaxial waveguide is TEM mode, based on the transmission characteristic, a dual-polarization waveguide antenna with high radiation efficiency and good cross polarization characteristics is presented. The waveguide antenna adopts the structure form of rectangular coaxial waveguide, its cutoff frequency is equal to zeros, by means of taking advantage of the transmission characteristic of the coaxial waveguide, this article reduces the cross section size and achieves the miniaturization,lightweight design. Compared with conventional waveguide antenna, the results show that the rectangular coaxial dual-polarization waveguide antenna has the characteristics of high polarization purity and high radiation efficiency; at the same time, its weight is reduced by more than 30% and its profile is reduced by more than 40%, providing new ideas for the miniaturization and lightweight design of waveguide antennas, possessing certain engineering application value.

articleTitle: Near-Sea Surface Meteorological Parameters Influences on Electromagnetic Wave Propagation
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The modified refractivity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(M)$</tex> has a direct impact on the operational effectiveness of radio systems such as radar. Because the near-sea surface is affected by ocean spray, solar radiation, etc., the sea-air interaction is more intense, resulting in more dramatic changes in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> at near-sea surface. In order to analyze the influence of meteorological parameters changes on the electromagnetic (EM) wave propagation in near-sea surface, this paper obtained the measured data of near-sea surface meteorology and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> in the South China Sea by Shiptime Sharing Project. Under different atmospheric conditions, the change of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> deviation of the fitted <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M-\text{curve}$</tex> from the measured <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> is comparatively analyzed at the near-sea surface. The influences of their differences on the EM wave propagation loss is further analyzed based on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M-\text{curve}$</tex> obtained separately according to whether or not consider the meteorological parameters of the near surface. The results show that at near-sea surface, whether or not to consider the meteorological parameters will lead to deviations in the calculation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>, and will cause different degrees of EM wave propagation loss under different atmospheric conditions. The larger deviation is as high as 32.78 percent with the EM wave propagation loss. Therefore, in order to improve the performance of radar and other radio systems, the observation of near-sea surface meteorological parameters should not be ignored.

articleTitle: A Full Planar Low-Profile Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Antenna Based on Structure Reusing
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A low-profile dual-band dual-polarized full planar antenna is developed by structure reusing. The antenna is made up of 4×4 square rings. All the square rings form the low-band antenna (LBA). Four center square rings serve as high-band antenna (HBA), which are also part of the LBA. The LBA is differentially fed with four feeding probes. The HBA is excited by two coaxial cables. Because the LBA reuses the HBA, the dual-band antenna has a full planar structure. The dual-band antenna achieves impedance matching of VSWR < 1.5 for the low band (LB) of 1.38-1.53 GHz and the high band (HB) of 1.76-2.06 GHz. The port isolation is > 43 dB in the LB and > 30 dB in the HB. A 4-element dual-band dual-polarized full planar antenna array has been investigated to demonstrate the potential of the proposed antenna in base station applications.

articleTitle: Locating Technology of Civil Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Based on Muti-Illuminator Single-Channel Non-Cooperative Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: As the rapid development and application of various UAVs brings increasingly severe safety threaten. To solve the problem that it is hard to detect and locate the electromagnetic silent UAV in civil environment, we propose a locating technology of civil UAVs based on single-channel multiilluminator non-cooperative detection, in which ubiquitous radiation sources such as the mobile base stations and the radio/television stations are utilized as the illuminators. The effectiveness of the proposed technology is verified by the experiment results with actual UAVs.

Author Keywords: unmanned aerial vehicles monitoring and location

articleTitle: The Response of Quasi-Two-Day Waves to the 2013 Major Stratospheric Sudden Warming Over Low-Latitude Region
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The stratospheric sudden warming (SSW) is an important phenomenon in which the stratospheric temperature in the high latitude region suddenly rises of several K in a few days. This phenomenon can strongly affect the dynamics and thermal balance in the middle atmosphere and/or the near space region. Past observational and modelling studies have shown the influence of SSWs, but the impact of SSWs on the quasi-two-day waves (Q2DWs) has not been fully understood. In this study, we report the response of Q2DWs in the low-latitude mesosphere and lower thermosphere (MLT) region to the 2013 major SSW. The quasi-two-day waves are observed by the Kunming (25.6°N, 103.8°E) meteor radar. The 2013 SSW is identified by the ModernEra Retrospective analysis for Research and Applications, version 2 (MERRA-2) reanalysis dataset. The observation provides a clear enhancement of the amplitudes of Q2DWs in both zonal and meridional wind components during the 2013 major SSW. Besides, the SSW can also affect the horizontal winds in the low-latitude MLT region. This finding provides a valuable insight to better understand the coupling between stratosphere and mesosphere.

articleTitle: Design and Performance of Spaceborne Active Low-Frequency Subsurface Radar System
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The World Radiocommunication Conference 2023 (WRC-23) expanded the frequency range of spaceborne active radar for earth observation, of which 40MHz~50MHz was allowed for the first time to carry out subsurface active radar penetration detection missions, making spaceborne radar detection of glaciers in the Earth region a hot topic. This paper introduces a single-satellite low-frequency active radar detection system with two-band low-frequency active radar detection capabilities, which can achieve a performance index of 4km detection depth for polar glaciers. This paper simulates and analyzes the resolution and coverage performance achieved by the system. The results show that by combining the advantages of the two frequency bands, the technical index of horizontal resolution better than 2km can be achieved. The radar has the ability to cover more than 95 % of the area in the Arctic for 6 months, and has great application prospects in desert groundwater and underground structure detection.

articleTitle: Efficient Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method for Solving Electromagnetic Scattering in Layered Anisotropies
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this article, we propose an efficient numerical method for layered models based on the conventional finite difference time-domain (FDTD) method. The three-dimensional (3-D) layered model is compressed into one-dimensional (1-D) calculation, which improves the problem of large space memory and long running time for 3-D modeling while ensuring the accuracy and feasibility of the algorithm. On the one hand, by employing the transformation relationship between the transverse wave vector and the field in space, the expanded Maxwell's rotation equations are simplified, so that the equation system only retains the spatial transformation in the propagation direction. This processing allows for the calculation of the propagation characteristics of layered media without requiring more computational resources. On the other hand, to ensure the universality of the algorithm, a fully tensor anisotropic medium is selected for detecting the propagation data. At the same time, we design the layered structure and conduct the consistent 3-D modeling in the simulation software COMSOL. The results showed that our proposed efficient numerical algorithm greatly reduced the loss of computing resources while ensuring accuracy.

articleTitle: An Accurate and Efficient Hybrid Method for Calculating Electromagnetic Scattering from Honeycomb Sandwich Composite Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An accurate and efficient method for calculating electromagnetic scattering from honeycomb sandwich composite structure using hybrid finite element and multilayer surface integral equations (FE-MSIE) is proposed in this paper. In composite structures, the middle honeycomb core structure is modeled using finite element method, while the remaining uniform dielectric structures are modeled using surface integral equations method. To overcome the multiscale problem caused by the extremely thin honeycomb wall, the impedance boundary conditions (IBC) are introduced in the finite element method to simplify the honeycomb wall into a zero-thickness surface. The domain of MSIE adopts the discontinuous Galerkin method to improve the flexibility of modeling. In the iterative solution of the final matrix system, the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) is used to accelerate computation and reduce memory costs.

articleTitle: Design of a wideband wide-angle scanning 1- D phased array antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband wide-angle scanning one-dimensional phased array antenna at the Ku-band is designed, which use a continuous current sheet structure to form a tightly coupled dipole array (TCDA), to achieve a wide bandwidth. In addition, a structure consisting of dielectric substrate and toroidal metal sheet on top of the antenna is added as a wide-angle matching layer to improve the active VSWR during large-angle scanning. The simulation results show that the VSWR under 3.1 at different scanning angles within the frequency band of 11 GHz~24 GHz, realizing the scanning angle ranges from -60<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∘</sup>to 60° in the E-plane of the array, and the gain fluctuation less than 2 dB during beam scanning.

articleTitle: OTFS-Based Method for Interference Suppression in Integrated Communication and Sensing Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation is a promising modulation scheme for next-generation integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system. Nevertheless, there exists a problem of mutual interference between uplink communication signals and sensing echo signals, which leads to the degradation of both communication and sensing performance. For this reason, a successive interference cancellation (SIC) method based on the delay-Doppler (DD) domain to ensure the coexistence of communication and sensing is investigated in this paper. Firstly, the sensing echo signal is treated as interference to the communication signal, which is detected using a threshold-based channel estimation method and the Message Passing (MP) algorithm. The communication signal is then reconstructed and subtracted from the mixed signal. At last, the remaining signal is then subjected to parameter estimation with the Maximum Likelihood (ML) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that this method enables the ISAC system to function effectively in both communication and sensing. Additionally, compared to traditional interference suppression methods belong to TF domain, the performance of sensing parameter estimation is improved by approximately 2 dB.

articleTitle: Transfer Matrix Method Applied for Radio Waves Reflection on Sporadic E Layers
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The Sporadic E layers have effects on HF and VHF electromagnetic waves. In general, the electromagnetic waves are partially reflected by sporadic E layers. Thus the reflectivity is crucial for radio propagation. In this study, we apply the transfer matrix method to calculate the reflectivity of sporadic E layers. This method gives the reflectivity of sporadic E layers with any structures. Results show the reflectivity is largely determined by the structures and edge thickness of sporadic E layers.

articleTitle: Research on Time-Domain Deceptive Jamming Method for Passive Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The passive radar's excellent concealment and cost advantages make it attractive in various scenarios and specifically effective against drone swarms. This paper investigates time-domain deceptive jamming methods to counter passive radar systems. To achieve TDOA jamming effects, we propose using signal synthesis from drone swarms to mislead the positioning results of passive radar. Through the establishment of theoretical models and simulation experiments, it is demonstrated that the proposed method can effectively achieve TDOA jamming of passive radar by altering signal phase, pulse duty cycle, and retransmission delay. The proposed method can effectively disrupt the precise positioning of passive radar, thereby deceiving enemy systems. This technique can be employed in radar countermeasures and electronic warfare.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Wide-Angle Scanning Phased Array Antenna for High-Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a high-power, wide-angle scanning circularly polarized (CP) phased array antenna is proposed, based on multi-layer microstrip structure. In order to realize CP radiation, symmetric cross slots are designed to generate two sets of orthogonal polarizations, and a planar phase shifter is designed to form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^\circ$</tex> phase difference. The unit size of the proposed antenna is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$18^*18^*6.4 \text{mm}^{3}(0.54\lambda_{0^{*}}0.54\lambda_{0^{*}}0.19\lambda_{0})$</tex>. Simulation of the infinite array shows that it achieves 10-dB impedance bandwidth of 35.6% (7.4-10.6 GHz) and 3-dB axis ratio bandwidth of 27.8% (7.8-10.3 GHz). And it achieves wide-angle scanning up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 40^{\circ}$</tex> in both orthogonal planes. The power capacity is up to 10 kW.

articleTitle: Wireless Jamming Identification via Hypergraph Partitioning and Spectral Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Wireless jamming identification (WJI) is crucial for enhancing the robustness of radio systems in the complicated electromagnetic environments. In this paper, we present an WJI approach that leverages the feature extraction and the hypergraph learning to improve identification performance. Specifically, the spectrum features of the received signal are first extracted to represent the essential distinctions of the jamming signals. Then, we construct the hypergraph model utilizing the extracted feature vector to capture the multi-way relationships within the signals, followed by the hypergraph partitioning and the spectral clustering to determine the unknown jamming type. Numerical results show that the proposed hypergraph learning identification approach outperforms the baseline methods, achieving high identification accuracy with well-designed features and improving the robustness to the noise.

articleTitle: Effect of Surface Roughness of Dielectric Rod Antenna Used in Phased Array Radar on Radiation Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The effect of surface roughness of dielectric rod antennas on radiation performance is analyzed in this paper. The dielectric rod antenna consists of a cylindrical structure and a frustum structure, and both structures have a certain curvature. Therefore, compared to the ideal structural model, the dielectric rod antenna will produce surface errors. Surface roughness based on Gaussian distribution is used to describe this surface error. Furthermore, the solid model of a dielectric rod antenna based on surface roughness was established to analyze the impact of surface errors on radiation performance. In order to more deeply evaluate the impact of antenna surface roughness on radar performance, the dielectric rod antenna array model based on surface roughness was established. Research on the impact of surface roughness on radar antenna performance helps to better evaluate the actual performance of phased array radar, and thus provides a reference for the improvement of antenna processing technology.

articleTitle: Enhanced Hybrid OMP Channel Estimation Algorithm for SC-IFDMA System in ISC
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The presence of multi-path and Doppler effects of ionospheric scatter channel (ISC) leads to severe dual-selective fading, affecting channel estimation performance. To achieve reliable data transmission under ISC, a sparse channel estimate algorithm based on orthogonal matching tracking (OMP) for single carrier interleaved frequency division multiple access (SC-IFDMA) systems is proposed, called as enhanced hybrid OMP (EH-OMP). The EH-OMP integrates the linear minimum mean square error (LMMSE) of the OMP framework and incorporates a discrete Fourier transform (DFT) noise reduction algorithm. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the conventional OMP estimation algorithm. The transmission performance of the EH-OMP algorithm improves by about 1.8 dB when the bit error rate (BER) is 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>. The normalized mean square error (NMSE) of the EH-OMP algorithm is reduced by approximately 86% compared to the OMP at the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).

articleTitle: The Influence of Electricity Consumption on Power Line Radiation in the Topside Ionosphere- A Case Study Using CSES Satellite Observation
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The variation of the Power Line Radiation (PLR) occurrence rate over the Ukraine region is studied using the electric field data from the China Seismo- Electromagnetic Satellite (CSES) in low Earth orbit. The results show that the PLR occurrence rate is mainly controlled by solar radiation, but can still respond to the significant changes in electricity consumption. According to the research, the PLR occurrence rate in Ukraine's eastern region, where the military conflict between Russia and Ukraine occurred, the PLR occurrence rate decreased significantly in March 2022, while the PLR occurrence rate in Ukraine's western region, which was less affected by the military conflict, remained unchanged. The PLR occurrence rate in the Eastern conflict region reduced dramatically again in October 2022. We speculate that it may be due to the decrease in electricity supply again.

articleTitle: Analysis of Delay Variations of the Loran-C Across Different Atmospheric Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The Loran-C signal propagates through various atmospheric environments, and the speed of the electromagnetic signal changes as it moves through different media. This study aims to analyze the variations in the time delay of the Loran-C signal resulting from its passage through distinct atmospheric conditions. This study simulates different atmospheric environments by varying ground conductivity and corresponding atmospheric refractive indices. The propagation of the Loran-C signal through these varied conditions is modeled using a time-domain finite difference method within a two-dimensional coordinate system. The results indicate that, in the atmospheric environment, the ground conductivity has the greatest impact on the secondary delay of Loran-C signals, on the order of microseconds, whereas the effect of atmospheric refraction index is on the order of nanoseconds. The secondary delay of Loran-C signals decrease monotonically with increasing conductivity of the atmospheric environment. When Loran-C signals traverse different atmospheric conditions, propagation delay may experience abnormal changes of tens of nanoseconds. These variations arise from the inconsistency between the signal envelope and waveform propagation speeds.

articleTitle: Rapid Generation of Clutter Correlation Sequence Based on FFT
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Clutter simulation is an important part of radar signal processing system. In this paper, the generation method of clutter correlation sequence in clutter simulation is analyzed, and it is concluded that the generation of clutter correlation sequence generally has the problem of high time complexity, which cannot be applied to real-time echo processing in radar signal processing system. In this paper, by ignoring the clutter signal outside the range of radar instrument, a rapid generation of clutter correlation sequence based on FFT is proposed. The simulation experiments of signal processing under typical radar parameters and geographical environment show that the proposed method can greatly reduce the time complexity of clutter correlation sequence generation and meet the real-time processing requirements of radar echoes. Compared with the Range-Doppler distribution of clutter correlation sequence generated by LLT decomposition auto-correlation matrix, the clutter correlation sequence generated by this method has a good fit.

articleTitle: Flexible Multibeam Time-Modulated Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Multibeam time-modulated arrays (TMAs) can be used to simultaneously receive multiple copies of the same signal from different directions to achieve spatial diversity reception and reduce the impact of multipath effects. This conference proposes a method to realize flexible multibeam using coded TMAs. Using genetic algorithms for the design of coded modulating waveforms, the power spectrum energy can be focused at desired harmonics and the energy share of non-utilized harmonics is suppressed. Numerical simulations validate the flexible multibeam method and achieve the desired results.

articleTitle: The Design of a UWB Omnidirectional Dipole Antenna using Impedance Loading Applied in Borehole Logging Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Ultra-wideband (UWB) antennas play a crucial role in exploring underground resources, acting as an important tool in borehole logging radar. The UWB omnidirectional dipole antenna excited by impulses is highly suitable for detecting subsurface structures for its time-varying characteristics. However, low-frequency current reflections always appear near two ends of the arms, severely impacting the borehole radar's performance. We utilized the method of impedance loading to mitigate that effect, which can realize the antenna's UWB specifications to achieve underground oil exploration. The simulated results demonstrate the feasibility of adopting impedance loading to UWB dipole antennas applied in oil explorations, as an effective approach to remarkably improving their subterranean detection performances.

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband ‘Rocket’ Synthetic Array Feed
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A more accurate name “Synthetic Array Feed (SAF)” is proposed for phased array feed (PAF) by reviewing its basic concept and operating principle. A new SAF design is presented for radio astronomy applications. The array is composed of ‘Rocket” elements fed by coaxial probes. An infinite array and a 5×4 finite array model are established in CST software to simulate its transmission and radiation characteristics., respectively. The results show that the bandwidth can reach 3:1., and the active voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) is less than 1.25. The aperture efficiency of the QiTai radio Telescope (QTT) with this SAF is higher than 60% in the whole frequency band.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Multi-Layers Absorber Based on Equivalent Circuit Model
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this work, an ultra-wideband multi-layers absorber composed of five-layers indium tin oxide (ITO) resistance films is presented based on the equivalent circuit model (ECM). Square patch and square loop are selected as the lossy patterns due to their simplicity of construction and better electromagnetic performance. The absorption of electromagnetic waves can be enhanced by cascading ITO with different sizes of square pieces and square ring patterns. Further, the proposed cascade structure is analyzed by ECM. The reflection coefficients of the ultra-wideband absorber is lower than -10dB from 1.14 to 29.26 GHz (the fractional bandwidth (FBW) of absorption is 185%). Finally, the theoretical analysis with ECM and the simulation results are in good agreement.

articleTitle: Waveguide Travelling-Wave Slot Array Achieved by Conductive Metallization on Dielectric
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Waveguide slot array is a conventional method to achieve low side lobe large-aperture planar antenna, but its fine processing accuracy makes it expensive, which makes it difficult to meet the requirement of low-cost radar. This paper introduces a metal-coated dielectric waveguide slot array where its radiating slots are etched by laser. This antenna is economical, lightweight, and water-resistant, making it suitable for low-cost radar applications.

articleTitle: Plasma-Tunable Double-Bandpass Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
