abstract: Herein, a tunable frequency selective surface (FSS) based on the regulation capacity of plasma in the X-band is presented. The proposed FSS is composed of a bi-layer resonant element separated by trapped plasma in quartz. The design exhibits two bandpasses with center frequencies at 9.542GHz and 11.124GHz when the plasma is not excited. When the plasma is excited, the two bandpasses with center frequencies shift to a higher regime as the plasma frequency increases; however, the bandwidth decreases, and the optimal insertion loss of bandpass can reach -0.35dB.

articleTitle: Weather Radar Echo Extrapolation Based on Convolutional LSTM Prediction Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: We conducted research on weather radar echo extrapolation prediction based on convolutional LSTM neural network. It can be seen that in the input-target (X-T) time-series samples, the sample closest to the predicted result gradually changes backwards (in time) as the epoch increases. When the closest sample is the target sample, it indicates that the model has good predictive ability. Therefore, a loss function based solely on the similarity between the predicted result and the target sample is not sufficient to determine the training level of the prediction model. It is recommended to simultaneously examine the similarity between the predicted result with X- T time-series samples to determine the training level and termination condition of the prediction model. In addition, by comparing with the small ball testing prediction model, we speculate that due to the smaller detection range and faster image change of X-band weather radar, the training of echo extrapolation prediction neural network is faster than that of S-band weather radar.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of Distance Error Based on Ionospheric Parameter Correction of Reference Source
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: By using the shortwave ray tracing technique and the quasi-parabolic ionospheric electron concentration model, this paper simulates and analyzes different ionospheric parameters (different critical frequencies, different bottom heights and different half-thickness) within one hop. Based on the ionospheric parameters of the reference source, the ionospheric propagation parameters of different distances are modified, and the distribution characteristics of ground distance errors with group distances are obtained.

articleTitle: Applications of RF Thin Film Integrated Passive Device in Heterogeneous System Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces thin-film integrated passive device (IPD) technologies with a focus on high resistivity silicon (HRS) IPD and Gaas IPD. Based on thin-film IPD technologies, various RF passive devices including filters and other passive components are discussed and RF module for the heterogeneous system integration is demonstrated.

articleTitle: A Design of Broadband Dual-Polarization Antenna Based on Fractal Geometry
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With the increassing widely application of wireless devices, the increasing number of terminals, and product upgrading, higher requirements have been concentrated on the capatity of channel and signal transmission rate of wireless communication systems Further, antenna design work attaches more requirements, which includes low profile, light weight, low cost, simp structure, and planarization. Thus, antennas with dual polarization simultaneous reception, broadband, high isolation, and other characteristics are more favored in many modern mobile and wireless broadband communication systems. In this paper, Minkowski geometry fractal structure and nested fractal geometry is selected to design a broadband antenna with slot coupling feeding, where bandwidth is improved compared with the original square ring antenna. It imposes a new trend for design and integration of large-scale highly integration antennas.

articleTitle: Design of Flat Luneburg Lens for Ka-Band Compact Antenna Test Range
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A flat Luneburg lens (FLL) antenna is designed with 6 layers in this paper. It is used to generate a quiet zone (QZ) of compact antenna test range (CATR) in the Ka-band. The flat Luneburg lens is designed by coordinate transformation mapping and phase compensation principle. The spherical wave could be converted to plane wave by the FLL. Therefore, The QZ with uniform phase and amplitude is obtained in the near-field. The results show that the diameter of the QZ is 12mm and the depth is 150mm. In addition, the amplitude error is 1 dB and the phase error is 10°.

articleTitle: Wideband Fabry Perot Antenna with the PRS Array Optimization Using the Electric Field Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A wideband Fabry-Perot (FP) antenna with the partially reflection surface (PRS) array size optimization using the electric field analysis is proposed in this paper. The PRS layer is composed of complementary square apertures and patches printed on either side of a thin dielectric sheet. Different from the previous works, this paper optimizes the size of the PRS array while ensuring the positive gradient reflection phase range of the PRS unit. By comparing the effects of different size PRS on antenna electric field distribution, a 6 × 6 PRS array is selected as the final version. The designed antenna operates at 8.8-11.6 GHz frequency band, and the 3 dB gain bandwidth is 29.1% (8.5-11.4GHz).

articleTitle: Ray-Tracing-Assisted Calibration Based on Divide-and-Conquer Algorithm in Macrocellular Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In addressing the significant influence of material dielectric parameters on outdoor three-dimensional ray tracing predictions, an algorithm based on divide-and-conquer strategy for calibrating the dielectric properties of materials is proposed. The algorithm segments the solution space for dielectric parameters into smaller sub-spaces, resolving each incrementally to arrive at the global optimal solution. It employs a prudent convergence strategy for the solution space, discarding those sub-spaces that have a low probability of containing the optimum. The results indicate that this algorithm not only maintains high accuracy but also facilitates rapid calibration of dielectric parameters.

articleTitle: Road Network Extraction from SAR Images Based on GaoFen-3 Satellite Image
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Road is an important part of the transportation network, and with the acceleration of urban and rural construction, how to quickly identify and extract the roads and update the road network becomes a crucial issue. Due to the coherent imaging mechanism, the SAR images of GaoFen-3 are inevitably speckled, which seriously affects the interpretation of the images. Especially the detection of dark and weak roads under strong speckle interference is difficult. In the actual production, most of the enterprises still extract the road network from SAR images by traditional manual outlining, which has a large workload and high labor cost. Therefore, we propose a method to extract roads from GaoFen-3 SAR images using deep learning, and the results of testing on data from two different regions show that the method has good extraction accuracy and has the potential to be applied to large-area extraction of roads from GaoFen-3 images.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Antenna with Ultrawideband RCS Reduction Based on Polarization Conversion Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a circularly polarized antenna with ultrawideband out-of-band radar cross section (RCS) reduction based on polarization conversion metasurface (PCM) is created. A polarization conversion unit consists of 3 pairs of symmetrical L-shaped strips. The substrate and air gap are designed to expand the working band of the PCM to achieve ultrawideband RCS reduction. Polarization conversion bandwidth of the designed PCM unit is 6.9-25.2 GHz (114%) with a polarization conversion ratio exceeding 90%. The circularly polarized antenna loaded with PCMs has a radiated operating frequency of 6 GHz and an ultrawideband RCS reduction from 8.8 to 27 GHz (101.7%).

articleTitle: A Novel Double-Feed Microstrip Balun for Planar Antennas to Enhance Radiating Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To enhance the feed power of a planar antenna, a novel symmetric three-layer double-feed balun is proposed, which can be excited by positive and negative pulses. The structure boasts compact size, good generality and easy integration with planar antennas. The main method is to feed two transient pulses of opposite polarity into the two arms of antenna through the coupling conduction of common grounding and the microstrip line, so as to increase the electric field distribution on the surface of the antenna and increase the radiation field intensity. For validating the analysis, a double-feed microstrip balun whose feeding impedance is 50 Ω, developed with the basic model of antipodal Vivaldi antenna, is designed and simulated. It indicates that the radiating field of the antenna is increased by 1.40 times under the excitation of positive and negative pulses of the same magnitude with pulse width of about 1ns.

articleTitle: A New Dataset and Benchmark for Cross-Domain Automatic Modulation Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Automatic Modulation Classification (AMC) is a promising technique for automatically analyzing the modulation type of the received signals, and it plays an important role in both military and civilian fields. Recently, Deep Learning (DL) has been introduced into AMC for better performance. However, these previously proposed methods have not been tested for generalization and robustness, due to the lack of crossdomain datasets, such as those varying in environment and time. To tackle this challenge, we developed a new dataset for AMC, dubbed “CD2024”. This dataset comprises modulation signal samples from four distinct scenarios and encompasses 25 modulation types, totaling 50,000 samples. Utilizing this dataset, we evaluate the robustness of existing DL-based AMC methods. The experimental results indicate that these methods still exhibit significant potential for enhancement when dealing with crossdomain data.

articleTitle: A Compact Tri-Band Tri-Polarization Antenna for Autonomous Vehicles and Drones
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a tri-band antenna that supports three types of polarization for autonomous vehi-cles and drones. The proposed antenna employs a stacked structure. A left-hand circularly polarized (LHCP) radiating patch, fed directly by a coaxial probe, is printed on the first substrate. The second substrate hosts both a right-hand circularly polarized (RHCP) radiating patch and a linearly polarized (LP) radiating patch. The RHCP and LHCP patches operate in the BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) B3 band and L band, respectively, while the LP patch works in the 2.7-3.05 GHz range. The third and fourth substrates incorporate feed networks for the LP and RHCP patches. Moreover, the antenna's overall size is only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.14 \times 0.14\lambda_{0}^{2}$</tex>, making it quite attractive for autonomous vehicles and drones.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized MIMO Antenna Design for Ku/K Wave Band
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A miniaturized multiple-input multiple-output an-tenna design for Ku/K wave band is proposed in this paper. By etching arch groove inside the radiation patch and loading rectangular radiation patches, the working bandwidth of the antenna is effectively expanded. High isolation of the antenna is achieved by etching toroidal grooves on the ground plate. The antenna holds a small size of only 32mm×56mm × 1.6mm, having an operating bandwidth of 11~V28GHz. The designed antenna is simulated in the High Frequency Structure Simulator(HFSS) platform. The results demonstrated that within the operating band of the antenna, the Reflection Coefficient(S11)<-10dB, the Transmission Coefficient (S21)<-25dB, and the Envelope Correlation Coefficient(ECC) is less than 0.0005. The antenna performs well and can be widely used in wireless communication systems and other related fields.

articleTitle: Study on the Inversion Method of Rendezvous Parameters Using Near-Field Echo Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a rendezvous parameter inversion method based on one-dimensional convolutional neural network is proposed by using near-field rendezvous echo data. The simulated near-field rendezvous echo data of typical targets are preprocessed and data enhanced to form a training set. A one-dimensional convolutional neural network for inversion of rendezvous parameters is designed and trained. The influence of different network structures on the accuracy of inversion parameters is analyzed. The results show that the inversion method based on near-field echo characteristics has good robustness and accuracy.

articleTitle: Error Analysis of Gain Measurement for Large Aperture Antennas Using APM
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper analyzes the error for large aperture HPM antenna gain measurement using the method of absolute power method (APM). Firstly, the basic theory of APM is introduced, followed by an analysis of the error ranges of various error sources involved in the measurement methods. Then, the measurement errors of APM are summarized: APM can control the gain error range within 0.32dB by using the highest precision instrument, Finally, suggestions were proposed to minimize errors based on the conclusion of error analysis.

articleTitle: Implementation of Low-Cost Large-Spacing Phased Array Key Methodology for Grating Lobe Suppression (Invite)
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: High costs, energy consumption, and complexity are the most significant reasons hindering the application of phased arrays in civilian sectors in recent years. A feasible solution is to reduce the number of elements within a fixed aperture, evolving a half-wavelength array into a large-spacing array. However, this simultaneously introduces grating lobes at each scanning angles. To this end, Computational Electromagnetic Laboratory (CEMLAB) at University of Electronic Science and Technology of China (UESTC) has carried out related research since 2013. Starting from the generalized pattern multiplication theorem, they analyzed the mechanism of lobes formation in relation to the position vectors of the array element. Subsequently, they developed theoretical methods for grating lobe suppression in low-cost large-spacing scanning arrays using techniques such as null steering, special regular arrangements, and aperiodic configurations. Finally, the development trend of grating lobe suppression in large-spacing array is predicted in the conclusion.

articleTitle: Tunable Chirality and Helicity of Bessel Twisted Beams Near the Dirac Points in Topological Metacrystal
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this work, we undertake an approach to describe the tunable optical chirality and helicity of twisted beam near the Dirac point in topological meta-crystals. An improved method based on the full vector wave analysis is introduced to investigate the chirality and helicity of Bessel twisted beams near the Dirac point in the interface of topological meta-crystals. It is showed that the giant non-specular effects of chirality and helicity are discovered when a Bessel twisted Beam reflects in the vicinity of a Dirac point, which is sensitive to the incident frequency, angle, and electromagnetic properties of the topological meta-crystal. We can attribute the giant non-specular effect of chirality and helicity to the degeneracy between critical angle and Brewster angle caused by the Dirac point. The results will be of significant interest of study the measurement of Dirac point, and inspire a perspective for manipulating twisted beams with Dirac point.

articleTitle: A Dual-Wavelength Bifocal Microwave Metalens Based on Bi-Layer Plasmonic Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Metasurfaces (or metalenses) provide an excellent platform to manipulate incident waves across wide spectrums. Compared to traditional microwave lenses based on phase accumulation along trajectory such as Luneburg lens, meta-lenses can greatly reduce the device thickness simultaneously with more degrees of freedom. In this paper, a dual-wavelength microwave metalens with a single-layer plasmonic metasurface with two different phase gradient profile via spatial multiplexing is designed and simulated numerically. It is shown that the designed flat metalens can produce a dual-focus spot with two different focal length at two distinct wavelength of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{1}=10.5\text{GHz}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{2}=14.5\text{GHz}$</tex>, respectively. Besides, the focusing performances at these two wavelengths are also analyzed and the spot size is diffraction-limited with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.48\lambda_{1}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.87\lambda_{2}$</tex> in the far field, respectively. Moreover, the focusing efficiency is about 45% and 42% for low frequency and high frequency operation, respectively. The proposed scheme and studies provide a method to develop dual-band and multi-functional microwave metalens and meta-devices by integrating different types of meta-atom in a single-layer metasurface.

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Reconfigurable Patch Antenna Loaded with a Dielectric Lens for mm-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a millimeter-wave(mm-Wave) radiation pattern reconfigurable patch antenna loaded with a dielectric lens is proposed. The antenna consists of a driven patch, two groups of parasitic patch elements, two groups of PIN diodes and an extended conical dielectric lens. The H-plane maximum radiation direction can be switched between +30° and -30° by controlling the states of PIN diodes. In order to improve the gain and radiation performance of the antenna, an extended conical lens is added onto the antenna. It increases the antenna gain by 5–6 dB, and makes the radiation pattern more stable. It is suitable for satellite communication, mobile communication and other wireless systems.

articleTitle: Ground Target Recognition Method for Laser Proximity Fuze Echo Based on KNN Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aiming at the urgent demand for accurate recognition of ground target by the new-generation of laser proximity fuze, an exploration study on ground target recognition using KNN algorithm based on the echo of the mission-target encounter of laser fuze is conducted. Firstly, the echo equation of mission-target encounter is established by the radar equation. Secondly, the echo data is processed by normalization, and the data is divided into the training dataset and the test dataset. Then, the data are subjected to feature extraction, such as the number of strong scattering points, equivalent target size. Finally, the obtained feature subset is used for target recognition training and testing based on KNN algorithm, linear support vector machine algorithm and Gaussian naive bayes algorithm. The experimental results indicate that the recognition method based on the KNN neighbor algorithm has high accuracy and can effectively achieve classification and recognition of different targets. It has a good application value in the recognition of lase ground fuze, and lays a solid foundation for the subsequent fine recognition and efficient destruction of laser fuze.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Driven Design of Freeform Metasurfaces for Holographic Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Deep learning (DL), with its strong nonlinear fitting capabilities, has found extensive application in the inverse design of metasurfaces (MSs). This paper presents a deep learning-driven approach to design MSs for holographic imaging. We first pre-analyzed the metallic structures within the meta-atoms in our training dataset to achieve a full <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\pi$</tex> phase range. A forward network is then designed to predict the electromagnetic (EM) responses given a meta-atom pattern. Furthermore, an inverse network capable of determining the necessary structure for a desired EM response is constructed. To mitigate the issue of non-uniqueness, we cascade these two networks, forming a tandem network to achieve holographic imaging. The simulation results demonstrate that under plane wave illumination at 10 GHz and 15 GHz, the MS array can project high-resolution holograms of the letters “T” and “F”, respectively.

articleTitle: Radiation characterization of a new type of dipole antenna lying on an Unmanned Surface Vessel
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With the rapid development of unmanned technology, the application prospect of unmanned surface vessel (USV) in the sea is increasingly broad. Considering the USV antenna's radiation characteristics is affected by ocean waves, the USV, antenna and ocean waves are jointly modeled and simulated by the electromagnetic simulation software HFSS. The impedance and radiation pattern of the USV antenna located at different positions of the waves, immersed in seawater at different depths and tilted at different angles are obtained, which provides theoretical basis for the design of the USV antenna.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Super-Resolution for Power Delay Profiles Towards Digital Twinning of Wireless Channels in 6G and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The digital twinning (DT) of wireless channels is crucial in the sixth-generation mobile communication system (6G) and beyond. Ray-tracing (RT) is a critical technology in DT of wireless channels with the limitation of significant computational resources. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a deep learning (DL) based super-resolution (SR) model for power delay profiles (PDP). This model can restore the PDP from low-resolution to high-resolution. The RT generates the datasets in outdoor and indoor scenarios at multi-frequency bands for training and test. Compared to the RT, the efficiency of this method is enhanced, and the accuracy is improved compared to the traditional linear interpolation method. In summary, the proposed method can serve as a reference for the DT of wireless channels.

articleTitle: SAR Imaging for a Missile Above Two-Layered Rough Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In the past, there have been many studies on electromagnetic scattering calculation of targets. But there are fewer studies on the scattering calculation of rough surfaces, especially for the layered rough surfaces. When the target is above the layered rough surface, it is necessary to solve the composite scattering of the rough surface and the target. In this paper, we focus on a missile above two-layered rough surfaces (MTRS) scene. And based on the ray tracing, we analyze the complex scattering between a target and two-layered rough surfaces. Based on the geometric optics (GO), the incident fields of all the surfaces are obtained, and then apply the time domain physical optics (PO) to calculate the scattered fields. In the end, considering the effect of the roughness of the rough surface on the scattered field, we give the SAR images for different roughness to explore the effect of roughness on the scattered field.

Author Keywords: a missile above two-layered rough surface (MTRS)

articleTitle: An Absorber Using Indium Tin Oxide for High-Power Microwave Application
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this work, an absorber with indium tin oxide (ITO) for high-power microwave (HPM) application is proposed, which combines the advantages of ultra-wideband absorption, high angular stability and high power handling capability. The proposed design is constructed by two different media plates with ITO conductive films, which demonstrates a wide operating frequency range from 2.876GHz to 20.633GHz. The absorbing band with fractional bandwidth of 151.066% for absorptivity greater than 90%. Besides, the proposed absorber has high angular stability. When the absorption greater than 90%,in transverse magnetic (TM) mode, the incidence angle can be achieved 70°, in transverse electrical (TE) mode, the incidence angle can be achieved 50°. To study the power handling capability of the proposed ITO absorber by quantifiable the maximum field enhancement factor (MFEF), which crest value can be achieved 13.0587. The excellent characteristics with ultra-wideband and steady performance under high-power incident make the proposed absorber has various application prospects in HPM protection and stealth.

articleTitle: Analysis of Jammer Effectiveness in Typical Electromagnetic Combat Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This article focuses on the jamming effectiveness of jammers on radar systems in the electromagnetic combat environment. The article adopts linear frequency modulation (LFM) signal as the simulated jamming source in order to simulate the transmission of jamming signals under real operating conditions. Applying the coordinate transformation technology, the relative positions of the jammer and the radar receiver were located accurately and efficiently. Combined with the dynamic characteristics of the antenna to update the azimuth in real time, the instantaneous simulation of the signal transmission is achieved. With the simulation results as a support, this article optimises the antenna servo control system of the jamming system and automatically adjusts the antenna pointing to achieve the best jamming performance. The research results provide theoretical basis and practical guidance for the jamming strategy in electromagnetic combat, which helps to improve the real combat effectiveness of the jamming system.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Coupling Analysis Method for Aircraft Based on Electromagnetic Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: High intensity radiated field (HIRF) significantly impact aircraft flight safety, and currently a lack of necessary technical means for HIRF protection design in the early development stages of aircraft. Taking the AG300 aircraft as the subject, this paper proposes a method for generating and simplifying the electromagnetic topology coupling path set for aviation systems. Based on electromagnetic topology theory, an electromagnetic coupling path set for external electromagnetic interference entering the aircraft was constructed. The methods for obtaining coupling coefficients under different coupling paths, including slots, cable bundles, and dielectric wave propagation, were studied. The coupling path set was simplified through a three-tier screening method and validated for application, providing technical support for the electromagnetic vulnerability analysis and forward design of aircraft.

articleTitle: X-band and 2-18GHz Frequency Overlap Heterogeneous Array
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel frequency overlap heterogeneous phased array (HPA) is put forward. The array consists of two types of all-metal Vivaldi elements with distinct lattice sizes, namely 13.5mm×13.5mm and 9mm×9mm. These elements operate in the X-band and the frequency range of 2-18GHz, resulting in a 3:2 aperture ratio. Unlike traditional phased arrays that are designed and function independently, the HPA can operate in both independent and collaborative modes for various states. In contrast to the independent mode, when the HPA operates in the collaborative mode, the array gain is enhanced, thereby facilitating the improvement of system performance and the reduction of hardware costs.

articleTitle: A Broadband Reflectarray Antenna on Glass Substrate for V-Band Satellite Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel broadband reflectarray antenna on glass substrate for V-band satellite application by utilizing nested square rings on two glass layers is developed in this paper. To enlarge the bandwidth and the transparency of the antenna, the nested metal square rings serve not only as radiation patch but also as metal bonding medium for the two layers of glass. A passive reflectarray antenna with above method is designed, fabricated and measured. Experimental results demonstrate the 3dB gain loss bandwidth is about 19% and the aperture efficiency is about 46% within the frequency band from 47.5 to 57.5GHz. Moreover, another passive array prototype with the beam aiming to 30 ° is also proved good performance by measured results Therefore, the presented reflectarray antenna is an attractive candidate for V-band satellite applications.

articleTitle: Design of ELF/ULF Induction Magnetometer Based on Particle Swarm Otimization
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Nowadays, the existing ELF/ULF antennas generally have the problems of large size, low efficiency and poor signal-to-noise ratio, so that the noise level of the induction magnetometers as the receiving end needs to be improved urgently. This paper combines the design process of the existing induction magnetometers, analyzes the influence of each design parameter on the noise level, and proposes an optimized design scheme based on particle swarm optimization algorithm. Simulation results show that the optimal magnetic core has a length of 1.09m, a diameter of 0.024m, an optimal number of turns of 4200, and a noise level of 0.05pT/ Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup> at 1Hz and 8fT/ Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup> at 10Hz when the magnetometers weighs less than 7.5kg and the length less than 1.25m, and the noise level can satisfy the demand of ground-transparent communication.

articleTitle: Significant Bandwidth Enhancement of LowReflection Checkerboard Metasurfaces Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A method of machine learning is proposed for enhancing the low-reflection bandwidth of checkerboard metasurfaces. Instead of iterative optimization to a satisfying performance, a conditional deep neural network (cDNN) is trained to establish a mapping relation between reflection phase and the unit-cell structures first, with which new types of unit cells are massively generated to explore the largest bandwidth limit. As a result, the checkerboard metasurface designed by the trained cDNN achieves a 10-dB bandwidth of scattering reduction 22% higher than the best in the training dataset, from 62% to 84%. The proposed method demonstrates the ability of machine learning for electromagnetic discovery and performance breakthrough.

articleTitle: Direct Printing of Curved Conformal Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Conformal antenna has the characteristics of miniaturization, low profile and large aperture, which is one of the key antenna development trends in the future. How to realize the conformal printing of antennas has been a tricky problem. We propose a high-precision microdroplet jet printing method of conformal antenna, which realizes direct conformal antenna direct printing on curved surfaces. By theoretically deriving the directional map function of an arbitrary directed array, a conical conformal antenna model is established, and the directional map function of the conformal antenna array is obtained. The test results show that the strategy can accurately print a conformal antenna on a curved surface, and the antenna's operating frequency is basically the same as that of the design, with a small return loss, which can satisfy the performance and usage requirements, and it can provide a technical basis for the subsequent design and processing of conformal antennas.

articleTitle: Research on Real Time Single-Station GNSS PWV Monitoring Method and Experimental Verification at Sea
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Ground-based GNSS PWV has been operationalized utilizing abundant historical radiosonde (RS) observations. However, in ocean areas, especially in the open sea, there is a lacking of RS observations which results rare research on GNSS PWV monitoring method at sea. Moreover, Network solution of GNSS PWV is difficult to achieve at sea due to extremely limited communication bandwidth on offshore observation platforms, which makes single-station GNSS PWV monitoring more suitable for this type of application scenario. In this paper, a real time single-station GNSS PWV monitoring method is proposed based on real-time precise point positioning (RT-PPP) exploiting BD3 PPP-B2b precise point positioning service signal and weighted average temperature <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{T}_{\mathbf{m}})$</tex> model established by regression using ERA5 reanalysis data. To evaluate the accuracy of this method, an experimental system has been implemented at coastal station in Qingdao. The results show that compared with RS PWV monitoring data from a nearby radiosonde station, the RMSE of the proposed method is 1.51mm, which proves that this method is applicable for real-time tropospheric PWV monitoring at sea.

articleTitle: Research on the Significant Wave Height Calculation Method and Its Influence on Electromagnetic Wave Propagation
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Ocean wave is an important and complex marine hy-drographic element, in which, the significant wave height of ocean wave has a major impact on studying electromagnetic waves at sea. Based on the millimeter-wave radar wave monitoring system, this paper calculates the root-mean-square height deviation using the significant wave height obtained by the cross-zero method, and compares it with that calculated by the traditional empirical model using the wind speed. The effective reflection coefficient and electromagnetic wave propagation loss are further analyzed experimentally in conjunction with the parabolic equation (PE). The results show that there is a strong correlation between the root-mean-square height deviation and the effective reflection coefficient obtained by the two calculation methods, however, there are also large deviations in the values, and with the maximum deviation of the electromagnetic wave propagation loss reaching 11.51 dB For the actual marine environment, the significant wave height calculation method based on millimeter wave radar proposed in this paper is adopted, which has an important impact on improving the calculation accuracy of electromaanetic wave propagation loss.

articleTitle: A Wearable All-Fabric Wilkinson Power Divider for Flexible Radio Frequency Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The rapid development of wearable electronic technology has increased the demand for flexible RF devices. In this paper, we propose a prototype of a two-way equal-split Wilkinson power divider operating in the ISM 2.45 GHz band, specifically designed for flexible wearable RF applications. We innovatively prepared the device prototype based on the fabric circuit board quasi-surface mount technology (FCB-SMT). Both the substrate and the metallic structure are realized using all-fabric material to ensure the full flexibility and lightweight advantages of the entire component. Key performance indicators of the power divider, such as return loss, insertion loss, and isolation, are carefully evaluated under both flat and bent conditions. The results show that the proposed all-fabric Wilkinson power divider performs comparably to traditional power dividers made from rigid materials, offering a viable alternative for advanced wearable RF technology.

articleTitle: Microwave/Millimeter-Wave Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Antenna with Beam Scanning in Millimeter-Wave Band
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A dual-band dual-polarized shared-aperture antenna with beam scanning capability operating in sub-6G and millimeter-wave bands is proposed. The proposed antenna is a 4×3 cascaded triangular cavity array in the millimeter-wave band. The entire millimeter-wave array may resonate in the microwave band. Therefore, the same radiator can be used as a sub-6G antenna with a broadside radiation pattern as well as a millimeter-wave array. The radiator has a novel structure and a simple and compact design. Experimental results show that the gains in the sub-6 GHz and millimeter-wave bands are 5.2 dBi and 13.1 dBi at 3.25 GHz and 27 GHz, respectively. the isolation of the different ports is higher than 14 dB, and the millimeter-wave arrays provide beam-scanning performances of −27°-28° and −25°-23° at 0° and 90° polarization, respectively.

articleTitle: Secure Transmission in Segmented RIS-Assisted NOMA Networks with Imperfect SIC
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In recent years, the use of reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) to enhance physical layer secure transmissions has been widely researched. To further enhance the secrecy rate and effectively reduce system complexity, this paper innovatively proposes a secure non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) communication scheme based on the assistance of a segmented RIS. In order to maximize the minimum secrecy rate, an optimization problem is established to joint optimize base station (BS) beamforming, RIS phase shifts and RIS segmentation matrix. An alternating optimization algorithm is proposed to solve the non-convex problem by combing successive convex approximation (SCA), semi-definite programming (SDP) and greedy algorithm. The simulation results show the superiority of the proposed scheme in enhancing the secrecy rate compared with traditional OMA, non-RIS-assisted, and fixed-segmentation RIS-assisted schemes.

articleTitle: Design and Manipulation of Electromagnetic Metasurface Based on Bidirectional Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In the current research field, metasurface technology has attracted much attention because of its excellent electromagnetic wave manipulation ability, and is widely used in the field of micro and nano photonics. In the lower frequency band, the megahertz band, metasurface technology also shows great potential for development, especially in the field of medical imaging, which is becoming increasingly important. However, the design process of metasurfaces is intricate and computationally costly. To tackle this challenge, this paper introduces a deep learning-based approach for the electromagnetic control and design of metasurfaces in the megahertz frequency band. By developing a Deep Neural Network (DNN), we are able to rapidly predict the electromagnetic response of metasurfaces, substantially reducing the time and memory consumption required for simulations. Moreover, the application of deep learning technology in metasurface design extends beyond forward prediction to inverse design, allowing for the prediction of metasurface structures that meet specific electromagnetic response requirements from the design objectives. This method overcomes the limitations of traditional design methods, offering new possibilities for the advancement of metasurface technology.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Reflectarray Antenna Based GeTe Phase-Change Material in the Ka-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces a 1-bit broadband digital metasurface unit based on the phase-change material(PCM) GeTe in the Ka-band. The metasurface unit achieves a stable phase shift of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$180^{\circ}+25^{\circ}$</tex> within the frequency range of 27.87GHz to 41.99GHz, with a bandwidth of 14.12GHz and a relative bandwidth of 40.42%, exhibiting stable broadband characteristics and reflection losses below 0.45dB. A 15×15 array based on this metasurface unit is designed, and simulations demonstrate that the antenna can achieve a wide-angle scanning of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 50^{\circ}$</tex> with excellent beam scanning performance, reaching a peak gain of 17.57dBi.

articleTitle: The Effect of Solar Flares on the VLF Waves in the Topside Ionosphere Radiated from Ground Transmistters
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Enhanced X-rays due to solar flare bursts can lead to a significant increase in electron density in the lower ionosphere, which can change the height of reflection at the base of the ionosphere. A large number of previous studies have focused on the effects of solar flares on Very Low Frequency (VLF) waves propagating in the ground-ionosphere waveguide. In this study, the impact of solar flares on VLF waves propagating through the ionosphere is investigated using the China Seismo-Electromagnetic Satellite (CSES) satellite, and the results show that solar flares can cause energy attenuation of the VLF waves propagating upward from the ground to the topside ionosphere.

articleTitle: Wideband Characterization of Single Parabolic Cylindrical Compact Range for Linear Array Feeds
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Compact antenna ranges test (CATR) are commonly used for antenna testing and radar cross section measurements. The single parabolic cylindrical reflector (SPCR) compact range with a linear array feed can enhance aperture efficiency while maintaining high-quality quiet zone performance, thereby reducing the cost of measuring large equipment. This paper investigates the wideband characteristics of SPCR compact range. Firstly, the system design of the SPCR compact range with a linear array feed is introduced. Next, the wideband optimization function and optimization methods are discussed. Full-wave simulations and system experiments in the sub-6G operating frequency band are then conducted. The designed compact range achieves a high-quality quiet zone with an aperture efficiency of 60-70%, demonstrating the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Efficient High Order Domain Decomposition FE-BI-MLFMA for Electromagnetic Scattering by Inhomogeneous Objects
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An efficient high order domain decomposition method (DDM) based hybrid finite element-boundary integral-multilevel fast multipole algorithm (FE-BI-MLFMA) is presented in this paper. The hierarchical high order vector finite element (HVFE) is employed to reduce the numerical dispersion error in the FEM. True second-order Robin transmission conditions are employed in the FE subdomain interfaces, while first-order Robin transmission conditions are employed in the interfaces between the FE region and the BI region. Numerical results are provided to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed high order DDM-FE-BI-MLFMA for scattering by a frequency selective radome.

Author Keywords: hierarchical high order vector finite element

articleTitle: The Performance of GeTe Phase-Change Switches Based on SiC and Si Substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The influence of heat dissipation on the performance of GeTe phase change switches cannot be ignored. During the phase transition process, the temperature of GeTe films rises significantly, especially at high frequency or long time operation, and this temperature rise will lead to the degradation of phase-change switch performance or even failure. Therefore, optimizing the heat dissipation structure and materials is crucial to improve the performance of phase-change switches. In this paper, by selecting two different substrate materials, SiC substrate and Si substrate, we analyze the effect of different thermal conductivity substrates on the device performance from the thin film material characterization analysis to the device performance test, and find that SiC, as a high thermal conductivity substrate, has better heat dissipation performance, and the higher the thermal conductivity of the substrate material, the lower the pulse voltage required for the phase-change switch to realize turn-on and turn-off under the same pulse time, and the smaller its power consumption. It has some reference significance for future device fabrication and energy consumption reduction.

articleTitle: Endfire Circularly Polarized Antenna for Satellite Communication in Metal-Rimmed Mobile Phones
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This invited paper focuses on metal-rimmed mobile phone antenna with an endfire circularly polarized (CP) beam for satellite communication, which is a hot topic of research in mobile terminal antennas. This paper consists of 3 parts: The first part discusses some key technical challenges and recent developments in endfire CP mobile phone antennas; the second part presents a novel design of endfire CP antenna suitable for metal-rimmed mobile phones. By integrating two slot antennas operating in and modes, respectively, into the metal rim, two orthogonal E-field components along the two edges of the front surface are achieved. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed antenna is able to produce a CP beam with a peak gain of 1.07 dBic at 2.1GHz within 30° along the endfire direction. To the best knowledge of the authors, this is the first report of a simple endfire CP antenna design for metal-rimmed mobile phones without utilizing any metal cavity or shorted parallel patches, which are complicated and bulky. This design is promising for applications in next-generation mobile terminals supporting satellite communication. The final part presents a conclusion and discusses future development trends of satellite communication mobile phone antennas.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Circular Polarization Van Atta Array Based on Non-Uniform Arrangement
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A reconfigurable circularly polarized Van Atta array with non-uniform arrangement is proposed. The circular polarization reconfigurability of the antenna is achieved using PIN diodes embedded in the element. Each element is an aperture-coupled microstrip antenna with an impedance bandwidth of 2.9% (2.35-2.42 GHz) and a 3dB axial ratio bandwidth of 0.8% (2.39-2.41 GHz). For extending the retrodirective angle, the proposed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times 8$</tex> Van Atta array is designed as a non-uniform array with a total size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.92\times 0.44 \times 0.02 \ \lambda_{0}^{3}$</tex>. The -3dB beamwidth of the monostatic radar cross section (RCS) at 2.40 GHz is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 54^{\circ}$</tex> for both the right-hand circular polarization and left-hand circular polarization incident waves. Compared with the uniform Van Atta array, the proposed non-uniform array has a wider monostatic RCS beamwidth at 2.40 GHz.

articleTitle: Multi-Model Ensemble Diagnostic Method for Evaporation Duct Considering Physical Property
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Evaporation duct is an phenomenon in the marine atmosphere that can cause anomalous transmission of electromagnetic (EM) waves. Therefore, accurately obtaining the evaporation duct height (EDH) is of great significance to the propagation of EM waves. Currently, evaporation duct diagnostic methods based on machine learning only consider mathematical relationships of data, without considering the physical properties of ocean-atmosphere interaction. To overcome the above problems, a multi-model ensemble diagnostic method for evaporation duct considering physical properties with convolutional neural network (CNNM) is proposed in the paper. Using meteorological and hydrological parameters and optimal model diagnostic values as inputs and EDH reference values as outputs constructing a deep learning model-CNNM. Experiments and analyses of the diagnostic method were conducted using the observational data from 19 August 2023 to 16 September 2023 on the research vessel “Tan Kah Kee”. The results show that the CNNM is more suitable for EDH diagnosis and has a higher accuracy than other models. Under stable atmospheric condition, the average errors of diagnostic values of CNNM model from the reference values is 1.09 m. Under unstable atmospheric condition, the average errors of diagnostic values of CNNM model from the reference values is 1.06 m.

articleTitle: A Novel Application of RLS Algorithm Based on Fractional Fourier Domain in the Presence of Non-cooperative Radiation Source
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: High frequency hybrid sky-surface wave radar(H SSWR) is widely used due to its wide propagation distance and rich state information of propagation space which covers not only the ocean surface but also the ionosphere. However, for the receiving subsystem, the complex electromagnetic space in which it operates can cause significant interference to the echo signal, especially for non-cooperative radiation sources with similar operating frequency bands. In the above situation, this article found that groups of range-domain periodic interference (GRPI) occur in the HSSWR echoes. This paper proposes a FRFT based recursive least squares (RLS) suppression algorithm. Simulations have demonstrated its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Quality Assessment of Android Smartphone with GNSS Raw Measurements in the Arctic Region
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This study analyzes the positioning performance of smartphones using the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) in the Arctic region. It was found that the complex electromagnetic environment and unique climatic conditions in the Arctic impact the GNSS performance of smartphones, leading to frequent errors and satellite lock loss, affecting the accuracy of positioning results. By analyzing the GNSS raw measurements collected using an HONOR 50 smartphone near the NYAL station in the Svalbard Archipelago, this paper explores critical indicators such as the number of visible satellites, carrier-to-noise density ratio (C/N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>), and positioning accuracy. The results indicate that despite signal interruptions and clock biases, the GNSS signal quality received by smartphones in the Arctic region is sufficient to meet positioning requirements, providing valuable data support for polar scientific research and navigation applications.

articleTitle: A Wideband Vertically Integrated Open-Ended SIW Circularly Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A wideband vertically integrated open-ended substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) circularly polarized (CP) antenna based on stacked PCB is presented in this paper. The proposed element consists of three layers of dielectric substrates, the bottom layer is the feeding structure, the middle layer and the top layer collectively configure the radiator. Surrounding metallic via fences are used to form a hollow waveguide. Therefore, the antenna structure can be equivalent to a vertical open-ended SIW with broadside radiation. By introducing a rotationally symmetric etched metal strip, the antenna can form a wide axis-ratio (AR) bandwidth. The simulation results show that the proposed antenna impedance bandwidth is better than 40% (20-30GHz), the AR bandwidth is 35.2% (21-30GHz), and the maximum gain is 7.5dBic. The antenna has a compact structure and is easy to integrate with multi-layer PCB, making it suitable for wideband millimeter wave CP broadside radiation large-scale array applications.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Broadband Frequency Reconfigurable Patch Antenna Based on Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a low-profile broadband frequency reconfigurable patch antenna based on a metasurface is proposed. The antenna consists of an upper metasurface layer consisting of square patches and a lower patch antenna layer. Varactors are inserted between the square patches of the metasurface layer, and the capacitance value of the varactors is controlled by a single DC voltage source to change the operating frequency of the antenna to achieve the function of frequency reconfiguration. Simulation results validate the performance of this antenna. The antenna can achieve continuous frequency tuning within 4.22-5.17 GHz with a single operating state bandwidth of up to 10% (4.68-5.17 GHz). The gain of the antenna can be maintained in a stable state from 6.3-7.4 dBi in all operating bands.

articleTitle: Dual-Band MIMO Antenna with Extended Ground Open-Stubs and Parasitic Patch for Decoupling
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This work reports a dual-band MIMO antenna for the fifth-generation (5G) application. The antenna achieves enhanced isolation by adding extended ground open-stubs and parasitic patch. As the antenna resonates, the antenna current forms one decoupling path in the upper operation band and two decoupling paths in the lower operation band, achieving both electric and magnetic decoupling. The simulation results show that the proposed antenna has a return loss better than 10 dB and an isolation over 20dB in the frequency range of 3.35 GHz-3.45 GHz and 3.75 GHz-4.1 GHz. The efficiency exceeds 90%, and the envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) is below 0.023.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Metasurface Antenna for Indoor Access Point and 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this work, a metasurface antenna suitable for dual-band operation is proposed. The antenna is driven by a microstrip line with a fan-shaped fillet at the end, consisting of a 4 ×4 square patch, whose side and edge patches are etched with single slots and cross slots, respectively, for the purpose of controlling the mode and radiation pattern of the patches. The antenna is analyzed using the method of characteristic modes analysis (CMA). The simulation results depict that the -10 dB impedance bandwidth of the antenna is 3.48-4.34 GHz (21.99<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) and 5.26-6.0 GHz (13.14%), together with a simulated gain of 11.35 dBi and 7.11 dBi, respectively. The proposed metasurface antenna is designed to cover the 5G band and Wi-Fi 6 band, making it an optimal choice for indoor access point applications.

articleTitle: Improved Radiation Performance of Printed Monopole Antenna Using Wideband Planar AMC Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A low profile, gain enhanced printed monopole antenna loaded with artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) is presented. In this work, an AMC structure with wide bandwidth is proposed as the reflector of printed antenna for the purpose of electrical performance improved. The AMC surface is employed as the ground plane of the proposed antenna instead of the perfect electric conductor (PEC) ground plane in the traditional antenna. By loading the AMC structure as reflector, the radiation performance of the printed monopole antenna is enhanced. The impedance bandwidth of the proposed antenna is in the frequency range of 5.01-8.96 GHz (S11<-10 dB) with the size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{30}\mathbf{mm} \ast\mathbf{30}\mathbf{mm} \ast\mathbf{6}\mathbf{mm}$</tex>, which the height is about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.01}\boldsymbol{\lambda}$</tex> at 6 GHz. The relative impedance bandwidth of the proposed antenna can achieve 56.55%, in addition, the gain in the frequency bandwidth range have an average increase of 4dB. Finally, the actual product of antenna and measured results is provided, which are consistent with the simulated results.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis of Time-Domain Ultra-Wideband Radar Receiver Noise
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the time-domain UWB (ultra-wideband) radar receiver is studied from the perspective of noise analysis and processing, and the sampled noise of the time-domain UWB radar receiver under different settings is measured experimentally. The noise components and influencing factors of the measurement system are discussed, the system noise characteristics in time domain and frequency domain are analyzed, and the measurement signal is denoised by multistage wavelet transform. The measured results show that choosing a smaller time window width and more sampling points is conducive to reducing the influence of noise in the measured signal, and the wavelet transform is suitable for denoising the measured signal.

articleTitle: Design of C-Band Four-Element Grounded Coplanar Waveguide Feeding Microstrip Patch Antenna Array for Airborne Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper designs and studies a four-element microstrip antenna array based on grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW) feeding. Rhombus-shaped patches, matching the shape of the cavity edges, are used, and the four-element array is arranged in a diamond distribution to enhance the effective utilization area of the dielectric substrate. Utilizing the characteristics of transmission lines, a 1-to-4 equal amplitude and phase-reversed power divider is employed for the feeding design. The grounded coplanar waveguide replaces the traditional microstrip line feeding structure, further improving the gain. The designed antenna is intended for airborne platforms. This paper presents an antenna design with an operating frequency range of 4.2GHz-4.4GHz, an E-plane beamwidth greater than 50°, a roll plane beamwidth greater than 50°, a vertical plane beamwidth greater than 45°, and a gain greater than 11dB.

articleTitle: A Polarization Switching Low-Profile Transmitarray Unit Design
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a polarization switching low-profile transmitting array (TA) unit operating in the X-band. The receiving and transmitting patches are composed of square patches connected to two microstrip delay lines per patch layer. Crossed-shaped slots are etched on the patches to realize a dual-mode resonance. The structure can realize the polarization, switching between dual-linear polarization (x-, y-) and circular polarization. Continuous polarization transmission phase compensation is achieved by adjusting the length of the microstrip delay lines. The overall profile of the unit is only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.1\lambda$</tex>, Simulation results indicate that the transmission bandwidth reaches 14.3%, and the axial ratio bandwidth is 8.1 %, meeting the design requirements.

articleTitle: A Fast Direct Position Determination Method for Tri-Satellite Based on Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The direct position determination method frequently depends on an exhaustive search to estimate positions. This approach can lead to substantial computational burdens, thereby constraining real-time positioning, particularly in scenarios characterized by extensive satellite coverage. To address this issue, we introduce the MSEPSO-TSDPD algorithm (Multi-Strategy Enhanced Particle Swarm Optimization for Tri-Satellite Direct Position Determination). This algorithm constructs a cost function to estimate the target position using time difference and frequency difference information. By incorporating particle swarm optimization, the algorithm leverages social interaction and a collaborative search strategy between particles, guiding the particle swarm iteratively towards the current optimal solution. This approach avoids the inefficiency of traditional exhaustive search methods that require traversing the entire search space, thus reducing unnecessary computation and enhancing search efficiency. Simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm significantly reduces computational complexity, with computation time being only 15% of that required by exhaustive search algorithms, while maintaining comparable positioning accuracy.

articleTitle: On the Computational Analyses of Eigen Frequencies of Cavity with Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The FEM computational model of eigen frequencies of cavity with loss is presented. According to the computational results, the imaginary parts of frequencies appear. The imaginary parts of frequencies are necessary in the cavity with loss, which is the perturbation of eigen frequencies of the cavity without loss.

articleTitle: Single-Substrate Transmissive Metasurface with Controllable Amplitude and Phase
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this article, a single-layer transmissive metasurface(MS) with independent amplitude-phase modulation is proposed. It has a higher transmission coefficient of -0.77dB, while the coding sequences is 2-bit. Compared with other current MSs, this MS has a higher transmission amplitude. Based on this MS, a spatial power divider is designed and simulated. The simulated results show that, two directed beams pointing to (214°, 0°) and (155°, 90°) are generated with a power ratio of 1:1 at 11GHz

articleTitle: Ultra-Thin Mm-Wave Filtering Antenna with Improved Bandwidth and Frequency Selectivity
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-thin millimeter-wave filtering antenna with improved bandwidth and frequency selectivity is proposed. The antenna is composed of a 0.3 mm thick substrate integrated cavity (SIC) with a crossed slot etched on the top and a probe feed, featuring a very simple structure and reduced profile. In this design, the resonant modes of the cavity, the probe feed and the crossed slot are innovatively combined to form a 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup>-order filtering response without resorting to extra resonant structure. Due to the opposite current induced by the crossed slot, two radiation nulls are introduced at the lower and higher band edges, resulting in a very sharp roll-off between the pass and stop bands. The principles of the antenna are analyzed with a detailed parametric study. For demonstration, the antenna is fabricated and tested. The results show an impedance bandwidth of 24.1-25.5 GHz and a gain of 5.7 dBi. The gain suppression is more than 10 dB within 250 MHz (FBW<1%).

articleTitle: Design of Slotted Waveguide Array Antenna with A Novel Matching Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel matching technique for slotted waveguide array antennas is proposed. Different from the common slotted waveguide array antennas, the metal surface of the proposed antenna is covered with a layer of medium. Then, the metal block used to adjust the matching is introduced into the slots. The relative bandwidth(VSWR<2) of the proposed antenna is 3.68%. The maximum gain is 18dBi and the maximum sidelobe level is -15.4dB.

articleTitle: A Sensitivity Calibration Method for Induction Magnetic Sensors Based on TEM Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A Sensitivity Calibration Method for Induction Magnetic Sensors Based on Transverse Electromagnetic Wave CELL is proposed to address the shortcomings of traditional calibration methods for Induction Magnetic Sensors in terms of frequency, shielding, and space. By utilizing the transmission characteristics of TEM CELL and the ease of obtaining voltage type signal instruments, a new calibration system is constructed and compared with the test data of traditional calibration systems to verify the feasibility of the method.

articleTitle: A Novel Compact Magic-Tee Using Substrate Integrated Fin-Line Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel magic-tee using substrate integrated finline (SIFL) technology is proposed in this letter. To overcome the integration challenges posed by the traditional waveguide magictee structure, which requires installation within a waveguide cavity, the SIFL magic-tee has been proposed. By using the substrate integrated suspended line (SISL) structure of the air cavity, miniaturization and self-packaging of the fin-line magic-T have been achieved. Based on HFSS simulation validation, the proposed compact SIFL magic-tee has advantages of selfpackaging, low loss, lightweight, and easy integration with planar circuits. Within the frequency range of 8GHz to 10GHz, the insertion loss between the input port and the output port is around 3dB, the isolation between output ports is better than 15dB. The return loss of all ports is better than 10dB.

articleTitle: Field on Ground Excited by VLF Vertical Electric Dipole in Horizontal Stratified Nonuniform Ionosphere
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The spaceborne VLF transmitting antenna is idealized as a vertical electric dipole. According to the model of the horizontal stratified nonuniform ionosphere, it has been analyzed and calculated. The magnetic field intensity can be obtained by the Fourier inversion to the wave spectral intensity of the field. The fast Fourier transform method is more correct than the quasi longitudinal approximation method. The calculation results are drawn as follows. First, when the VLF wave arrives at the lower boundary of the ionosphere, it can only pass through the boundary between the air and the ionosphere and continue to propagate for the wave beam of close to vertical downwards propagation. However, the majorities of wave beams are reflected on the boundary, which has the significant inclination angles. Second, the VLF vertical electric dipole antenna laying at the ionosphere can efficiently emit the electromagnetic wave. It can pass through the ionosphere and the air to arrive at the sea surface, and is received. Third, because the D layer of the ionosphere exists at day, and the attenuation of the magnetic field intensity is bigger, so the signal can easily be received at night.

articleTitle: The Research and Design of Quasi-Optical Mode Converters Mirror System
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The quasi-optical mode converters (QOMC) is the key device to improve the efficiency of high-power fusion gyrotron transmission. In this work, the authors report an efficient QOMC design for a compact three-mirror layout in 140 GHz, TE22,8. Based on geometrical optics and iterative phase correction technique, the design of the first-stage focusing mirror and the second and third-stage phase mirrors is completed. The full vector physical optics integration is adopted as the main computational means, and the three-level phase correction surface is iterative optimized around the main polarization field component to realize the mode field conversion with high outgoing Gaussian purity. The outgoing Gaussian purity μv of the phase-corrected converter system is improved from 94.1% to 99.7%, which, combined with a power transfer efficiency μp of more than 98.7%, realizes a high-performance prototype design of a higher-order cyclotron QOMC.

articleTitle: A High Efficiency Ku-band Ridge Gap Waveguide Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A Ku-band high-gain and high-efficiency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{8} \times \mathbf{8}- \mathbf{element}$</tex> slot array antenna was proposed, designed, simulated, and optimized. The prototype of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{8}\times \mathbf{8}-\mathbf{element}$</tex> array antenna is fabricated by the NC milling process on an aluminum plate which can obtain the good mechanical strength performance based on the simulated results. The measured input reflection coefficients <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{S}_{11}$</tex> for the array antenna are below -10 dB over the desired frequency range from 14.2 to 15.2 GHz, and the gain of the array antenna is more than 26dBi, which can be agreement with the simulated results. The dimension of the prototype array antenna is about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{144}\mathbf{mm}\times \mathbf{144}\mathbf{mm}\times \mathbf{18.3}\mathbf{mm}$</tex>, the measured total radiation efficiency of the array antenna is better than 65% in the designed bandwidth. And the weight of the prototype is only about 324g which is suitable for applying on the portable communication system which required the light weight.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband 45° Linearly Polarized Tightly Coupled Antenna Without Collector Loading
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$45^{\circ}$</tex> linear polarization tightly coupled array antenna with an operating frequency covering <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{S}$</tex> to Ku bands. By improving the antenna shape, no collector resistor loading is achieved while eliminating the common mode resonance in the band. The VSWR of this antenna element is less than 2.5 in most frequency bands of the working bandwidth. The tightly coupled structure between adjacent elements effectively offsets the inductance brought by the floor to expand the antenna bandwidth, and the horizontally placed square resistance film effectively suppresses the resonance point in the frequency band. Finally, an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\times 8$</tex> antenna array is designed, which has VSWR <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 3$</tex> in the entire frequency range except for a few edge elements, and a VSWR <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 3.5$</tex> when scanning to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$45^{\circ}$</tex>.

articleTitle: E-Band High-Gain Wideband Slot Antenna Array with Microstrip Ridge Gap Waveguide Feeding Network
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A broadband high-gain 16 ×16 array in E-band and its radiation character are presented. The array consists of subarray of 2 × 2 cavity antenna based on microstrip ridge gap waveguide technique (MRGWG). The upper printed circuit boards (PCB) lays the substrate integrated 2 × 2 slot antenna array and the lower layer is the GWG power divider feeding network. A novel T-junction power divider and a standard rectangular waveguide GWG transition interface is designed and manufactured. Simulated results show that the array has a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert \mathrm{S}11 \vert \leqq 10\ \text{dB}$</tex>, a maximum gain of 29.6 dB and a 3dB beam width of 4 degree in the operating frequency range of 73–84 GHz.

articleTitle: A Multifunctional Metasurface for Broadband Amplitude and Phase Control in the W-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This article proposes a new multifunctional metasurface for controlling the transmission phase and amplitude of incident electromagnetic waves. Different polarization modes are switched to achieve different functions by connecting different branches. At the center frequency of 90GHz, electromagnetic waves can be controlled to achieve beam either deflection, focusing, or multiple beams. Selective transmission of different linearly polarized waves can be achieved within 80-100GHz, and linearly polarized waves can be converted into circularly polarized waves within 80-89GHz.

articleTitle: Based on Wavelet Packet Fractals and PSO-LSSVM Nuclear Explosion and Lightning Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The electromagnetic pulses (EMP) from nuclear explosions and lightning are non-stationary and nonlinear. To effectively identify nuclear explosion EMP (NEMP) and lightning EMP (LEMP), we propose a least squares support vector machine optimized by particle swarm optimization (PSO-LSSVM), combining wavelet packet fractal analysis and particle swarm optimization. Wavelet packet fractal analysis extracts features and calculates the fractal box dimension of each wavelet packet layer. The PSO-LSSVM classifier uses these dimensions to classify the signals. Experimental results show that the fractal box dimension of the 2-layer wavelet packet decomposition effectively distinguishes NEMP from LEMP, achieving a recognition rate of 95.25%.

articleTitle: Anti-Reflection Layer Enhanced Absorption of Laser-Induced Phase-Change RF Switch
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An anti-reflection layer is employed in this study to facilitate the optical switching of GeTe phase-change material, thereby enhancing the efficiency of laser utilization. The film serves a dual purpose by improving optical absorption and providing dielectric passivation for the device. The present work involves the design of anti-reflective layers using different materials, with a comparative analysis of their impact on reducing power consumption. Simulation results demonstrate that the reflection rate of the laser equipped with an anti-reflective layer can be reduced to less than 27% at a wavelength of 532nm. Furthermore, compared to switches lacking an anti-reflective film, the energy density required for amorphization can be decreased from 160 mJ/cm2 to 95 mJ/cm2, effectively lowering the energy threshold for amorphization switching.

articleTitle: Highly Selective Dual-Band Frequency-Selective Rasorber with Second-Order Resonance
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A dual-band frequency-selective rasorber (FSR) with highly selective passband based on second-order response is proposed in this paper. The structure is composed of a lossy layer and two lossless layers. The lossy layer is formed by dual-passband resonators to realize dual transmission performance.
