The lossless layer is cascaded by a two-layer square slot FSS, which realizes second -order band-pass response. The simulation shows that the transmission bands are located around 7 and 10.5 GHz, respectively. The reflection bandwidth below -10 dB covers 3.68-9.9 GHz and 10.12-11.09 GHz. Additionally, the proposed FSR shows the stable transmission and absorption performance for both TE and TM polarizations. It is worth mentioning that the dual-polarized dual-band FSR with second-order response is proposed for the first time, which improves the passband selectivity of dual-band FSR.

articleTitle: Wideband and Low-Profile Magneto-electric Dipole Array with AMC Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a Wideband, low-profile array antenna based on a magneto-electric dipole antenna element. To mitigate the impact of the metal reflector on the radiation of the electric and magnetic dipoles, an artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) is introduced in the design of the antenna element. By incorporating a periodic AMC structure between the radiation source of the antenna element and the metal reflector, the reflection phase characteristics of the metal reflector are altered. This allows the radiation source to be positioned as close as possible to the metal reflector. The designed antenna element achieves good impedance matching and a stable radiation pattern over a wide bandwidth from 5.6 GHz to 8.7 GHz with VSWR <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq 2$</tex>. The total profile of the antenna element is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.06\lambda_{5.6\text{GHz}}$</tex>.

articleTitle: The Impact of Raindrop Size Distributions on the Propagation Characteristics and Differential Parameters of X-Band Polarimetric Weather Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper studies the impact of different raindrop size distribution choices on the propagation characteristics and scattering parameters of polarimetric weather radar at x-band operating frequencies. Firstly, the importance of dual-polarization radar in meteorological observations and its basic principles are introduced, explaining the key role of raindrop size distribution models in radar data interpretation. Then, numerical simulations and comparative analyses are conducted using several common raindrop size distribution models and measured raindrop size distribution data. Through these comparisons, we evaluate the impact of different raindrop size distribution models on radar observation parameters under various rainfall intensities and types, and we compare the changes in multiple parameters with rainfall intensity. The results show that the choice of raindrop spectrum significantly affects the propagation characteristics and polarization parameters of the radar. Especially under heavy rainfall conditions, the deviation of the model is more significant, and the combination of multiple parameters can improve this situation. The conclusions of this study provide data references for the application of dual-polarization radar in precipitation measurement, emphasizing the importance of considering raindrop size distribution choices in data processing and analysis. Additionally, it offers valuable insights for correcting rain attenuation and improving precipitation estimation models.

articleTitle: Application of FDTD Method in VLF Propagation Research
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Electromagnetic waves in the very low frequency (3k-30kHz, VLF) band have the characteristics of low attenuation and good penetration performance during transmission. At the same time, the amplitude and phase of very low frequency electromagnetic waves are relatively stable. These characteristics have made very low frequency electromagnetic waves widely used in fields such as long-distance communication, lightning remote sensing, and global climate observation. In order to accurately simulate the propagation characteristics of VLF electromagnetic waves in the ionosphere, the FDTD method is currently mainly used for modeling and analysis. This article first introduces the historical evolution of FDTD method in studying VLF propagation, analyzes the established FDTD model, and finally provides a summary of certain reference values.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Stopband and Polarization-Insensitive Active Frequency Selective Surface with a Ultra-Wide Tuning Range
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a widely tunable dual-stopband active frequency selective surface (AFSS) is proposed. The proposed design includes a periodic pattern printed on top of a thin substrate and a feeding network at the bottom. Varactor diodes are symmetrically installed on the top metallic layer. The simulation results indicate that the designed AFSS has two operating bands. The first stopband can be continuously tuned within the range of 0.97-6.88 GHz, while maintaining the stability of the second operating stopband. Additionally, the proposed AFSS exhibits excellent angular stability, polarization-insensitivity, miniaturization, and ultra-wideband tunability. It can be used to control electromagnetic wave propagation in various communication systems.

articleTitle: A Modified Simplified Subentire Domain Basis Function Method for Finite Periodic Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A modified simplified subentire domain (SSED) basis function method is presented for solving electromagnetic scattering by the finite periodic arrays. In the method, the SSED bases defined on the cell are obtained by analyzing one cell excited by multiple plane waves. The number of SSED bases is independent of the gap size between the cells. Afterwards, a reduced matrix equation can be obtained. The size of matrix equation is less than that based on modified accurate SED basis functions. Numerical results are shown to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of this new method.

articleTitle: A Geometry-Based Marine Channel Model with Ship Roll
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a three-dimensional (3D) geometry-based stochastic model (GBSM) is proposed for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) land-to-ship channels. For the most serious roll motion in ship fretting, we use a sinusoidal random process to characterize its impact on the ship's attitude. Based on the constructed model, we derive and simulate the space-time frequency correlation function and Doppler power spectrum. The results show that channel correlation grows with the roll angle decreases, implying that the ship roll introduces additional non-stationarity to the marine channel in the time domain.

articleTitle: An Efficient Calculation Method for the Near Field Distributions of Phased Array During Beam-Scanning Status
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Beam-scanning status of the phased array leads to variations in the near-field distributions, and it is costly to carry out exhaustive calculations through full-wave simulation or actual measurements due to the numerous beam-scanning angles. In this paper, an efficient calculation method is presented to obtain the near-field radiation characteristics. A planar array composed of infinitesimal electric dipole elements is selected as an example. The expression of the radiated electric field in the near field is derived through a summation of the radiated field from each array element. Corresponding results are compared with those obtained by full-wave simulation to verify the accuracy of the numerical model. This model can be employed to rapidly obtain the statistical characteristics of the near-field radiated field. The presented results are potentially beneficial for comprehending the near-field radiation characteristics in the case of dynamic beam scanning of arrays. Additionally, these results may further assist in avoiding potential electromagnetic interference issues when other receivers are located in close proximity to phased arrays.

articleTitle: Target Recognition from HRRP Based on Physical Optics Method
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the high-resolution range profile (HRRP) of targets is firstly established with the far-field scattered field. And the scattered field is obtained by the physical optics (PO) method. The convolutional and pooling layers of the convolutional neural network (CNN) are extracted local spatial features from the HRRP sequence. The fully connected layers combine the features of each module to complete the extraction and classification recognition of the overall features.

articleTitle: Domain Decomposition Method Based 3-D Electromagnetic Simulation Research
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces a regional decomposition electromagnetic simulation method, first of all, the antenna structure module is divided into regions to obtain a plurality of subdomains; for each subomain, a tetrahedral mesh is utilized to dissect said subdomain to obtain a plurality of tetrahedra; for each tetrahedron, according to the position of the vertices of the tetrahedron and the length of the edges, a vector basis function is obtained for each edge of the said tetrahedron; for each edge, a vector basis function is obtained for each edge, and a vector basis function for each subdomain is obtained for each edge. function for each edge and the two-spin electric field fluctuation equation of the subdomain to which the edge belongs, calculate the tetrahedron to which the edge belongs. For each edge, the electric field value at any point in the tetrahedron to which the edge belongs is calculated using the corresponding vector basis function of the edge and the double spin degree electric field fluctuation equation of the subdomain to which the edge belongs. Compared with the conventional finite element method (FEM), the method proposed in this paper shows a significant improvement in terms of computation time and required storage space efficiency.

articleTitle: PYRL: A Radiation Source Localization Method in Urban Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In complex urban environments, traditional radiation source localization methods are difficult to achieve fast and accurate localization and cannot spatially visualize their geographic locations. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a radiation source localization method for urban environments called PYRL. The method maps electric field strength values received from sensors into field strength distribution maps and uses binarization and morphological expansion operations to delineate clusters of areas where radiation sources may exist. Subsequently, in combination with the You Only Look Once (YOLO) network, accurate localization of radiation sources at any transmit power is achieved. Experimental results show that the average localization error of this method in complex environments is approximately 4.8 meters, the time to locate a radiation source is about 0.012 seconds, and the determined location of the radiation source is highly consistent with the actual situation, which demonstrates a good application prospect.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Shielding Effectiveness of Metallized Aramid Paper Honeycomb Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aramid paper honeycomb with light texture and high strength is widely used in aerospace, rail transportation, and electrical motor fields. Based on the above advantages of aramid materials, this study first prepared metalized aramid paper, tested its complex dielectric constant and magnetic permeability coefficient by waveguide method, and analyzed the electromagnetic shielding performance of the honeycomb structure composed of metalized aramid paper. Then the equivalent model is employed to calculate the equivalent medium parameters of the honeycomb structure. Finally, the FDTD method is used to obtain the electric field of observation points, from which the electromagnetic shielding effectiveness of the metalized aramid paper honeycomb structure can be calculated for a typical application scenario. The results show that the metalized aramid paper honeycomb structure has a good wave-absorbing function, and its reflectivity can be reduced by up to 93.97% compared with the traditional aluminum honeycomb material.

articleTitle: Low-profile Ultra-wideband Wide-Angle Scanning Tightly Coupled Dipole Array Loaded with Improved WAIM Layer
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this work, an ultra-wideband wide-scanning tightly coupled dipole array (TCDA) antenna is designed. A simple microstrip-to-slotline structure is adopted as the feed for the antenna, which can avoid complex baluns and realize low profile structure. The three-layer dielectric structure is adopted as the upper layer of the antenna to act as a wide-angle impedance matching (WAIM) layer, which can effectively reduce the antenna profile and achieve impedance matching capability when the antenna is scanning at large angle. As a result, the TCDA can achieve wide scanning range of ±60° in the E-/H-planes at 6–18 GHz with VSWRs under 2, and the profile of the array is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.202\lambda_{l}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{l}$</tex> is the wavelength of the lowest operating frequency at the free space. The array proposed in this article has the advantages of ultra-broadband, wide scanning range, low-profile, low-cost, and easy fabrication.

articleTitle: The Influence of Verticality of the VLF Trailing Antenna on the Radiation Field
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The paper calculates the current distribution of very-low-frequency trailing antennas of different shape using the moment method. Based on the propagation theory in the isotropic and homogeneous earth-ionosphere waveguide propagation theory for very-low-frequency electromagnetic wave, we investigate the influence of the antenna verticality for the electric field distribution. The result suggests that the electric field strength is increased by 5dB when the antenna verticality increases from 60% to 80%.

articleTitle: A Res-FCNN-Based Correction Method of Urban Environment Radio Propagation Model
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Radio wave propagation models play a crucial role in the design and optimization of communication systems, especially in complex urban environments. However, traditional radio wave propagation models often exhibit deviations in practical applications, necessitating correction to improve prediction accuracy. Firstly, this paper proposes a method for correcting radio wave propagation models in urban environments and verifies its feasibility using the ITU-R P.1411 model as an example. Secondly, an urban environment radio wave propagation model was constructed based on the ITU-R P.1411-12 recommendation. Finally, the Residual Fully Connected Neural Network (Res-FCNN) model was used to correct it. Simulation results show that the prediction accuracy of the ITU-R P.1411 model is significantly improved after deep learning correction.

articleTitle: Design of a Graphene-Based Hexagonal Circular Patch Yagi-Uda MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to build a Terahertz (THz)-based 2×2 multi-input, multi-output (MIMO) hexagonal angular patch (HCP) antenna. Graphene's unique electrical properties have made it a compelling material for THz-frequency antennas, owing to its capacity to support surface plasmon polariton (SPPs) and high conductivity in this range. We've constructed the antenna on a silicon nitride (Si3N4) substrate, 17 microns thick, with 0.1-micron-thick graphene layers to enhance MIMO antenna efficiency and directivity. The hexagonal patch structure of graphene was chosen for its exceptional characteristics at Terahertz frequencies. Our study highlights the radiation properties of THz-based HCP antennas across the 0.1 THz to 1 THz frequency range. Notably, we achieved return loss (S11) better than -10 dB at 0.52 THz for the unit cell and for the MIMO antenna at 0.69 THz, more bandwidth was achieved. Both the radiation patterns and S-parameters exhibit significantly improved gain and directivity compared to traditional antennas.

articleTitle: An Approximate Algorithm for Transient Near Field Scattering from a Rough Surface in 2-D Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An approximate algorithm is proposed to improve the computational efficiency for analyzing the transient near-field electromagnetic (EM) scattering from a rough surface in two-dimensional (2-D) mode, which is a combination of the time domain physical optics (TDPO) with the time domain Huygens principle. In this scheme, the equivalent EM currents and charges on rough surface are computed by applying the TDPO method. The near-field radiation of these equivalent sources is solved in marching-on-in-time way based on the time domain Huygens principle, where the semi-analytical recursive convolution (SARC) scheme is utilized to reduce the computational cost of the convolution integration of equivalent source and time domain Green's function based on digital signal processing idea. The proposed hybrid algorithm is validated through the comparison with the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method, indicating its reliability and efficiency in the calculation of the transient near-field scattering from rough surface.

articleTitle: Recent Progress in Versatile Metasurface for Microwave and Infrared Manipulation
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In the realm of modern military and stealth technology, the study of infrared and microwave versatile manipulation holds significant practical importance. Such technology allows stealth devices to seamlessly integrate into a multispectral environment, enhancing their resistance to various detection methods. In this paper, our recent related works about versatile metasurface for microwave and infrared manipulation is introduced.

articleTitle: A Dual-Cascaded-Line Method for Sidelobe Suppression of Endfire Leaky-Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces a method to suppress the sidelobe of endfire leaky-wave antenna by cascading two similar leaky-wave antenna structures with perturbed period lengths, different propagation constants, and different ratios to the total length. By designing the two antennas carefully, the first null of one antenna will locate at the first sidelobe of another one, so that the highest sidelobe of the total antenna can be suppressed. The operation performances are predicted and explained, which explore the relation between the required key parameters and realizable antenna performances. The stub-loaded type leaky-wave antenna is utilized to reach the required propagation constant properties and antenna sizes. A prototype leaky-wave antenna is designed and fabricated, where the matched simulated and measured low sidelobe patterns prove the usefulness of the proposed method to suppress the sidelobe of endfire pattern.

articleTitle: A Novel Active Anapole Independent of High Permittivity Material
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel active anapole independent of high permittivity material has been designed. It consists of a linear current source and eight loop current sources. By adjusting the magnitude and phase distribution of these two types of sources, the electric dipole moment and toroidal dipole moment are configured to meet the conditions for anapole, thus an anapole state with no far-field radiation is realized. In contrast to passive anapoles excited by incident plane waves, the proposed anapole is achieved by active feeding, allowing for more flexible control methods. Furthermore, there is no need of high permittivity materials in constructing the anapole, and thereby the robustness in diverse electromagnetic environments is improved. The simulation results indicate that the radiation gain of the proposed anapole is low to -28.5 dB and is significantly lower than those of the linear or loop current source fed individually, which demonstrate its anapole characteristics.

articleTitle: A Wideband High-Efficiency Dual-Polarized Transmitarray Using Strongly-Coupled Grounding ME-Dipole Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a wideband dual-polarized magneto-electric (ME) dipole transmitarray antenna (TA) characterized by high efficiency and independent polarization control. The design integrates the strongly-coupled grounding ME-dipole structure with interlaced orthogonal feeding probes, facilitating independent control of dual linear polarizations within a compact configuration. By adjusting the length of the phase-delay line connected to the feeding probe, a continuous phase tuning range exceeding 400° can be achieved without introducing additional design complexities. As a proof of concept, a prototype TA consisting of 16×16 elements has been designed and analyzed. Simulation results demonstrate that the aperture efficiency reaches 43.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, with a 3-dB gain bandwidth of 23.1 %, spanning from 23 to 29 GHz. The proposed dual-polarized TA exhibits significant potential for millimeter-wave applications.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Prediction and Analysis of Electromagnetic Susceptibility in Integrated Underwater Transducer
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Underwater transducers play a critical role in underwater sensing and communication, but the complex electromagnetic environment inside submarines necessitates research on the electromagnetic compatibility of these transducers. This study first utilizes bulk current injection (BCI) with single-frequency signals to test the conducted susceptibility of the transducer to electromagnetic interference (EMI). Then the electromagnetic susceptibility thresholds of the transducer under different test conditions are compared. It can be concluded that the transducer is more susceptible at lower frequency bands, with unstable susceptibility thresholds. Finally, multiple machine learning techniques are employed to predict the electromagnetic susceptibility of the transducer. The results show that using a BP neural network yields the smallest prediction error for the electromagnetic susceptibility thresholds and has a narrow confidence interval, indicating good prediction stability.

articleTitle: Decoupling Magnetic Dipoles by Mu-Near-Zero Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A decoupling method for magnetic dipole antenna array based on mu-near-zero (MNZ) metamaterials is proposed in this paper. A small loop antenna with a circumference of 0.085λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is used as an equivalent magnetic dipole, operating at a center frequency of 35 MHz. The MNZ metamaterials with double split resonant ring-wire (DSRR-wire) units are placed in the spacer of coaxial small loop antennas. The simulated results show that the coupling between small loop antennas is successfully suppressed, with a maximum decrease of 12.55 dB. This proposed decoupling method is a candidate for future full-duplex communication and multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technology applications.

articleTitle: Far-Field Radiation Variations of the TACAMO Antenna with the Aircraft Orbiting
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The TACAMO system of US Navy releases two antenna cables from the aircraft platform to form a V -shaped dipole antenna with unequal length. Theoretical research and experiments show that with the aircraft orbiting, the field strength radiated by the TACAMO antenna will fluctuate periodically. In this paper, the earth-ionosphere waveguide model is used to establish the very low-frequency (VLF) radio wave propagation calculation code of the TACAMO antenna. The variety characteristics of the radiation field strength at different distances with different antenna verticality when the aircraft is circling around the orbit are analyzed, which provides a basis for evaluating the radiation efficiency of the system.

articleTitle: Theoretical Basis and Application of Dielectric Constant
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The dielectric physical mechanism of complex permittivity is analyzed, and by analyzing typical dielectric computational models for water as well as vegetation, it is found that factors such as water content, temperature, salinity, etc., in addition to frequency, are responsible for influencing the dielectric constant of a substance. This coincides with the dielectric physical mechanism. Finally, the value of dielectric constant in engineering applications is briefly introduced in the form of remotely sensed thermograms.

articleTitle: A Low RCS Microstrip Antenna Based on Chessboard AMC Structure in Ku-band
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A new method aimed to design microstrip antennas with low radar cross section (RCS) is proposed in this paper. An effective phase difference of 180° (±37°) can be obtained over a wide bandwidth frequency range by designing the AMC unit with a reflection phase inversion point and a 0° phase reflection point. The antenna has a chessboard structure and consists of two AMC units. The simulated results show that the proposed antenna possesses more than 10dB RCS reduction with 4.6GHz bandwidth, covering the Ku band. The maximum reduction is 27 dB. Meanwhile, the radiation properties of the antenna have no deterioration, even the maximum gain of the antenna's main flap is increased by 2dB.

articleTitle: A High Isolation Design Used Between Broadband Dual Polarization Transceiver Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: We proposed a high isolation design between two broadband dual polarization transceiver antennas in this paper. It employs periodic metal isolation walls with equal spacing and height to strongly suppress the low-frequency band (LB) coupling. Covering the vertical and horizontal surfaces of the metal with flexible graphene high resistive metasurfaces that easily conform to the structure improves 40 dB in isolation between different polarizations at 6–18 GHz. This device has less impact on the radiation pattern of the antenna. This design not only enhances the isolation between different polarizations but also optimizes equipment heat dissipation and improves device performance.

articleTitle: Adaptive Tunable Flexible Metasurface for Microwave Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Fabric poses a significant challenge as a substrate for active devices due to its weak thermal tolerance and the specific soldering requirements of lumped elements. This creates a notable disparity between flexible and rigid RF technologies. Leveraging the distinctive inner structure of fabric, we propose an innovative method to integrate discrete components on fabric substrates using sewing techniques. We have successfully validated and ensured the stability of this approach. As an example, we have developed a fabric-based adaptive metasurface designed for potential applications in portable electromagnetic (EM) protection.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Planar Isophoric Non-Uniformly Spaced Array for Microwave Power Transmission via Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This work presents a synthesis method of planar isophoric sparse array with maximum beam collection efficiency based on a deep neural network (DNN). Due to the powerful fitting capability of neural networks, a DNN framework is established to determine element positions. Crucial constraints including the aperture size, the minimum element spacing, and the maximum sidelobe level outside the receiving region are considered. This method largely reduces the cost and complexity of feeding networks. Numerical results are presented and compared to the state of the art to demonstrate effectiveness and efficiency.

articleTitle: Reflector Antenna Deformation Compensation Based on Phased Array Feed
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: As human exploration of the universe advances, there is an increasing demand for spaceborne antennas with improved gain, frequency capabilities, and surface accuracy. This paper examines a 9-meter diameter spaceborne reflector antenna, characterized by a focal diameter ratio of 0.6 and operating at 31 GHz, utilizing a truss structure for precise modeling. The study compares the antenna gains achieved with Gaussian feed and phased array feed under varying reflector surface accuracies. At a panel accuracy of 2 millimeters, the Gaussian feed antenna experiences a 2.16 dB decrease in gain compared to an ideal reflector surface, while the phased array feed shows a smaller reduction of 1.55 dB, indicating superior performance with lower energy loss and higher antenna gain. Furthermore, the phased array feed exhibits a gain 1.14 dB higher than the Gaussian feed antenna under the same 2 millimeter panel accuracy condition. This research confirms the feasibility of using phased array feed for spaceborne reflector antennas to mitigate deformation losses. By accurately modeling the antenna's reflective surface, the study demonstrates that phased array feed, employing focal plane field analysis, effectively adapt to deformations of the reflector surface, thereby enhancing antenna performance in spaceborne applications.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Topside Ionospheric Scale Height Modelling Based on Three Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The top ionosphere refers to the ionospheric region above the height of the maximum electron density of F2 layer, and the topside ionosphere scale height is an important parameter to characterize the ionospheric electron density profile above the top. The variation rule of the topside ionosphere scale height model is analyzed, and the relevant model is established to improve the accuracy of the empirical model of the top ionosphere. It plays a vital role in space science research and related engineering applications. In this paper, three kinds of topside ionosphere scale height models are established based on COSMIC observation data from 2007 to 2020, combined with three machine learning algorithms (BP, RF and SVM) and peak parameters (peak height and peak density) are introduced as the main control parameters. BP model only has 0.12GB memory and 0.27s estimated time, which has obvious advantages. The estimated value of the RF model has the most significant correlation with the observed value and the slightest error. The correlation coefficient is 0.84, and the root-mean-square error is 25.97km, significantly improving accuracy.

articleTitle: A Compact Low-Profile Folded Transmitarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A compact low-profile folded transmitarray antenna (FTA) is designed. The antenna includes a top transmission surface (TS), a bottom reflection surface (RS), and a planar feed. The transmission element employs a couple of vertically oriented C-shaped slits etched on a single-layer substrate's opposite sides. The 360°phase span with high transmission amplitude is realized by adjusting the C-shaped slit length and mirroring the element bottom layer. The reflection element is composed of a metal patch printed on a dielectric substrate, which can realize polarization conversion. The profile of the proposed array is reduced to 1/3 of the focal length of the traditional transmitarray, and the profile-to-diameter ratio is 0.22. The simulation results demonstrate that the antenna 3 dB gain bandwidth is 13% and the peak aperture efficiency is 33%.

articleTitle: Inversion of Oblique Ionograms Using the Newton-Raphson Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The inversion of oblique ionograms allows for extraction of ionospheric state information and retrieval of electron density profiles at midpoints along oblique sounding paths, However, traditional inversion methods often face the problems of large computation and slow convergence. This paper presents an enhanced Newton-Raphson-based optimizer (NRBO) algorithm with dynamically adjusted decision factors (DF). It compares the inversion results with those obtained from various optimization algorithms. Experimental results demonstrate that the new algorithm outperforms the improved Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm in both inversion accuracy and computational speed. In a multi-layer Quasi-Parabolic Segment (QPS) ionospheric model inversion scenario, even with an observation error increase of 10 km, the inverted electron density profiles closely approximate the true values, showcasing robust noise resistance. Thus, this method proves suitable for practical oblique ionogram inversion based on actual measurements.

articleTitle: A Passive Target Localization Method Based on Electromagnetic Positioning System Perturbations
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Electromagnetic localization systems are widely used in various environments due to their advantages of not requiring line of sight, no drift, and high signal-to-noise ratio. However, environmental interference can affect the magnetic field distribution, leading to decreased accuracy of magnetic field models and increased localization errors. When metallic objects are present in the localization space, the altered magnetic field induces eddy currents within the metal, further disturbing the original magnetic field distribution. This paper proposes a method for analyzing the position of interference sources based on electromagnetic localization. This method can inversely determine the location information of interfering media within the magnetic field, thereby effectively identifying the positions of interference sources.

articleTitle: Application of Matrix Partitioning Technique for Analyzing the Wide-Angle Electromagnetic Scattering Problems Based on Compressive Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: For the wide-angle electromagnetic scattering problems, a fast computational model based on the method of moments (MoM) combining with compressive sensing (CS) theory has been proposed. Compared with MoM, the computational process is divided into the measurement and the recovery parts by the model, which can effectively enhance the efficiency. To further improve the model, a novel scheme is proposed in this paper by introducing the matrix partitioning technique, by which the computational complexity of both parts can be reduced. The basic principle of the scheme is elaborated in detail, and its effectiveness is validated through numerical examples.

articleTitle: Hybrid Method for the Coupling Effect Analysis of Strong Electromagnetic Pulse on the GSM - R Antenna of High-Speed Train
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Large mesh divisions and low computational efficiency are encountered when traditional full-wave algorithms are used to simulate the coupling effects of strong electromagnetic pulse (EMP) to the antennas of high-speed train (HST). An efficient time domain-frequency domain hybrid algorithm for the rapid prediction of strong EMP to the Global System for Mobile Communications-Railway (GSM-R) antenna of HST is proposed, which consists of the reciprocity theorem, large-scale parallel Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) algorithm, subgridding technique and automatic mesh generator technique. Firstly, an equivalent antenna having the same performance with the GSM-R antenna is designed. Secondly, rapid computation of the radiation electric fields of the GSM - R equivalent antenna is achieved by using the large-scale parallel FDTD algorithm combining with the subgridding and automatic mesh generator techniques. Finally, an equivalent circuit of the GSM-R antenna is constructed, and the reciprocity theorem is applied to quickly calculate the voltage response at the antenna port. To verify the correctness and efficiency, the coupling results of the GSM - R antenna radiated by the NEMP are compared with that of the CST Microwave Studio.

articleTitle: Global Sensitivity Analysis of Eddy Current NDT System Based on SVR Model
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The physics-based simulation model saves times and computational costs for the eddy current nondestructive testing (ECNDT) system to perform sensitivity analysis (SA) over experiments. However, the evaluation of SA by simulation model requires repeated calculations with a large number of uncertain parameters considered. The purpose of this paper is to reduce the cost of model-based SA for ECNDT systems by replacing accurate physics-based model with support vector regression (SVR) model to rapidly calculate Sobol indices. The accuracy of this model is evaluated based on the normalized root mean square error (NRMSE) at a fixed number of testing points. The proposed model is validated by the example of an eddy current NDT system with three uncertainty parameters selected. The numerical results show that the SVR model can be a good substitution of the physical simulation model for SA in ECNDT system.

articleTitle: Design of dual-band filter using SIW resonators with open circuits on opposite sides
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel dual-band filter using SIW resonators with open circuits on opposite sides is proposed. Inner coupling is realized by the coupling slot and metal-hole rows. External coupling is achieved by the dual-feeding line, simultaneously exciting the desired modes (TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100</inf>and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">102</inf>). Through the technology of slot perturbation, a closely-space dual-band (4.85/5.45 GHz) filter is achieved with a 3 dB fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 3.8% and 3.9%, respectively. The dual bands achieve a low insertion loss of 2.4 dB and 2.3 dB, respectively, along with return losses better than 15 dB. The adjacent passband isolation exceeds 20 dB, and stopband high rejection is achieved by introducing six transmission zeros. The measured results are consistent with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: Design of Beamforming Metasurface Based on Fully Connected Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to solve the problem that the period of designing metasurface with specific functions is too long by using electromagnetic simulation software, this paper proposes a metasurface design method based on artificial neural network, which can accurately predict the far-field pattern. In the training process, the root-mean-square error decreases with the increase of the number of iterations, the minimum root-mean-square error is 0.01, and the training time is 21 s. After the training is completed, the model can quickly predict the far-field pattern according to the coding matrix. The single prediction time of the neural network is 0.0065 s, while the single simulation time of the full-wave simulation software is 4 min, which is far more than that of the neural network. The accuracy of the predicted data is verified by comparing the predicted results with the results of the full-wave simulation. By combining the neural network with particle swarm optimization algorithm, the metasurface coding matrix corresponding to the target pattern can be designed. Compared with the traditional metasurface design method, this design method greatly reduces the design time and solves the problems of time consuming and cost in the traditional design method.

articleTitle: B2Net: Body and Boundary Learning for Salient Object Detection in Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Salient object detection (SOD) in remote sensing images (RSIs) has gained popularity recently. However, existing methods do not fully utilize edge information of salient objects. To address these challenges, we propose a Body and Boundary Learning Network (B2Net) to solve the problem of inaccurate edges in saliency maps. Specifically, the B2Net incorporates a body and boundary decoupling module to decompose salient objects into high-frequency boundary details and low-frequency central body features, overcoming the problem of uneven edge pixel distribution. In decoding, we design a multi-scale feature filtering module and a feature cross-fusion module to preserve local features and calibrate global information, thereby enhancing feature representability. Finally, the model is trained using a weighted fusion loss function to achieve accurate detection results. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm significantly outperforms existing methods in SOD.

articleTitle: Decoupling for Closely-Spaced Co-Polarized Antennas Using Heterogeneous Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Heterogenous array is studied in this paper to obtain the low in-band mutual coupling between two closelyspaced co-polarized antennas. By the characteristic mode analysis of a slotted rectangular patch, the linearly polarized mode with bidirectional radiation is selected to form an array with a dipole. Feeding structure is proposed to purely excite the patch mode. Due to the orthogonality of the patch mode and dipole mode, the two-element heterogenous array achieves high isolation of 28.6 dB with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\lambda}/\boldsymbol{4}$</tex> array spacing, which is much higher than the array with two identical dipoles.

articleTitle: Design of Non-Reciprocal Absorbing Material Based on One-Way Transmission Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the Magnetic Surface Plasmon States (MSPs) of ferrite, a new one-way transmission structure is proposed. In the presented structure, unidirectional transmission of surface wave is achieved by applying a static bias magnetic field (BMF) on the ferrite and activating non-reciprocal transmission mode on ferrite's surface. Then, a new Radar Absorbing Material (RAM) is constructed by adding metal ground at bottom of the one-way transmission structure. Compared to traditional RAM, the new design can block the reflected wave besides absorbing the incident electromagnetic energy. The simulation result showed good electromagnetic wave absorbing properties. Our work may provide a new approach of RAM designing.

articleTitle: Ray-Tracing-Based Modeling and Analysis of Complex Urban Channels at 1 and 2.8 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In wireless communication simulations, under-standing the propagation characteristics of electromagnetic waves and establishing accurate channel models are crucial. This paper proposes a wireless communication simulation method that utilizes ray tracing algorithms to rapidly and precisely compute the propagation paths of rays in complex urban environments. This approach greatly addresses current challenges such as limited measurement data availability and high costs associated with data acquisition.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Wireless Power Transfer Based on Nonlinear Planar Spiral Coils
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: While wireless communications are well established, Wireless Power Transfer (WPT), particularly Inductive Power Transfer (IPT), has recently gained renewed interest. This work not only derives the integral functional for the coupling coefficient of generalized spiral coils in the IPT system, but also optimizes it for Nonlinear Planar Spiral Coils (NPSCs), addressing the inefficiencies observed in conventional IPT systems using linear spirals. The optimal NPSCs achieve a coupling coefficient that is 66% higher than that of conventional spiral coils and demonstrate a coupling efficiency of 93% at a transmission distance of coil diameter, significantly improving IPT system performance.

articleTitle: Omnidirectional Circularly Polarized Antenna with Wide Bandwidth and Axial-Ratio Beamwidth Using Conformal Dielectric Polarizer
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An omnidirectional circularly polarized (CP) antenna with wide bandwidth and axial-ratio (AR) beamwidth is proposed for millimeter-wave applications. The wideband (WB) and wide AR beamwidth (ARBW) performance is realized by a novel conformal dielectric polarizer design. Each curved slab of the polarizer is conformally tilted 45° to the incident electric field of the linearly polarized (LP) spherical wavefront. Apart from the conformal polarizer, the proposed CP antenna utilizes a bicone antenna as the omnidirectional LP radiator. Two additional anti-reflection layers are used on the inner and outer surfaces of the conformal polarizer to reduce reflections. Simulation results show that the antenna has an ARBW of more than 60° from 27 to 33 GHz.

articleTitle: Analysis and Evaluation of Uncertainty of Electromagnetic Anti-Interference System in Virtual Dark Chamber
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to extract the radiation signal of the equipment to be measured more accurately in the field test of electromagnetic radiation, in this paper, the virtual dark chamber electromagnetic radiation anti-interference test system based on MVDR (Minimum Variance Distortionless Response) wide beamforming technology and airspace weighted cancellation principle is adopted to deal with the environmental interference. This paper analyzes the detection principle of the system, determining the source of uncertainty in the detection process, classifying and establishing the analysis model of the uncertainty of the system method, and provides a good theoretical basis for determining and reasonably compensating environment and the electromagnetic radiation test to obtain more accurate test results, and optimizes the test process and algorithm model.

articleTitle: Low-SAR Design Methods for Terminal Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To reduce the effects of electromagnetic radiation from terminal antennas on human health, low specific absorption rate (SAR) design methods are proposed in this work. Utilized the mode-current control on the loop structure and metal ground, the antenna element achieves a SAR reduction of more than 65.4% while maintaining good radiation performance. In addition, a low-SAR <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{4} \times \mathbf{4}$</tex> multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) array is developed by placing the presented antenna elements with an optimized layout.

articleTitle: VLF Radiated Field from Curved Wire Antenna in Free Space
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the very-low-frequency radiated fields of a bent wire antenna are presented using the dipole approximation. Firstly, the near-field formula and the far-field formula for electric dipole radiation polarized in arbitrary direction in free space are derived. Then, the superposition of radiated fields of multiple electric dipoles are also given. According to the current distribution flowing through the bent wire antenna, radiated fields from the 6km wire antenna is regarded as the fieldsuperposition of those from 1200 electric dipoles in series of arranging along the bent wire antenna. The correctness of the proposed method is proved by comparing the numerical results with those of the Feko software.

articleTitle: A Novel PN Weighted Timing Synchronization Algorithm in Ionospheric Scatter Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Ionospheric scatter channel (ISC) exhibits a wide range of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), so transmission systems may work at a low SNR, and ISC also has a severe frequency-selective fading, causing low detection probability. A novel pseudonoise (PN) weighted timing synchronization algorithm is proposed. The constant amplitude zero autocorrelation (CAZAC) is weighted by PN to constitute a two-stage preamble, by employing hierarchical correlation detection at the receiver to decline the computational complexity; before executing the conventional adaptive threshold algorithm (CATA), the proposed non-coherent combining is performed to accumulate the sub-peaks power on main peak to obtain the new peak, which enhances the discrimination between the new peak and background noise under low SNRs and dense multi-path channels. Simulation results show that compared to CATAs based on constant false alarm rate (CFAR), the detection probability is improved by approximately 2 dB.

articleTitle: An Inversion Method of Water Vapour Profile by Using GNSS Wet Delay to Get PWV
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The traditional method to get Precipitable Water Vapor (PWV) from the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) is by using Zenith Wet Delay(ZWD) by means of the approximate coefficient which can cause larger error when the significant fluctuations of water vapour occur. This paper proposed a new inversion method of water vapour profile by using GNSS wet delay to get high-accuracy PWV. By using ten years'(2014∼2023) historical radiosonde meteorological data at Haikou radiosonde stations, water vapor density profiles are retrieved with the intelligent optimization algorithm named Relevance Vector Machine (RVM) based on high correlation between ZWD and water vapor density profile. The highaccuracy PWV is then integrated by water vapor density profiles. The PWV computed from water vapor density profiles are compared to the PWV from the traditional method, the results show that the RMS of PWV computed from water vapor density profiles agree to within 1 mm which is much precisely than the traditional method, which enhanced the precision and versatility of PWV.

articleTitle: Vision Transformer-Based Multi-Physics Field Prediction for Real Marine Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper implements the fine-tuning of a multiphysical field prediction model for the real marine environment based on a pre-trained model of atmospheric physical fields, and proposes optimisation ideas and fine-tuning strategies for more downstream tasks. The physical field of marine environment is affected by its own and atmospheric factors, and it is difficult to capture the deep features of the marine physical field for small area prediction and prediction with few input types. Simple networks such as RNN and LSTM can hardly meet the needs of complex data and increasing number of downstream tasks, and the Transformer has the powerful ability of deep feature extraction and task expansion, and this paper introduces the VisonTransformer architecture for atmospheric physical field prediction. In this paper, we introduce the data methodology and performance evaluation indexes for fine-tuning the atmospheric physical field pre-training model using VisonTransformer structure to predict the multi-physical field of the real marine environment in the Chinese region. The results show that this paper achieves higher prediction density of multi-physical field prediction of the marine environment in the Chinese region, with stable performance in short-medium- and long-term prediction, and significantly better performance than the traditional prediction methods in long-term prediction, which provides a pretraining substrate for the downstream tasks of spatial prediction in the Chinese region.

articleTitle: Unidirectional Transmission Waveguide with Polarization Locking Based on Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: When the polarization state of a system is linearly locked to momentum and its scatterers do not induce spin flips, the resulting edge state with polarization locking can demonstrate unidirectional reflectionless transmission. In classical systems, the creation of polarization-locked edge states relies on two key symmetry transformations: electromagnetic duality (EM-duality) symmetry and parity time-reversal duality (PT-duality) symmetry. While EM-duality supports infinitesimal line-surface wave modes, PT-duality facilitates line-guided wave modes. However, the transmission power capacity of these modes is typically limited by the size of the model. To overcome this limitation, our work integrates both transformation physics mechanisms to develop a chiral waveguide with miniaturization, high power, and increased capacity through the design of a tailored metasurface structure. This innovative design approach opens up new avenues in the realms of photonics and electronics, particularly in the domains of information transmission and processing.

articleTitle: Efficient Analysis of EM Scattering from Multiple Identical Targets Using a Tailored ACA-MoM
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To solve the electromagnetic (EM) scattering from multiple identical rigid targets with traditional ACA-MoM, the multiple targets are treated as a whole, and the ACA is introduced directly without considering the characteristics of the target. This results in repeated storage of sub-matrices, low simulation efficiency, and large memory requirements. To overcome the disadvantages mentioned above, a tailored ACA-MoM is proposed and validated in this paper. In the new algorithm, only one target needs to be divided by octree, and the traditional ACA-MoM is applied to construct the self-interaction impedance submatrix of this target. Based on the translation rotation invariance of the Green's function, the self-interaction impedance submatrix of other targets is the same as that of the established one. Therefore, only one self-interaction impedance submatrix is established and stored in the new algorithm, which results in a large reduction in simulating time and memory requirements. And then the ACA is introduced again to establish the interaction impedance matrices between any two targets, in which translation and rotation are performed to obtain the triangular and RWG information of other targets, and a so-called adaptive near-field coupling (AD-NFC) technique is proposed and introduced. According to AD-NFC, the interaction impedance submatrix is compressed by ACA directly once the distance between the center of the targets is greater than twice the maximum length of the target. As a result, the simulating time is further reduced. Numerical results demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the new algorithm.

articleTitle: A Small-Dimension-Dictionary Sparse Model for OFDM-Based Passive Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In passive radar using sparse representation theory to generate a range-Doppler (RD) map that can achieve better resolution than traditional methods, but has an obvious disadvantage, which is the high computational complexity due to the large dimension of the sparse dictionary. Therefore, basing on a special signal processing method in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing signals, the Doppler channel detector(CHAD), a new passive radar sparse model with a small-dimension-dictionary is proposed. And then the passive radar target detection method is established, considering the sparsity of the CHAD function of the echo signal in the range-Doppler domain. Simulation and experimental results show that the sparse model we proposed has high detection performance while avoiding the problem of too large dimensions of the sparse dictionary.

articleTitle: A V-Band Linear Power Amplifier with 20.4-dBm Psat and 17.5-dBm OP1dB in 65-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a V -band two-stage power amplifier (PA) implemented in 65-nm CMOS technology, featuring a symmetrical two-way parallel power combiner. The design utilizes a cascode amplifier in the power cell and a common-source (CS) amplifier in the driver cell, both integrated with neutralizing capacitors. The PA demonstrates a simulated peak small-signal gain of 18.2 dB and a 3-dB bandwidth of 11.5 GHz. It achieves a saturated output power of 20.4 dBm, an output 1-dB compression point (OP1dB) of 17.5 dBm, and a peak power-added efficiency (PAE) of 13.2%, respectively. The compact core area occupies only 0.125 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>,

articleTitle: Shielding Effectiveness Analysis of Curved Anisotropic Multi-Layered Carbon Fiber Composite Cavities
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The shielding effectiveness (SE) of complex cavities made from curved anisotropic multi-layered carbon fiber composite (CFC) materials is calculated and analyzed using the embedded thin layer technique integrated in commercial software. This analysis aims to identify the factors influencing the shielding properties of these materials. In the paper, a truncated cone-shaped cavity made from curved anisotropic multi-layered CFC materials serves as an example. We calculate its SE for CFC materials with varying layer numbers and fiber orientations. The results demon-strate that the number of layers and the fiber orientation of each layer are key factors influencing the SE of curved multi-layered CFC materials. However, once the number of layers exceeds a cer-tain threshold, these factors have little effects on their shielding properties. The study would provide guidance for designing CFC materials to achieve better electromagnetic shielding properties.

articleTitle: Research on MIMO Beam Integration Optimization Method Based on PredRNN Prediction and Ant Colony Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of 5G base station construction and application, Massive MIMO technology has become an essential key technology in 5G network optimization, and accurate and efficient optimization of MIMO antenna beam configuration has become a research focus. For the optimization of MIMO antenna beam configuration, an integrated scheme based on PredRNN prediction and ant colony optimization is proposed. The experimental demonstration shows that the PredRNN prediction model is closer to the real user distribution, and the ant colony optimization algorithm can effectively solve the difficulties of multi-base station multi-beam joint optimization, thus improving the energy efficiency of 5G network.

articleTitle: Fuze Echo of Background Adaptability Evaluation Model Based on Data Driven
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To address the need for evaluating the adaptability of radio proximity fuze components under complex conditions, a data-driven modeling method based on target characteristics for assessing fuze echo adaptability to ground backgrounds is proposed. The study investigates the impact of soil moisture content on fuze echo responses, using silty soil as an example. The variation in scattering coefficients of silty soil with different moisture levels and grazing angles is provided. The results show that the scattering coefficient is significantly affected by soil moisture content. For instance, at a grazing angle of 90° and moisture content of 1%, the scattering coefficient is about -8 dB, while at 40% moisture content, the scattering coefficient increases to 3 dB. Using the developed fuze ground background adaptability evaluation model, the echo response characteristics of Ka-band fuzes under different moisture levels were predicted. The results indicate that higher moisture content leads to a higher signal-to-noise ratio in fuze echoes.

articleTitle: The Key Technology of PIM in Mobile Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The successful construction of communication satellite system has filled the gap of our national commercial autonomous satellite mobile communication service. With the advent of Huawei Mate 60 series mobile phones, satellite communication has gradually entered the era of popularization. The solution to the problem of passive intermodulation interference is the key guarantee for the successful development and stable operation of communication satellite system. This paper introduces the passive intermodulation problems and related technical breakthroughs in the development of communication satellite payload, and compares the advancement of similar technologies, aiming to provide some reference and enlightenment for aerospace engineering development and ground mobile communication.

articleTitle: Low-Temperature Superconducting RF Integrated Filters for Multi-Band Cryogenic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This work discusses on-chip integrated low-temperature superconducting (LTS) filters that possess triple passbands with prescribed equiripple performance. Based on a polynomial synthesis approach, equal ripple response can be achieved in each passband by introducing a pair of additional transmission zeros (TZ). In addition, two different ripple factors are set for three symmetrical passbands, and their ratios can make the return loss (RL) levels different and controllable. The prototype, after proper transformation /simplification, is then corresponded to lumped inductors and capacitors on-chip using a 4-metal layer LTS Niobium process. With an enhancement of out-band attenuation (thanks to the finite TZs), the filter is expected to be implemented with superconducting rapid single- flux-quantum (RSFQ) logics for generating narrow-line-width microwave pulses for different cryogenic applications.

articleTitle: Holographic Subsurface Imaging with Variance Weighted Canopy-Kmeans Clutter Suppression Method
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Holographic subsurface radar (HSR) is an active remote sensing technology, proven to be highly effective in detecting shallow buried objects. However, HSR is often subject to strong reflected clutter, noise, and other interference from the ground surface in practice, resulting in poor imaging results. To address these issues, this paper proposes a clutter suppression method combining the Canopy-Kmeans clustering algorithm and variance-weighted L1 norm minimization (VWLNM). This method first uses the Canopy-Kmeans clustering algorithm to divide the radar data into several clusters, then weights the clusters based on the prior that the variance of rows and columns in the target area is significantly greater than that of the non-target area. Finally, the weights of the clutter and noise clusters are attenuated by minimizing the L1 norm of the objective function. Experimental results show that the proposed method effectively restores shallow buried targets while eliminating clutter.

articleTitle: Broadband Omnidirectional Antenna with Stable Radiation Patterns for Indoor Data-Intensive Regions
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this letter, a broadband horizontally-polarized omnidirectional antenna (HPOA) with stable radiation patterns in vertical plane is presented. In this design, sector-like slots are loaded at the end of slotline structures to improve impedance matching and to reduce gain variation at high frequencies by changing current path on the ground. Metamaterial-based slow-wave structures, complementary split ring resonators (CSRRs), are introduced to improve impedance matching at low frequencies and to stabilize main beam direction at high frequencies. A prototype of this antenna is fabricated and tested. The designed antenna has stable main beam direction of 30°±5° in vertical plane, and small gain variation less than 1.78 dB in horizontal plane within 1.6-5 GHz (103%).

articleTitle: Research on Obstacle Avoidance Path Planning for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Formation in Urban Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The application of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) in military, civil fields is becoming increasingly prevalent. Due to the complexity of the environment and the diversity of missions, current UAV technology is evolving towards the concept of swarm concept. In this paper, we introduce the environmental factors of the simulation and then adopt the elevation data of the urban model. Subsequently, the Rodrigues' rotation formula is introduced to facilitate the rotation of the UAV formation, combined with the translational coordinates of the path planning, in order to enable the transportation of the UAV formation within the three-dimensional environment. The particle swarm algorithm is highlighted as a key component in the planning of paths for point target formations in urban environment. The algorithm enables the control of distances between targets, the planned paths can be applied in the UAV swarm after the expansion process of the urban model. The above parts are finally integrated to realize the UAV formation's obstacle avoidance trajectory in urban environment.

articleTitle: A 1-Bit Low-Cost Phased Array Element with Switchable Circular Polarization
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a 1-bit low-cost phased array element with switchable circular polarization (SCP) is proposed. The proposed element consists of a cross shaped patch, an annular patch, four diodes, and three direct-current (DC) bias lines. By controlling the on-off state of the four diodes, the phase shift between 0° and 180°, as well as circular polarization switching, can be independently achieved. The proposed element can be applied to the design of a 1-blt satellite communication phased array.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile and Dual-Band Shared Aperture Sparse Array for Beam Scanning Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a low-profile and dual-band shared aperture sparse array for beam scanning applications. A multi-layer structure is used in the design, and metamaterial grid and fractal slot are used to enhance the impedance bandwidth. The proposed dual-band shared aperture array has a bandwidth wider than 14.5% at C-band and 13.3% at Ku-band. Moreover, Floquet modal analysis and genetic algorithm are used to optimize the Ku-band array, and 56.5% sparse ratio is achieved. The proposed shared aperture antenna array consists of 234 Ku-band cells and 57 C-band cells, and has a scanning range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 30^{\circ}$</tex> at C-band and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 60^{\circ}$</tex> at Ku-band. In the whole scanning range, the transmitting and receiving side-lobe-level is basically lower than -18 dB and -25 dB, respectively. To verify our design, the proposed shared aperture antenna array is fabricated and measured, and the preliminary experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Square Tangential Metasurface Automatic Design Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To accelerate the design of electromagnetic metasurfaces, a machine learning-based approach has been proposed, which has resulted in a automatic design of square tangential metasurface. When the scattering parameter (S-parameter) curve of the metasurface, centered between 3.5GHz and 3.8GHz, is provided, the network immediately returns its dimensional parameters. A dataset of the electromagnetic response curves of the metasurface is extracted using a joint Matlab-CST simulator, upon which a neural network comprised of convolutional and fully connected layers is constructed. The network's output dimension is 2, representing two actual dimensional parameters of the square tangential metasurface. After feeding the validation set into the network, it was observed that the network exhibited a high level of accuracy.

articleTitle: A Method for Generating Partial Discharge Signals Based on Time-varying Dipole Model
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With the development of power systems, the safe and stable operation of distribution networks has become a focal point of attention. In this study, we propose a method for generating partial discharge signals based on the time-varying dipole model. By employing the dipole model and combining it with the Hermite interpolation method, we establish a gap-frequency correspondence, allowing the generation of fault signals corresponding to different gap sizes based on existing measurement data. This approach provides a novel method for generating partial discharge fault signals, addressing the challenges of fault signal collection and dataset creation, and opening new prospects for the application of deep learning methods in the field of distribution networks.

articleTitle: A Fast Synthesis and Optimization Method for Filter Antenna Based on Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel optimization method for filter antenna design by use of neural network techniques with coupling matrix is proposed. This method can quickly and efficiently optimize the performance of filter antennas according to the customized demand criteria. Compared with traditional methods, this optimization method greatly simplifies the optimal design of filter antennas by avoiding the complex and time-consuming manual debugging of constructing model dimensions full-wave electromagnetic simulation. The model of T -patch filter antenna with the operating frequency of 2.45 GHz and the bandwidth of 0.3 GHz is used to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Finally, the obtained optimization results are in high consistency with the expected index requirements.

articleTitle: A Joint Optimization Method for TDOA-based HF Source Localization with QP Ionosphere Model
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A hybrid Sinh Cosh gradient projection (HSCGP) algorithm is proposed for solving the high frequency (HF) source localization based on the monolayer quasi-parabolic (QP) ionosphere model using time-difference of arrival (TDOA) measurements of the refracted radio rays. The algorithm utilizes Sinh Cosh Optimizer (SCHO) and gradient projection (GP) algorithm for joint optimization, introducing a novel information exchange mechanism. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm is superior to other algorithms in terms of computational efficiency and positioning accuracy.

articleTitle: A C-Band Low Sidelobe Microstrip Patch Antenna Array for Sum and Difference Beams' Application
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a microstrip patch antenna array for sum and difference beams' application operating from 5.8GHz to 6GHz with low side lobes and good directivity is proposed. The VSWR(voltage standing wave ratio) of the antenna unit in the working frequency band is less than 2. An 8×8 microstrip patch antenna array is formed on the basis of the antenna unit. The VSWR of the antenna array in the working frequency band is less than 1.4 and the gain is 21.6dB at 5.9GHz. By arranging subarrays symmetrically and adding a feed network between the units, the side lobe level of the antenna array exceeds 18dB.

articleTitle: Efficient Calculation of Electromagnetic Scattering Problem with Multiple Excitations by Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury Formula
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this article, the Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury (SMW) formula is applied to accelerate the direct solution of electromagnetic scattering problem with multiple excitations by electric field integral equation (EFIE). To reduce the calculation burden in method of moments (MoM), the dense discretized impedance matrix is transformed into several diagonal matrix blocks via the SMW formula. The low rank matrices are compressed by Lagrange interpolations. The adaptive cross approximation algorithm (ACA) is applied to reduce the storage costs for multiple right-hand sides (RHS) matrix, which can solve the monostatic radar cross section (RCS) over a wide angular band efficiently. The numerical results demonstrate both the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Human Tissue Equivalent Liquid Formulations for 30 MHz to 6 GHz in Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: International organizations have developed standard measurement methods for evaluating specific absorption rate (SAR) at RF using liquid phantoms. A method for preparing human tissue equivalent liquid suitable for 30MHz to 6GHz that meets the standard requirements is proposed. The liquid phantom is easy to prepare and has low viscosity.

articleTitle: Research and Implementation of Deep Underground Target Detection Based on TEM
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Currently, instruments using the Transient Electromagnetic Method (TEM) for target detection are mostly applied in ground, aerial, and marine fields. However, their theoretical methods are no longer suitable for underground spaces, and there are few instruments for deep underground target detection. Particularly in deep underground areas where metal casing exists, conventional detection methods cannot penetrate the casing to measure the target, and the electrode method for measuring through the casing poses various issues, often leading to unsatisfactory results. In order to detect deep underground targets, a theoretical method using the Transient Electromagnetic Method (TEM) for measuring target information beyond metal casings and an axisymmetric differential electromagnetic probe have been proposed. System circuit designs have been completed and a transient instrument suitable metal casings in deep underground environments has been developed.

articleTitle: Comparisons of Amplitude Scintillation Index Derived from 1-Hz BDS C/N0 Measurements Released by Different Types of GNSS Receivers
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Currently there are various Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receivers designed for monitoring ionosphere scintillation phenomena. These receivers are usually based on different hardware designs and use different methods to process raw data. When using simultaneous amplitude scintillation observations released by different GNSS receivers, it is necessary to assess whether their calculated amplitude scintillation index (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> index) are same under identical scintillation conditions.
