This study has compared the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> index derived from the 1-Hz BDS () carrier-to-noise density ratio <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(C/N_{0})$</tex> measurements of B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">lI</inf> signal (1561.098 MHz) and B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2I</inf> signal (1207.14 MHz) released by two types of receivers installed at Guilin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$25.29^{\circ}\mathrm{N}, 110.33^{\circ}\mathrm{E}$</tex>; geomagnetic: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$15.89^{\circ}\mathrm{N}, 177.19^{\circ}\mathrm{W}$</tex>). One of the receivers is ISATM (ionospheric scintillation and TEC monitor) developed by Wuhan University which key component is a OEM628 card produced by the NovAtel company, the other is a Septentrio PolaRx5S receiver. For a signal at the frequency of 1.5 GHz, the S4 value greater than 0.2 indicates the occurrence of amplitude scintillation. We found that for the two receivers the difference of S4 values derived from the 1-Hz <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C/N_{0}$</tex> measurements of B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">lI</inf> signals were close to 0.2, and the difference of S4 values derived from the 1-Hz <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C/N_{0}$</tex> measurements of B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2I</inf> signals were much larger than 0.2 during scintillation activities. Therefore, we recommend using GNSS receivers of the same type when conducting GNSS amplitude scintillation monitoring in a large area.

articleTitle: Design of Shared-Aperture Dual Circularly Polarized Filtering Waveguide Slot Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a dual circularly polarized (CP) ridged waveguide slot antenna array integrated with filters is proposed. The radiation layer and the filtering feed layer are integrated using ridged waveguide. The ridged waveguide is selected to reduce the overall volume, and filtering structure works to obtain high anti-interference capability. Both the right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) and left-hand circular polarization (LHCP) antenna elements are composed of 16 pairs of offset slots, i.e. longitudinal and tilted slots. The RHCP or LHCP is generated by the relative offset of the two slots. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \times \boldsymbol{16}$</tex> elements RHCP (or LHCP) linear array achieves a filtering bandwidth of 15% <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\vert \mathbf{S}_{\boldsymbol{11}} \vert < -\boldsymbol{10}\mathbf{dB})$</tex> and an axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 12.8% (AR<3dB). A linear array with 2 pairs of RHCP and LHCP element antennas is developed. Both the RHCP and LHCP achieve a filtering bandwidth of 14.8% <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\vert \mathbf{S}_{\boldsymbol{11}} \vert < -\boldsymbol{10}\mathbf{dB})$</tex> and an AR bandwidth of 8.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> (AR<3dB), with gains of 16.1dBi and 16.2dBi, respectively. Filtering antenna achieves integrated design and occupies much less space for communication system. The proposed antenna has the advantages of multi-polarization and out-of-band suppression, which can be applied to satellite communication.

articleTitle: Fast Electrical-Thermal Co-Simulation with Volume-Surface Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To achieve a fast electrical-thermal co-simulation of electronic devices, in the electromagnetic (EM) simulation stage, the EM probem is modeled by the volume-surface integral equation (VSIE) and a skeletonization based method for accelerating the MLFMA solution of VSIE is employed; in the thermal simulation stage, a parallel solver for transient heat conduction problem based on finite element method is also proposed, which is developed based on JAUMIN framework. Numerical experiments are conducted on a vivaldi antenna model to investigate the performance of the proposed fast multiphysics solver.

articleTitle: Research on Anti-Jamming Performance of Heterogeneous Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The anti-jamming ability of heterogeneous array antenna in complex electromagnetic environment is discussed and compared with uniform array and orthogonal dipole array in this paper. A circular heterogeneous array model based on sample matrix inversion (SMI) algorithm is adopted. Simulation experiments verify the ability of the model to receive signals and suppress interference under various conditions. The results show that the array produces significant zero values in the interference direction, while effectively maintaining the signal integrity. In addition, it is particularly noteworthy that the anti-jamming ability of the heterogeneous array using only 8 channels matches that of the orthogonal dipole array using 16 channels, which not only reduces the cost and simplifies the design, but also improves the resource utilization.

articleTitle: Real-Time Offshore BDS-3 Single-Station Ionospheric TEC Retrieval Method and Experimental Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Real-time ionospheric total electron content (TEC) retrieval is crucial for ionospheric electron density inversion and ionospheric scintillation detection. GNSS is currently the most effective technology for TEC retrieval. However, there is lack of research on the real-time single-station TEC retrieval methods for marine observation platforms. To address this issue, a real-time offshore BDS-3 single-station ionospheric TEC retrieval method is proposed in this paper. To verify the accuracy of this method, an experimental system is implemented at offshore station in Qingdao for 12 days using undifferenced uncombined precise point positioning (UUPPP) and carrier phase smoothing pseudorange (CPSP) models in ionospheric TEC retrieval. By comparing with Global Ionospheric Map (GIM) products, the RMS of TEC bias of the UUPPP and CPSP models are 14.2 and 19.5 TECU respectively. The results prove that compared with the CPSP model, the UUPPP model is more resistant and stable, which indicates that the UUPPP model is more suitable for offshore observation platforms such as ships and buoys where GNSS signals are more susceptible to radio frequency (RF) interference.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Planar Antenna with High Gain for Millimeter-Wave Application
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band, dual-polarized, high-gain patch antenna optimized for millimeter-wave applications. To achieve dual-band dual-polarized performance, the element is designed as stacked patches with dual-probe feeding. By integrating parasitic strips, the antenna gain is improved. In addition, a bandstop structure is loaded into the element to enhance the cross-polarization isolation. Simulation results of the 2×2 array constructed by the proposed elements show good impedance matching in 15.92-22.58 GHz and 29.47-34.95 GHz bands. The gain of the 2×2 array is 11.4 dBi at 20 GHz and 13.2 dBi at 30 GHz.

articleTitle: Fast Informer-Based Time Series Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Time series data are pivotal in modern technology and industrial applications,but they are frequently impacted by anomalies due to system failures,cyberattacks,or unexpected events. Therefore,swift and accurate anomaly detection in time series is crucial. This paper introduces ‘TransIDS’,an intrusion detection method that focuses on the efficient extraction and detection of time series features. TransIDS uses the Informer model to capture temporal features within data frames more effectively,improving detection performance and reducing runtime. We also fine-tune the Informer model and introduce an automatic anomaly threshold selection method,optimizing it for anomaly detection tasks. We validate TransIDS through experiments on various datasets and compare it with three existing methods. The results show that TransIDS outperforms the compared models in detection performance.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation Platform Development for Analyzing Near-Field Microwave Brightness Temperature Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In the current development context of microwave radiometer calibration, the focus for the calibration target has shifted from the EM and thermal characteristics of the target itself to the optimization of total brightness temperature characteristics; As for the calibration link, with the focus on brightness temperature transfer in the near-field, it has gradually evolved from 2D qualitative analysis to 3D quantitative analysis. In this letter, a numerical simulation platform development for analyzing near-field microwave brightness temperature transfer is reported. Introduced the application background and development status of the numerical simulation platform, including the FDTD solver platform for scattering & reflectivity problems and near-field brightness temperature transfer. In addition, prospects and outlooks were made for future applications.

articleTitle: An Effective TDR Simulation Tool for Circuit Design and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a simulation tool for the time domain reflectometry (TDR) analysis. A complete user interface is designed in this tool. For the TDR simulation, the excitation signal is initially transformed from the time domain to the frequency domain using the fast Fourier transform (FFT). Subsequently, it convolves this signal with the Y-parameter derived from the S-parameter conversion. The resulting response is then converted back to the time domain using inverse fast Fourier transform (IFFT) and analyzed to determine the impedance change through TDR calculation.

articleTitle: Influence of Depolarization Effects of Underlying Rough Surfaces on Polarization Measurement and Calibration
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Fully polarization measurements outdoors are not only affected by the distortion of radar systems, but also by the interactions between underlying rough surfaces and target. In this paper, the influence of depolarization effects of underlying rough surfaces on polarization measurements is analyzed. An improved outdoor polarization measurement signal model, introducing the influence matrices of depolarization effects, is proposed. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate the accuracy of the proposed signal model, revealing that in addition to the co-polarization component in depolarization effects, the cross-polarization component can also significantly impact polarization measurement and calibration.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Shared Aperture Antenna with Wide- and Narrow-Beam for Projectile Radio Detector
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel dual-band shared aperture antenna (SAA) with wide- and narrow-beam for projectile radio detectors. The high-frequency antenna is a 2×2 microstrip antenna array which designed integrally with the hood operating in the Ka-band. The hood of the Ka-band array can also serve as an S-band-working antenna, a differentially fed dielectric resonator antenna (DRA). Simulation results demonstrate that SAA achieves an operational bandwidth of 380MHz in the S-band and 1.1GHz in the Ka-band. The S-band DRA simulated gain is 4.6dBi and the 3dB beamwidth is 100°. The simulated gain of the Ka-band array is 13.5dBi with the 3dB beamwidth is 36°, and the frequency ratio of the proposed SAA is 1: 10.

articleTitle: Security Device Based on Terahertz Metasurface with Robust High-Order BIC
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Metasurfaces are widely used in terahertz sensing and communication devices for their ability to modulate terahertz waves in multiple dimensions. Metasurface devices based on the Dynamic Heterogeneous Redundancy (DHR) architecture have been shown to enhance the confidentiality and security of terahertz wave wireless communication. High-order BICs are particularly intriguing because of their strong resilience to structural defects. As a result, we propose an aluminum-graphene hybrid metasurface with high-order BIC, and leverage the robustness of the high-order BIC to design security hardware based on DHR architecture.

articleTitle: A Gramian Angular Field and Dual-Stream Transformer-Based Inversion Model for Retrieving Evaporation Duct from Radar Sea Clutter
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This article builds a novel evaporation duct inversion model based on the Gramian angular field (GAF) and dual-stream Transformer, termed EVDIFormer. Considering the complex nonlinear correlations between sea clutter and modified refractivity profile (M-profile) within the evaporation duct, this model leverages Transformer's superior feature extraction abilities to model the mapping between them. Moreover, the model will transform input sea clutter into two different sea clutter GAF matrices before feature extraction. This approach makes the model more efficient in processing sea clutter data by transforming complex nonlinear features into sparse matrix representations that can be handled more easily. By adopting dual-stream Transformer to extract features separately from the different GAF matrices, the model can extract and fuse different sea clutter features, thus achieving a more comprehensive feature extraction of sea clutter.

articleTitle: High Sensitivity Photodetector for Optical Undersampling Microwave Frequency Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To achieve high-sensitivity electric field signal measurement in an optical frequency comb undersampling real-time microwave measurement system, this article designs a high-saturation optical power balanced photodetector suitable for the system. Testing indicates that this photodetector supports pulsed optical power injection up to 5 dBm, resulting in a 21 dB improvement in SNR compared to single-ended detection and achieving a sensitivity better than 1 m V/m.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Multi-Beam Phase Array Antenna for LEO Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Multi-beam antenna has high-gain wide-beams to achieve 3D full space coverage. In this paper, an antenna with multiple beams is designed for the LEO satellite communication. Seven subarrays are used to cover different areas on earth with seven fixed wide-beams. Each subarray contains 4×4 antenna elements with 12mm element spacing. The entire array antenna including 16×7 elements form a phase-controlled beam to enhance the gain of antenna in a particular given area. Moreover, the designed antenna has a compact structure.

articleTitle: Overview of the Design Methods of Electromagnetic Compatibility in Electronic Systems of Fuzes
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Fuze is a control system or device that uses target information and environmental information to detonate or ignite the charge of the ammunition warhead under predetermined conditions. Fuze plays a more and more important role in modern battlefield electromagnetic environment. At present, the electromagnetic environment of the fuze electronic system is complex and harsh, and the lead-war cooperation and anti-electromagnetic interference have become new equipment development requirements. This paper summarizes the previous fuze electromagnetic design optimization methods, and provides a solution to the electromagnetic compatibility problem of the fuze electronic system in the early design stage.

articleTitle: Far-Field RCS Scattering Characteristics of Complex Targets Illuminated by Vortex Beams Based on FEKO Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Compared with the traditional plane wave, vortex beams have the advantages of improved resolution, improved anti-interference ability and flexibility in the field of target detection. Studying the scattering characteristics of radar targets on a vortex beam is the frontier research direction in the field of target detection. In this paper, FEKO simulation software is used to simulate the bistatic radar cross section (RCS) scattering characteristics by importing point source data of a vortex beam. The effects of different scattering directions, incidence angle and topological charge of a vortex beam, size and structure characteristics of a complex target on RCS are calculated and analyzed. The results show that the far-field RCS of the target is greatly affected by the incident and receiving parameters of the vortex beam. This paper lays a foundation for further obtaining more target information by using the vortex beam.

articleTitle: Theory and Analysis of Influencing Factors of Electromagnetic Wave Wireless Transmission in Cased Wells
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Low-frequency electromagnetic telemetry technology has been widely used in the oil and gas industry. It can realize the collection of downhole data and transmit it to the ground in real time, so that ground workers can obtain formation parameters in a timely manner. However, the application of this technology in cased wells has long been limited by the high magnetic permeability and low resistivity of metal casings. This makes the casing absorb most of the electromagnetic waves transmitted by the downhole transmitter, resulting in the electromagnetic signal received on the ground being much weaker than the signal transmitted by open hole wells. Based on the finite element method, this paper constructs a theoretical model of downhole electromagnetic wave transmission, and through simulation, deeply studies the influence of various factors such as casing conductivity on the attenuation law of electromagnetic waves. We propose a method of double helical loop antenna based on electromagnetic induction to solve the shielding problem of metal casing, and the calculation results are relatively ideal.

articleTitle: A One-Dimensional Electronic Fluid Model Based on the Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The breakdown of gas by high-power microwaves generates plasma, which significantly impacts the propagation of these microwaves. Consequently, investigating the atmospheric propagation of high-power microwaves is of paramount importance. This study employs an electron fluid model, integrating additional models to explore the interaction between high-power microwaves and gas plasma. The paper presents the difference equations of the one-dimensional electron fluid model, which are numerically solved using the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method. To validate the efficacy of this algorithm, the simulated air breakdown threshold is compared with experimental data, revealing a strong correlation between the two.

articleTitle: Application of the Sunflower Array in Sparse Phased Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents an aperiodic sunflower array. The positions of the antenna elements are directly obtained using a formula, resulting in a lower maximum sidelobe level over a bandwidth with a frequency ratio exceeding 25:1. Additionally, to enhance the directivity of the proposed antenna, all original antenna elements are replaced with a 4×4 antenna subarray. Each subarray's 4×4 antenna elements are synthesized through a passive power divider network and connected to the TIR component, with negligible cost increases to the antenna array. The adjacent subarray spacing is about 3λ. Additionally, the maximum sidelobe levels for the proposed sunflower array in the transmitting and receiving states are -17.5 dB and -29 dB, respectively. The maximum sidelobe level remains below -12 dB when the beam direction is scanned to 15°. Hence, this indicates that the proposed sunflower array has the capability to suppress grating lobes, making it highly promising for the design of large-spacing sparse arrays.

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Synthesis of Radome-Enclosed Sparse Linear Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Radiation pattern synthesis of sparse antenna arrays has always been a hot topic in antenna analysis and design. In engineering, sparse arrays can help reduce costs and have significant positive impacts. When considering the mutual coupling between elements, synthesizing the radiation pattern for sparse arrays becomes more complex, especially when taking into account of a radome. Considering the mutual coupling, the active element pattern (AEP) of each element of the sparse array is different, which will consume a lot of time if the full-wave simulation is used. In order to solve this problem, a method combining sub array approximation and simulated annealing (SA) is proposed to optimize the sparse position and radiation pattern of sparse array, which can greatly reduce the optimization time. The example of radome-enclosed sparse linear arrays validates the good performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Design of a Digitally Controlled Reconfigurable Dielectric Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The article presents a digitally controlled reconfigurable dielectric array antenna with polarization and radiation pattern agility. The design is based on dielectric antenna, with polarization direction changed by cross-shaped slot-loaded switches, and a microstrip line series 180° phase shifter to form a 1-bit phase. The array antenna has two orthogonal linear polarization states, as well as sum and difference radiation beams. The antenna operates with bandwidth of 3.2%.

articleTitle: Application of Optimal Sampling Interpolation Algorithm in Antenna Far-Field Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Antenna far-field measurement is a common method to obtain its radiation characteristics. In order to obtain the details of the pattern, the angular interval of the measurement of the pattern should generally be less than 1/10 of the half-power beamwidth of the antenna under test, otherwise it will lead to inaccuracies in the relevant parameters of the pattern such as half-power beamwidth and sidelobe level. In order to obtain accurate antenna far-field measurement results, the measurement angular interval is required to be as small as possible, which results in long test time and low test efficiency. In this paper, an efficient pattern measurement method based on the optimal sampling interpolation algorithm is proposed. By increasing the sampling angular interval to the order of the half-power beamwidth of the antenna under test, the pattern with arbitrarily small angular interval can still be reconstructed accurately and the measurement efficiency can be significantly improved.

articleTitle: Wideband Simulation of Electromagnetic Scattering from Multiscale Objects in Half Space
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Wideband simulation of electromagnetic (EM) scattering from multiscale objects in a half space is discussed in this paper. The half-space Green's function (HSGF) is applied in the integral equation formulation so that the discretization is only associated with the scattering objects. To account for the multiscale nature of the geometry, the discontinuous Galerkin (DG) approach which works for nonconformal mesh is further employed. Finally, the wideband current is reconstructed by the Maehly approximation based on Chebyshev polynomials, from which the wideband RCS can further be deduced. Numerical results have demonstrated the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method in the wideband simulation of multiscale objects in half space.

articleTitle: A Ku-Band Compact Wideband Tri-Polarized Antenna with Low Cross Polarization
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A Ku-band compact wideband tri-polarized antenna is proposed. The antenna consists of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 45^{\circ}$</tex> dualpolarized ring-shaped dipoles and the vertical distributed monopole. A simple feed structure formed by metallized vias is proposed to solve the feeding problem of the compact dualpolarization dipoles. Meanwhile, Y-shaped coupling lines and V-shaped parasitic strips are adopted to expand bandwidth for dipoles. The distributed monopole is fed by a four-ways power division network and its bandwidth is expanded through loading the feeding vias of dipoles. Simple feed forms and functional multiplexing of feed structures between different polarizations result in a compact and symmetric tri-polarized antenna with the size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.45\lambda_{0}\times 0.45\lambda_{0}\times 0.23\lambda_0$</tex>. The simulated results indicate the tri-polarized antenna has an overlap bandwidth of 28.7%, the port isolation greater than 30dB and the cross polarization less than -28dB in operating bandwidth, which can be applied in satellite systems to improve communication performances.

articleTitle: Ground Testing of the VLF Antenna in the Prototype Spaceborne Plasma Sounding System
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In response to the need for detecting the plasma environment within the inner magnetospheric region, Nanchang University has developed a prototype of a spaceborne radio plasma sounding (SRPS) system. One of the core systems of the prototype is the antenna system, which operates in a frequency range of 30 kHz to 3 MHz and includes a 240-meter-long satellite-borne very low frequency(VLF) broadband dipole antenna. However, unlike the space environment, the performance of large antennas can be affected by ground coupling. To test the performance of this antenna on the ground, a drone-suspended 120-meter monopole antenna and a horizontal low-frame 240-meter dipole antenna system were designed and fabricated. The antenna performance, especially in the very low frequency band, was tested through long-distance signal transmission and reception experiments, ionospheric vertical sounding experiments, and ionospheric oblique sounding experiments. The test results show that the antenna has good performance in the broadband operating range. This work can provide a reference for the design and ground testing of miniaturized satellite-borne very low frequency broadband antennas.

articleTitle: GNSS Ionospheric Scintillations Observed in the Western Pacific Sector During the 1 December 2023 Geomagnetic Storm
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A severe geomagnetic storm occurred on 1 December 2023. During this geomagnetic storm we found that strong ionospheric scintillations occurred from low-latitude to mid-latitude more than geomagnetic latitude 38° in the western Pacific sector along geomagnetic 170°W on 1 December 2023 by analyzing ground-based Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) observations. It is found that strong eastward penetration electric field (PEF) occurred from 10.12 to 13.12 UT (universal time) on 1 December 2023, corresponding to 18.12 to 21.12 LT (local time), i.e. the early evening period, in the western Pacific sector along geomagnetic 170°W. This intense eastward PEF mapped quickly along the geomagnetic field lines from high latitudes to the magnetic equator, and led to the occurrence of the intense eastward electric field from 10.12 to 13.12 UT on 1 December 2023 in the equatorial F region ionosphere along geomagnetic 170°W, which caused the uplifting of the equatorial F region ionosphere and provided suitable conditions for the growth of the generalized Rayleigh-Taylor instability (RTI), and then led to the occurrence of strong GNSS ionospheric scintillations in sequence from low-latitude to mid-latitude along geomagnetic 170°W in the northern and southern hemispheres on 1 December when GNSS ionospheric scintillations rarely occur in those regions.

articleTitle: A 2 × 2 Self-Decoupling MIMO Patch Antenna Array With Stable Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel 2 × 2 MIMO patch antenna array with high port isolation, stable radiation pattern, and high gain of element has been proposed. The array is composed of four TM12 mode circular patches with 0.2 mm patch-to-patch separation. By loading double slots to the patch center of each element, it reduces the sidelobe level (SLL) of the TM12 mode of the circular patch antenna and lowers the lateral radiation, achieving the stable radiation pattern. And by reshaping the electric field distribution in the E-plane, the electric coupling of the array in the E-plane is further suppressed. The original weak-field regions of the TM12 mode circular patch contribute to the intrinsic high isolation of the H-plane coupled. The measurements show that the array can achieve intrinsic high isolation of more than 20 dB, element gain of 9.9 dBi, and cross-polarization level below -20 dBi without using any extra decoupling network.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Evaporation Duct Delay for Over-the-Horizon TDOA Positioning
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The delay caused by rays must be evaluated effectively when using the evaporative duct to realize the over-the-horizon TDOA Positioning. Based on the ray tracing algorithm of Taylor series approximation, this paper establishes a propagation model of rays within the evaporation duct to analyze the delay caused by the multipath effect and the ray propagation speed. The results show that the evaporation duct delay is influenced by the height of the receiving antenna and the height of the duct. The multipath delay of rays that propagate over the horizon within 250 km is approximately on the order of 100 ns, and the multipath delay error is approximately on the order of 0.1 ns.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Metamaterial Structure for High-Loss Liquid Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces a dual-band RF planar sensor designed for the detection of sucrose solutions at varying concentrations. The sensor is composed of a microstrip line and complementary split-ring resonators (CSRR), with each CSRR unit demonstrating band-stop characteristics at resonant frequencies of 2.45 GHz (ISM) and 4.9 GHz. CST simulation results indicate that changes in the liquid concentration placed on the CSRR result in corresponding changes to its resonant center frequency and amplitude response. By utilizing data derived from CST simulations, a relationship between the complex dielectric constant and the resonant center frequency can be fitted. When compared with reference dielectric constants measured by a commercial coaxial probe, this method yields maximum relative errors of 3.6% for the real part and 9% for the imaginary part of the dielectric constant, respectively. The measured dielectric constants also validate the applicability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Efficient Analysis of Scattering Problems for Finite Periodic Arrays Using Compressive Sensing and Characteristic Mode Basis Function Method
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a new method combining compressive sensing (CS) with characteristic mode basis function method (CMBFM) is proposed to accelerate the solution of finite periodic array scattering problems. Due to the repetitive nature of the array elements, the proposed method only needs to perform eigenmode analysis on the reference elements. The sparse basis functions in CS theory are constructed subsequently and the least squares method is used as the recovery algorithm to solve the overdetermined CS equation quickly. Compared with the method of moments (MoM) and CMBFM, the proposed method effectively reduces the solution time and memory consumption. Numerical simulation results verify the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Fast-Processing Approach for Passive OFDM Radar Clutter Rejection
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The pervasive clutter in passive radar poses a significant challenge to radar target detection. Passive radars utilizing pulse-to-pulse incoherent signals, such as those derived from civilian communication signals, are particularly susceptible to clutter interference. This interference significantly raises the pedestal level of the Range-Doppler (RD) map, thereby completely obscuring the target. While numerous approaches have been developed to address this issue, including those based on least-squares or compressed sensing, they often suffer from practical limitations, such as high computational complexity or limited clutter suppression capabilities. In this paper, we present enhancements to the Extensive Cancellation Algorithm (ECA) method, leveraging the Least Squares QR factorization(LSQR) approach, which significantly reduces the time complexity but still maintain the performance levels of the original method. Furthermore, the original method is constrained by the storage requirements of computing devices, and the selection of clutter suppression points is limited. The new method overcomes these limitations, enabling the suppression of more clutter points at once.

articleTitle: Acceleration of FDTD Method Using Deep Computing Unit
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Parallel computing finds extensive applications in numerical modeling of large-scale electromagnetic problems. We present a method for accelerating finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method using deep computing unit (DCU). Simulation results show that the proposed method provides a significant improvement in efficiency compared to serial FDTD and parallel FDTD using multicore CPU. It offers a potential improvement for FDTD method in solving large-scale electromagnetic (EM) problems combining with high-performance computing (HPC) technology.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Study on Electromagnetic Absorption and Mechanical Properties of Honeycomb Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: As the detection capabilities of modern detectors represented by radar continue to improve, the demand for stealth technology in aerospace is growing, which has promoted the development of advanced absorbing materials and structures. Honeycomb absorbing structure is a new type of sandwich structure, has excellent load-bearing capacity and absorbing performance. In order to improve the absorption and mechanical performance of honeycomb structure simultaneously, the gradient honeycomb absorbing structures with top skin and bonding layer are designed. The equivalent electromagnetic parameters are obtained by Hashin-Shtrikman (HS) method and the out-of-plane compressive performance of the honeycomb is simulated using the quasi-static compression method. The results show that increasing the honeycomb height effectively enhances the wave absorption performance of the honeycomb, achieving a reflectivity below -20 dB near the absorption peaks, while having minimal impact on mechanical properties. Reducing the honeycomb aperture size can strengthen the out-of-plane compressive performance of the honeycomb, but does not significantly improve the wave absorption effect.

articleTitle: Temperature Effect on the Electromagnetic Susceptibility of Analog Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This article investigates the temperature effect on the electromagnetic susceptibility (EMS) of analog sensors through theoretical analysis and testing. The combined effects of electromagnetic interference (EMI) and temperature variation on analog sensors are analyzed based on the circuit principle of the operational amplifier. The test platform is constructed by using the equipment of bulk current injection (BCI) method and a temperature chamber, which are utilized to evaluate the temperature effect on the EMS of two different analog sensors. The results show that with the same EMI, temperature variations lead to differences in EMS of analog sensors.

articleTitle: Discussion on Mechanical ELF Antenna Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, mechanical extreme low frequency (ELF) antenna with rotating permanent magnet is discussed. Theoretically analysis and simulation show that in the near-field region within hundreds of kilometers, the amplitude of velocity field of the ELF antenna is much greater than that of the acceleration field. An ELF antenna, comprising a rotating permanent magnet cube made of NdFeB-N35 with the side length of 50mm, is fabricated and tested. The results verify that, rather than the velocity field, the velocity field is the main carrier for ELF communication.

articleTitle: Computerized Ionospheric Tomography Based on Simulated STEC Along Small-Satellite Constellation-AIS/ADS-B Signal Rays
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The Automatic Identification System (AIS)/ Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) signal received by satellites can be used to estimate slant total electron content (STEC) for computerized ionospheric tomography (CIT), and small satellites flying inside the ionosphere provide good opportunities for the ionospheric observation. STEC calculated using small satellite-AIS/ADS-B signals can be applied for high-resolution CIT. The CIT is performed using the simulated STEC along the small-satellite constellation-AIS/ ADS-B signal rays with a resolution of 5 km.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Antenna with Low Scattering Characteristic for Aperture-Shared Array
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A dual-polarized antenna with low scattering characteristic is proposed as a low-band (LB) antenna in aperture-shared antenna arrays without destroyed radiation pattern of high-band (HB) antenna over a broadband. The low scattering characteristic is achieved by etching composite slot included ring slot and quasi-cross slot (RSQCS) on the radiator of LB antenna. Due to the spatial bandpass response in HB, the RSQCSs make the LB antenna with reverse induced current realize little distortion to the radiation patterns of the HB antenna. For demonstration, the proposed dual-band antenna array, operating in the LB of 1.7-2.7 GHz (VSWR<1.5) and the HB of 3.3-4 GHz (VSWR<1.5), is fabricated. The simulation and experimental results present good capability of cross-band scattering suppression and restoring radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Laser-induced phase change RF switch with absorption enhancement based on gratings
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The present study introduces a radio frequency (RF) switch that leverages the phase change induced by laser irradiation, which is based on the principle of one-dimensional gratings. The technology of laser-induced heating is recognized for its efficiency, precision, environmental sustainability, and cost-effectiveness, characterized by its high local heating and rapid cooling capabilities. Through the fabrication of gratings on the upper surface of GeTe and the meticulous tuning of these gratings' parameters, the study achieves an impressive laser absorption rate of 84% for the crystalline film at an incident wavelength of 532 nm. Furthermore, the amorphous film demonstrates a laser absorption rate of 73%, thereby markedly enhancing the laser's utilization efficiency. This advancement holds significant potential for applications in RF switch technology, offering a novel approach to achieving high-performance phase change mechanisms.

articleTitle: A Broadband Dual-band Dual-circularly Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a wideband dual-band dual-circularly polarized antenna, achieved by integrating a helical antenna and an open-ended waveguide antenna to operate in two frequency bands. The antenna demonstrates bandwidths of 42.4% and 19.2% with S11<-10dB standard in the respective frequency bands, along with axial ratio bandwidths of 35.6% (4dB) and 19.9% (3dB). Both simulated and measured results confirm the excellent performance of the proposed antenna.

articleTitle: Validation of IRI and IRTAM Models Based on Global Ionosphere Radio Observatory Data
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The ionospheric model serves as a crucial pillar for both space science research and the engineering of radio systems. Precise understanding of the ionospheric model's performance is a foundational requirement for the attainment of high-precision corrections to ionospheric errors. Utilizing ionospheric data collected through Global Ionospheric Radio Occultation (GIRO), the International Reference Ionosphere (IRI) model and the International Reference Ionosphere Model (IRTAM) were subjected to analysis and evaluation. The outcomes of this evaluation indicate that: 1) The average absolute prediction errors of the ionospheric parameters foF2 and hmF2 of the IRI model in 32 regions including KING SALMON in 2011 were 2.8292 MHz and 48.7899 km respectively, while the prediction averages of the IRTAM model were 3.0790 MHz and 45.0783 km respectively. It can be seen from this that the reliability of the IRTAM model in predicting the foF2 parameter is slightly lower than that of the IRI model, but the difference is not significant. The error in predicting the hmF2 parameter is significantly lower than that of the IRI model, which means that the IRTAM model has a significant advantage in the performance of predicting the hmF2 parameter. 2) Within one day, with the fluctuation of solar activities, the fluctuation range of the prediction error maximum and minimum of the IRI model for hmF2 in different regions is between 2.15 and 4.46 times, while the error fluctuation range of the IRTAM model is within the range of 1.71 to 3.71 times. This comparison shows that solar radiation has a certain impact on the prediction accuracy of both models, but the degree of influence on the IRTAM model is relatively small, and its error fluctuation range is more convergent, reflecting the stability of this model in prediction accuracy is better than that of the IRI model. 3) For the prediction error of the hmF2 parameter, the average value of the IRTAM model is 0.1578, while that of the IRI model is 0.1674. For the foF2 parameter, the average prediction error of the IRTAM model is 0.3535, and that of the IRI model is 0.3360. In addition, the errors of the IRTAM model in predicting the B0 and B1 parameters are 0.3197 and 0.3824 respectively, which further confirms the advantage of the IRTAM model in prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Adaptive Clutter Suppression Method for Target Detection in Clutter Region
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The rapid growth of consumer-grade unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) not only brings convenience to people's life, but also poses risks to the public safety. Thus, effective low-altitude regulatory measures are urgently needed to respond to such situation. With advantages of no signal transmitting, less maintenance, and low operation costs, passive radars become an important means for low-altitude surveillance. In the passive detection, echo signals of UAVs are prone to entering clutter region and being obscured by clutters due to their characteristics of low flying height, slow speed, and small sizes, which challenges the clutter suppression and signal detection. To tackle this problem, an adaptive clutter suppression method based on successive cancellation for target detection in clutter region is proposed in this paper. By taking advantage of the time-invariant characteristic of clutter spectrum peak and the time-variant characteristic of target spectrum peak, this method transforms the range migration problem in conventional researches into a helper of target identification in clutter region, and thus achieves the purpose of adaptively identifying strong clutters from multi-frames detection data and suppressing them as well as protruding the target in clutter region, which lays the foundation for further target detection. Experimental results based on simulated data show that the proposed method can effectively suppress strong clutters and protrude the weak target in clutter region, which validates the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A C-Band Low-Profile Miniaturized Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This article describes a planar antenna array in C-band, which has the characteristics of low-profile and miniaturization. The antenna array element is designed on the double-sided PCB board with matching circuit structure and the antenna array is composed of four elements with the same structure. The simulation results show that the radiation frequency of the antenna array is 5.91GHz and the gain can reach 4.43dB. Moreover, this antenna array design does not require a separate radiator with a height of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.01}\boldsymbol{\lambda}$</tex>. By changing the capacitance value of the matching circuit, the antenna array elements resonate at different frequencies with good isolation, which can be applied to the transceiver antenna array.

articleTitle: High-gain Antennas Loaded with Metasurfaces for Customer Premise Equipment Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a design of a high-gain 5G antenna array for Customer Premises Equipment (CPE). The antenna unit in the array consists of two circular dipole elements, a partial reflecting surface (PRS) layer, and a feeding structure. Simulation results indicate that within the desired operating frequency range (3.2-3.8 GHz, VSWR<2), the PRS layer based on meta-surface effectively enhances the average gain of the unit by 1 dBi and provides a decoupling of at least 6 dB for the array. Physical validation confirms the antenna's operational frequency band from 3.15 to 3.75 GHz (VSWR<2), with unit's isolation exceeding 27.5 dB and inter-unit isolation exceeding 26 dB. The individual unit gains in the array range from 6.8 to 8.8 dBi. Overall, this meta-surfaces-based antenna array can be applied to CPE systems to enhance communication capabilities with base stations.

articleTitle: A High Gain Antenna with Loading Gradient Directional Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This article proposes a high gain antenna with loading gradient directional structure. Taking the planar printing Yagi antenna as an example, this directional structure changes the traditional single directional element to a symmetrical structure, improving the mutual coupling relationship between passive directional elements and driving elements. In addition, the symmetrical directional element is changed to a gradient form, which can improve the gain of the antenna over a wider bandwidth by fixing the relative position relationship between the directional element and the radiating element. In this article, the gain of the original antenna was increased by more than 3dB through three sets of gradient directional element.

articleTitle: A 3D Non-Stationary Geometry-Based mmWave Channel Model for RIS-Assisted MIMO Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A three-dimensional non-stationary intelligent reflecting surface (RIS)-assisted multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channel model is proposed. The model takes into account both the movement of the scatterer in the propagation environment and the receiver. Three types of phase modulation for RIS are also considered, i.e., 1-bit, 2-bit and continuous quantization set, respectively. Based on the different phase modulation, we investigate the effect to the time-varying spatial cross-correlation function (CCF) and the time-varying temporal auto-correlation function (ACF). The numerical results provided verify the rationality and validity of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Dual-Channel Millimeter-Wave Transmistarray for Non-Diffracting Bessel Beam Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-channel transmistarray for generating Bessel beams is introduced. The traditional orbital angular momentum (OAM) beam has the problem of beam divergence, which seriously affects its application in wireless communication systems. In this design, dual-channel multiplexing can be realized by recording the phase information of different modes of two OAM mode on an array at the same time. Then the correlation term of axicon angle of Bessel beam is introduced into the phase compensation information to suppress the divergence angle of OAM beam. Compared with the traditional OAM beam, the non-diffraction distance is longer and the electric field intensity is more concentrated. The simulation results show that the maximum non-diffraction distance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l=\pm 1$</tex> mode is 800 mm (about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$73\lambda_{0}$</tex>), and the mode purity is over 97%. The designed antenna has excellent performance and is expected to play an important role in communication system.

articleTitle: A Compact Circularly Polarized Antenna Based on Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper designs a circularly polarized antenna based on metasurface for internet of things (IOT) applications. The proposed antenna includes two parts, a 4x4-unit mushroom metasurface plane, and cross-shaped slot feeding structure. The metasurface is designed by adjusting the dispersion curve of a unit cell. According the composite right/left hand transmission line (CRLH-TL ) theory, negative 1st order mode is expected in the metasurface. The corss-shaped slot on the defected ground is coupled by a meander microwave line. Thus, the metasurface is excited the -1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> mode at 2.5 GHz with left hand circular polarization. The whole dimension of the antenna is (45×45×3.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) at 2.5 GHz, and the simulated -10 dB impedance bandwidth is from 2.16 GHz to 2.8 GHz with 25.6% fractional bandwidth. The maximum realized gain is 4.1 dBic and it has a broad side radiation pattern. This compact circular polarization antenna is a competitive candidate for IOT applications.

articleTitle: Rapid Design of Linear-to-Circular Polarization Conversion Metasurfaces Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on deep learning, this study proposes a rapid design method of line-to-circular (LTC) polarization conversion metasurface (PCM) using ellipticity angle and pixelated metasurfaces. In this study, the ellipticity angle is used to characterize the LTC polarization conversion performance and the grouped-trained multi-convolutional neural network combination models is utilized for the rapid design. In the frequency range from 6 GHz to 14 GHz, the rapid designs of the narrowband LTC PCM are executed, which indicates the diversity of the designed metasurfaces, validating the effectiveness of the rapid design method.

articleTitle: A Multiband Fusion ISAR Imaging Method Based on Signal Compensation Model for Compact Range Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A multiband echo fusion imaging method based on signal mismatch compensation model is proposed for ISAR imaging in compact range broadband measurement. Based on scattering center echo model, considering the variation of RF systems and antennas under multiple measurements, the echo signal mismatch model is proposed. Different from the remote sensing coherent compensation methods, which require parametric estimation of scattering centers, in this paper, the linear relationship between echo phase spectrum of single scattering center and frequency is used to estimate phase compensation parameters by the linear least square method. The multiband echo compensation and fusion imaging process is also provided. The fusion imaging results of scattering data measured in compact range anechoic chamber indicate that, compared with sub-band images, the resolution of multiband image has been effectively improved by the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Novel Spectrum Prediction Algorithm Based on Multi-Granularity Fuzzy Cognitive Map
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Predicting electromagnetic spectrum data helps identify patterns of electromagnetic data changes and guides spectrum management. Current forecasting methods struggle to balance accuracy and interpretability. Therefore, this paper introduces a multi-granularity fuzzy cognitive map (MGFCM) model for multi-step forecasting based on the multi-granularity concept. The model incorporates two levels of granularity. At the fine granularity, the trend components of the data are extracted. At the coarse granularity, a fuzzy cognitive map is constructed to explore the time-varying patterns of electromagnetic data. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves higher prediction accuracy compared to widely used models such as ARIMA, LSTM, and RNN.

articleTitle: Global Ionospheric Tomography Using Virtual Station Multi-Source Observation Fusion Based on Machine Learning Method
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Effective space weather monitoring, exploration endeavors, and radio signal applications rely on precise global ionospheric electron density modeling. In this study, we developed a novel three-dimensional computerized ionospheric tomography model. This model employs machine learning techniques to create virtual stations, enabling the integration of multi-source observations for tomography modeling. To enhance the utilization of real observational data and increase the accuracy of virtual observations, we implemented the virtual observations in each candidate area using a machine learning ensemble algorithm, specifically Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). We validated the tomography model with added virtual station data using observations from 100 GPS stations globally. The results indicate that incorporating virtual observations improved the accuracy of the independent reference station's differential slant total electron content (dSTEC) by approximately 0.45 TECU compared to previous tomography results. This method offers the potential to overcome challenges in global tomography modeling.

articleTitle: Ku-Band Dual-Circularly Polarized Phased Array Based on Short-Circuit Transmission Line Coupler
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A dual-circularly polarized (CP) phased array is presented for Ku-band satellite communication applications. The 3-branch coupler excites dual-linearly polarized dipole radiations to achieve left-hand and right-hand circular polarizations. The three-stage short-circuit transmission line is meticulously designed to meet the amplitude and phase requirements of the coupler in the Ku-band. The proposed dualCP antenna element exhibits a simulated -15 dB impedance bandwidth of 40% and port isolation below -13 dB from 10.7GHz to 14.5GHz. For the 2 × 8 array, the axial ratio in the ±60° beam scanning range is better than 4.9 dB. Gain drops less than 5.9 dB over the entire bandwidth.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Backscattering from Radar Antenna Footprint Confined Infinite Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This work studies the electromagnetic (EM) backscattering from an infinite surface whose illuminated area is confined by radar antenna footprint, which represents the cases for calculation and measurement of radar clutter from land and sea. We highlight the fact in such cases that the illuminated area depends on the radar antenna footprint, thus always belonging to a near-field problem. The analytical expression for the radar cross section (RCS) of antenna footprint confined infinite plate at normal incidence is derived, with the radar distance-variant characteristics being explained in terms of two interfering scattering centers. Using Kirchhoff approximation (KA) and small perturbation method (SPM), the near-field backscattering from rough sea surfaces is also studied, where both spherical wavefront and antenna pattern tapering are considered. Numerical simulation results demonstrate that radar range and antenna pattern do impact on the calculated RCS and backscattering coefficient for both smooth and rough surfaces.

articleTitle: Initial Structure Solution for Nonparametric Modeling of Waveguide Devices Based on Time Reversal Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The core of modeling microwave devices is to find a better initial structure for it, while nonparametric modeling provides greater design freedom; for this reason, this paper presents a method for finding a physical guidance-based initial structure for non-parametric modeling in microwave waveguide devices. This method involves obtaining the equivalent source inside the waveguide device through a single time reversal (TR) operation. It is avoided that starting from a random or unguided initial structure may hinder the iterative convergence. Furthermore, the internal structure of the waveguide device is obtained through equivalent sources. This article uses TR operation to design two internal structures for a 90° bent waveguide and a bent waveguide power divider operating at 3 GHz, each with a size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\lambda\times 1\lambda$</tex>. This initial structure has excellent electromagnetic properties.

articleTitle: Design of Robust Beamforming Algorithm for Intelligent Reflecting Surface-Assisted MISO Backscatter Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a multivariable coupled achievable rate maximization problem in an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) assisted multiple input single output (MISO) backscatter communication (BackCom) system based on bounded channel state information model by considering the backscatter device circuit initiation, base station transmit power and IRS phase shift constraints. The solution is obtained by relaxing variables, using S-procedure, alternating optimization and semidefinite relaxation. Moreover, a robust joint optimization algorithm (RJOA) is proposed. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm performs higher average achievable rate and stronger robustness compared with non-robust and random IRS phase shift schemes.

articleTitle: Effects of Atmospheric Turbulence on Atmospheric Refraction
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper focuses on solving the corrections required for small-scale effects in radio systems. By analyzing the essential characteristics of neutral atmospheric turbulence in detail, it reveals how it causes irregular fluctuations in atmospheric refractive index. This fluctuation has a significant impact on the propagation path of radio waves, which restricts the accuracy of the radio external measurement system. We first theoretically expounded the basic principles and characteristics of atmospheric turbulence, and with the help of meteorological sounding data in Qingdao area, we deeply explored the specific properties of atmospheric turbulence in this area, and studied the influence of turbulence on atmospheric refraction error.

articleTitle: Solving Broadband Scattering Problems by the Krylov Subspace Basis Function Method
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient numerical method for evaluating broadband scattering characteristics. The method is based on Krylov subspace basis functions (KSBFs) derived at the highest frequencies in the range of interest, which once generated also capture the electromagnetic characteristics at lower frequencies, these basis functions will be referred to as ultra-wideband Krylov subspace basis functions, which can be used to solve the scattering problem at any frequency point in the bandwidth without having to regenerate the KSBFs. Corresponding numerical results verify the accuracy and time efficiency of this approach.

articleTitle: High Gain Microstrip Array Antenna for 60 GHz Millimeter Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A microstrip array antenna with high gain, low sidelobe, narrow beam width and easy integration is designed to realize high precision target location in millimeter wave radar system. The array feeding network is designed by series parallel hybrid feeding method. The Chebyshev synthesis method is used to realize the in-phase non-constant amplitude feeding of the array elements, which can effectively suppress the sidelobe level of the antenna while maintaining high antenna gain. The results show that the center frequency of the array is 60 GHz, the bandwidth is 1.96 GHz, and the gain is 21.9 dB. The half-power beam width on the H-plane is less than 11°, and the sidelobe suppression is -21.56 dB. The half-power beamwidth on the E-plane is less than 17° and the sidelobe suppression is -20.4 dB.

articleTitle: Dynamic Tuning of Electromagnetic Properties in Active Metamaterials via Variable Capacitance
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for tuning the electromagnetic properties of active metamaterials through variable capacitance. By integrating active devices with adjustable capacitance into the metamaterial structure, dynamic control of the transmission is demonstrated. Simulation results indicate that varying the capacitance significantly affects the effective dielectric constant of the metamaterial. This tunability allows for real-time manipulation of electromagnetic wave propagation, enabling potential applications in adaptive electromagnetic systems. The findings underscore the potential of capacitance-controlled active metamaterials in achieving versatile and reconfigurable electromagnetic responses.

articleTitle: Computational Electromagnetic Software Design Based on Qt and OpenGL
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Accompanied by the popularity of computers, numerical calculation methods are also promoted as the main electromagnetic analysis methods because of their concise and effective characteristics. Among them, the finite-difference time-domain method (FDTD) has become one of the main stream numerical calculation methods in electromagnetism due to its simplicity and ease of implementation. Making the FDTD algorithm into software can make this powerful numerical calculation tool more popular and easy to use, and software interface design is a crucial part of the software development process. Good interface design can help users quickly find the functions, reduce errors and improve efficiency. To address all the needs, this article gives a Qt and OpenGL based interface design approach applicable to parallel FDTD algorithms. Through this interface, users can realize many functions such as function selection, parameter setting and result display. It is easy to expand, and has certain advantages in cross-platform transplantation, which is conducive to the application and promotion of localised professional electromagnetic simulation software in engineering.

articleTitle: Shielding Effectiveness Experimental and Performance Analysis of Hybrid Shielding Structures for Building Walls
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Qi Tai 110m radio Telescope (QTT) is a fully steerable single-dish radio telescope with an observing frequency coverage from 150 MHz to 115 GHz. The QTT will play an important role for fundamental research fields of radio astronomy, such as pulsars, molecular spectral lines, active galactic nuclei, and VLBI observations [1]–[2]. In response to the EMI (Electromagnetic Interference) coming from electronic equipment in buildings, we would like to shield the whole buildings with a hybrid shielding structure combining building walls and mesh layers. To verify the performance of the shielding structures, we conducted on three types of shielding walls (red brick, porous brick, and bubble brick) experiment and SE (Shielding Effectiveness) measurements. The testing results indicate that the SE of all three types of shielding walls can achieve 55 dB in 0.1-1GHz and 45 dB over 1 to 18 GHz respectively, which show that the performance of the hybrid shielding structure is perfect that can be employed in the buildings.

articleTitle: Inverse Design of Silicon-Based Interlayer Coupling Structures Based on Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: For the first time, we utilize artificial neural networks to achieve the inverse design of silicon-based interlayer coupling structures. By implementing data preprocessing and migration learning methods, we significantly enhance the accuracy of the neural network. This study demonstrates the practicality of this approach for the effective inverse design of silicon-based interlayer coupling structures.

articleTitle: ELF Transfer Functions for a HED Source Propagating to an Underwater Receiver
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Extremely low frequency radio waves are widely used for communication with underwater receivers because waves in this band can propagate with low loss in the earthionosphere waveguide and penetrate deep into seawater. In this paper, two transfer functions are presented to study the frequency response characteristics of the channel in this band. One is from a horizontal electric dipole source to the upper sea surface, and the other is from the upper sea surface to an underwater receiver. These studies are beneficial for designing communication systems.

articleTitle: Channel Estimation via Joint Angle-Delay Sparse Structure in ISAC Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In the upcoming 6G communications, radar sensing will merge with communication to support diverse application scenarios. However, within complex Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) channels, radar targets and communication scatterers may overlap. Sensing and communication channels can exhibit similar sparse distributions in both the angle and delay domains. The increasing adoption of channel sparsity in communication parameter estimation has led to the development of numerous Compressed Sensing (CS) algorithms, many of which are based on the Expectation Maximization (EM) method. However, most EM-based algorithms depend on specific scenarios for designing channel sparse structures. Therefore, there is a pressing need to develop suitable channel sparse structures and tailor CS algorithms specifically for ISAC scenarios. This paper addresses the multiple-input multiple-output ISAC channel estimation issue using a bi-static model. We propose a Joint Angle-Delay Sparse Structure (JADSS) to capture the sparse characteristics of ISAC channels in both angle and delay domains. Additionally, we devise a message passing estimator to estimate the ISAC channel. Simulation demonstrate that the proposed CS algorithm achieves competitive error performance.

articleTitle: Fine-Grained Vehicle Target Recognition in SAR Images Integrating RCS Distribution Feature
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Although the MSTAR dataset under Standard Operating Conditions (SOC) has achieved high accuracy in the recognition of vehicle targets in SAR images, the performance remains insufficient for more refined recognition under Extended Operating Conditions (EOC). The primary reasons for this shortfall are as follows: first, the subdivision of unified vehicle categories into fine-grained subcategories significantly reduces inter-class differences, often manifesting in the detailed features of specific vehicle components; second, most neural network algorithms used for vehicle recognition lack the capability to effectively extract and distinguish features between similar categories. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel network integrating Radar Cross Section (RCS) distribution feature, which can assist in capturing subtle differences at the vehicle component level, thereby enhancing target's ability to focus on the structural information. Furthermore, the Cross Attention module employed in the network can effectively model the relationships between the abstract feature extracted from the original image and the RCS distribution feature over long distances. This module further enhances the capability to capture and focus on complementary information from both features, leading to improved feature representation and better discrimination of fine-grained differences. Finally, the proposed method was evaluated on the MSTAR dataset under EOC, resulting an improvement of 1.62% in recognition accuracy. achieving the best performance compared to other methods, which effectively validated its superiority in fine-grained recognition.

articleTitle: K-GCRNN: A Kolmogorov-Arnold Approach for Multi-Band Spectral Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: As the global proliferation of wireless devices intensifies, the availability of spectrum resources is increasingly constrained. Consequently, developing predictive methods based on spectrum resource management is crucial. In this paper, we propose a new model to predict the spectrum. This model processes spectral data by utilizing Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) and Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs). In addition, the model is processed with a Kolmogorov-Arnold network(KAN) after the output of each time step, which enhances the adaptability to environments with complex spatio-temporal dynamics. Experiments show that this comprehensive approach not only enhances prediction accuracy but also expands the model's capacity to address complex data issues.

articleTitle: Design and Characterization of a Radio-Frequency Switch Based on GeTe Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This work presents an innovative radio-frequency (RF) phase-change switch utilizing GeTe material, distinguished by flexibility, efficiency, scalability, miniaturization, and security. Following optimization of parameters, the switch exhibits a shallow insertion loss of -0.66dB in the on-state and an impressive isolation of -14dB in the off-state at 100GHz, representing a substantial performance improvement over conventional RF switches. The switch's compact size enhances its suitability for integration and packaging, rendering it indispensable in contemporary applications.

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Decoupling Method of E-Plane-Coupled Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: RPD E-plane-coupled patch antennas are presented in this article with radiation pattern decoupling (RPD) characteristics. Two patch elements are placed side by side, forming a whole patch radiator. To decouple the patch antennas, TM20 and TM30 modes are excited simultaneously, and their resonant frequencies are merged together by L-shaped slots and metallic vias. The L-shaped slots can not only adjust the resonant frequencies of the TM20 and TM30 modes, they also provide slot mode. The metallic vias are placed in the interface of patches to tune that of the TM20 mode. To verify the presented idea, a prototype is designed, fabricated, and measured for 2.4-GHz WLAN band. Good agreement can be observed between the measured and simulated results. The measured overlapping 10-dB impedance bandwidth is 6.9% (2.35-2.52 GHz), with a port isolation level of higher than 20 dB. Undistorted and symmetrical radiation patterns can be highlighted, showing good RPD effect.

articleTitle: Validation of a Real-Time MUF Forecast Model in HF Communication Based on Real-Time Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Accurately forecasting the available frequency of a link is a prerequisite for high-frequency communication. To enhance the accuracy of the maximum usable frequency (MUF) forecast, this paper presents a real-time MUF forecasting model (SPM) comprising four key processes: 1) inverting the ionospheric critical frequency (foF2) from the maximum observed frequency (MOF) using ray theory; 2) forecasting foF2 with a geometrically weighted algorithm; 3) reconstructing foF2 using the Kriging method based on geomagnetic coordinates; and 4) performing real-time MUF forecasting using the Lockwood model. A test link was established to compare the performance of the SPM model with the Voice of America Coverage Analysis Program (VOACAP) and the Long-term Prediction Model (LPM) corrected by ITU-R P.533. The results demonstrate that, compared to VOACAP and LPM, the SPM model reduces the RMSE by 1.31 MHz and 0.77 MHz, respectively, with RRMSE values of 30.45%, 24.69%, and 15.53% for the three models. These findings highlight the advantages of applying the SPM model to real-world links and offer valuable insights for engineering applications.

articleTitle: An Efficient Higher-Order Parallel MLFMA with Hybrid Singularity Cancellation Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Applying higher-order technologies to method of moments (MoM) and multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) will commonly encounter the crisis of singularity cancellation. To obtain satisfactory accuracy and computational efficiency, parallel MLFMA based on surface integral equations (SIEs) together with a hybrid singularity cancellation strategy (HSCS) is presented in this paper. For electric field integral equation (EFIE) singularities and near singularities, an improved Duffy's transform is employed; while for magnetic field integral equation (MFIE) singularities, nonoverlapping integration rules for source and field elements are adopted to calculate the principle value term. Performance of this proposed approach is demonstrated via preliminary numerical results.

articleTitle: Target Recognition Through Time-Domain Scattering Echo based on CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, based on the shooting and bouncing ray (SBR) method to obtain a large number of target time-do main scattering echo data, an electrically large-size target echo dataset is produced, and two kinds of tank targets are recognized by using the convolutional neural network (CNN) model.
