The results show that compared with the target recognition using optical images, the target recognition by timedomain electromagnetic scattering data is better, and the minimum recognition accuracy of CNN for similar targets is above 95%.

articleTitle: Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar Imaging Method for Convolutional Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In recent years, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) has been used in Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR) due to its excellent feature extraction ability and data representation. However, standard CNNs treat all features equally, ignoring the importance of highlighting critical information and suppressing non-essential information, which often leads to limitations in imaging performance. In order to overcome this challenge, an ISAR imaging strategy integrating the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) mechanism has emerged. In this method, the convolutional attention module is embedded in the network architecture to deeply mine the details of features in the channel and spatial dimensions and enhance the representation ability of the network. In addition, it mitigates the effects of noise in the original feature in the residual connection, improving image clarity. The results show that the imaging technique using convolutional attention can generate high-resolution ISAR images, and its imaging performance is better than that of traditional fully convolutional neural network methods.

articleTitle: A Two-Channel Amplitude and Phase Consistency Calibration Algorithm for in-Situ Measurement System of Electromagnetic Radiation Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Due to the presence of various unpredictable and uncontrollable factors in the actual application of electromagnetic radiation characteristic in-situ measurement systems, the signals acquired by double channels are often inconsistent in amplitude and phase. To mitigate or eliminate the detrimental effects of these issues on the outcomes of the system and to enhance the anti-interference ability of the system, this paper has undertaken research into the calibration and compensation algorithms for dual-channel time-domain signal amplitude and phase, and has been proposed a calibration algorithm to search the minimum phase difference and achieve average amplitude compensation. This algorithm demonstrates lower errors in amplitude and phase calibration compared to the algorithms based on the minimum gradient descent method and ridge regression models, thereby facilitating the extraction of the electromagnetic radiation characteristics of valuable signals.

articleTitle: Conformal Metamaterial Isolator for 1.5T MRI System*
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The combined use of surface coils and metamaterials significantly improved magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) performance, providing an important advantage for the flexibility of 1.5T local imaging systems. However, coupling between components affected the future development of clinical MRI, resulting in reduced magnetic field enhancement and impaired contrast resolution. In this paper, we propose an isolator with a double-sided metal pattern that utilizes an omnidirectional polarization conversion mechanism to effectively eliminate the coupling between metamaterial and surface coil. This research paves a promising path for the practical application of portable metamaterials in MRI.

articleTitle: Dual Polarised Ultra Wideband High Isolation Vivaldi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband (UWB) dual-polarised Vivaldi antenna is designed. Firstly, a resistor is loaded on the conventional antenna to enhance the bandwidth of the antenna, and secondly, two Vivaldi antennas with the same amplitude are placed vertically across to form two mutually perpendicular polarisation components. The antenna operates with a bandwidth of 12:1 (1–12 GHz), at which the isolation between the two antennas is -33 dB, and the cross-polarisation level is about 30 dB. The transverse electrical dimension of the antenna is only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.14\lambda_{L}(\lambda_{L}$</tex> is the wavelength of the lowest operating frequency). The proposed antenna can be applied to UWB communication systems.

articleTitle: A Fast Analysis Method for Bistatic Broadband Electromagnetic Scattering Problems Based on Subdomain Method of Moments and Asymptotic Waveform Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A fast frequency sweeping algorithm based on subdomain method of moment (SMoM) and Asymptotic Waveform Estimation (AWE) is proposed to solve the bistatic broadband electromagnetic scattering problem of complex multiscale targets. In the proposed approach, the target is divided into several subdomains which are easy to solve according to the geometric characteristics. Firstly, the initial surface current of each subdomain is solved by MoM and the initial Taylor expansion coefficient of the surface current is solved by traditional AWE. Then, the boundary conditions on the interfaces between adjacent subdomains require to be enforced to ensure the current continuity. Next, the excitation vector is updated and the new expansion coefficient is solved until the error of the old and new expansion coefficient meets the convergence condition. Finally, the Taylor series is transformed into rational function by Pade approximation to obtain the broadband scattering characteristics of the target.

articleTitle: Comparison of PINN-SAMI3 and 4D-Var Data Assimilation Methods for Ionospheric Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Purely data-driven ionospheric modeling inadequately adheres to fundamental physical laws. PINN-SAMI3 [1], as a novel data assimilation framework, integrates the control equations of the fully physical model SAMI3 with neural networks to construct a physics-informed ionospheric parameter inversion framework. This paper compares PINN-SAMI3 with traditional data assimilation methods EKF [2] and 4D-Var. The test results indicate that PINN-SAMI3 outperforms EKF but has lower accuracy than the 4D-Var method. This framework has important implications for the future construction of a hybrid model of space weather prediction that integrates physical models and neural networks.

articleTitle: AB-YOLO: A Novel Deep Learning Approach for Accurate and Efficient SAR Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce an innovative Synthetic Aperture Radar target detection approach that mitigates the impact of noise on radar detection by leveraging an AB-YOLO algorithm. The proposed method integrates an adaptive kernel convolution module, AKconv, which dynamically adjusts sampling shapes to effectively capture features of diverse forms and locations. This is followed by a dual-layer routing attention mechanism that enhances dynamic sparse attention, filtering irrelevant key-value pairs at a coarse level and preserving only the most pertinent routing areas to reduce redundancy. We further apply a Token-to-Token attention mechanism within these joint routing areas, linearly mapping feature maps and utilizing deep convolutional computation with the most relevant token regions as keys to bolster local feature extraction. The resultant local features of varying scales are sampled, fused, and mapped to generate detection outcomes. Extensive experimental validation on the SAR-AIRcraft-1.0 dataset confirms the superior detection capabilities of our proposed method, showcasing its robustness and precision in noisy conditions.

articleTitle: A Method for High-Precision Direction Finding of a Satellite Navigation Interference Source Using the UAV
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Satellite navigation signals are easily susceptible to various intentional or unintentional interference. The Unmanned Aerial Vehicle(UAV), with its convenience and lift-off advantages can effectively compensate for the drawbacks of traditional satellite navigation interference source detection, which has low efficiency and high difficulty, reducing time and manpower costs. However, because the UAV is susceptible to the influence of wind and its own flight control in the air, even in a hovering state, it cannot remain completely still. The UAV will experience irregular minor vibrations, leading to poor accuracy and slow convergence of satellite navigation interference source direction finding. Based on the real-time direction finding algorithm, this study proposes a high-precision direction finding method for satellite navigation interference sources on unmanned aerial vehicles, with linear interpolation of electronic compass and multistage adaptive filtering. The results show that the proposed method can effectively solve the problem of poor directional accuracy and slow convergence of direction finding results for UAVs in non-stationary states in the air, and greatly enhancing the efficiency of identifying satellite navigation interference sources for UAVs.

articleTitle: Graphene based Ris for thz Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Recent research endeavors have been dedicated to innovative wireless hardware designs and connection concepts aimed at fulfilling the ambitious objectives of 6th Generation (6G) wireless communications. The inclusion of Terahertz (THz) technology in modern infrastructure holds immense potential for shaping 6G networks, offering amplified throughput, extended coverage, heightened security, and improved positioning while reducing power consumption. The demand for efficient control over THz waves has grown alongside the advancements in wireless domain. Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) have garnered a lot of attention as a means of regulating electromagnetic waves. In this study, we investigate the utilization of a RIS employing graphene-based materials to control THz waves, with a specific focus on enhancing reflection performance and enabling beam steering. Our proposed RIS design entails a periodic array of graphene stacked over a grounded substrate.

articleTitle: Design of a New Dual Polarized Waveguide Slot Antenna Array with High Polarization Purity
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel dual-polarized waveguide slot array antenna. The horizontal polarization antenna employs waveguide narrow-edge slots as the antenna array, while the vertical polarization antenna utilizes open-end waveguide structures slot antenna arrays loaded with double short-circuit blocks, These two forms of waveguide structures are arranged in an alternating pattern on the array surface, contributing to a reduction in antenna profile. These two antenna arraying approaches effectively suppress cross-polarization to a certain extent, with the cross-polarization level reaching approximately -71 dB, and the antenna demonstrates high polarization purity. Additionally, the antenna adopts the Taylor distribution for weighting, attaining the characteristics of high gain and low sidelobe. The designed antenna acquires a gain of 29.3 dBi in the horizontal polarization form, with a sidelobe of -26.1 dB, a gain of 29.7 dBi in the vertical polarization form, a sidelobe of -24.5 dB, and both null depths reach below -30 dB, which holds extensive application prospects in radar and communication systems.

articleTitle: A Symmetry Treatment in Cylindrical Explicit and Unconditionally Stable FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A symmetry treatment in cylindrical explicit and unconditionally stable FDTD (CEUS-FDTD) method is given. The system matrix of CEUS-FDTD method is unsymmetric, which will render instability since the explicit central–difference scheme is used for temporal discretization. By splitting the grid matrix reasonably and modifying the corresponding coefficients, the system matrix is transformed into a new symmetric matrix compulsively. Then an additional diagonal matrix will be obtained naturally on the other side of the equation to ensure that the time marching equation still holds. At last, unstable modes could be obtained by solving generalized eigenvalue problem of the new symmetric system matrix with respect to the diagonal matrix. Numerical results illustrates that the stability of CEUS-FDTD could be ensured and the accuracy would not be affected.

articleTitle: A Flexible Low-Pass Filter Based on CPW-SSPPs
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a flexible low-pass filter structured with only a single metal layer of CPW-SSPPs on a polyimide film substrate. Spoof surface plasmon polaritons are realized by carving periodic rectangular grooves on both sides of the CPW ground. The flexible low-pass filters in two states, flat and bent, are designed and simulated. The simulation results show that the designed flexible CPW-SSPPs low-pass filter have very sharp transition band and good stopband performance. The proposed flexible low-pass filter has a very low insertion loss of less than 1.93 dB under 5.2 GHz in the unbending state, and the out-of-band rejection is higher than 30 dB in the frequency range of 5.82–12 GHz, and compared with the flat state, the change of the S-parameters is very small in the bending state, and the designed flexible CPW-SSPPs low-pass filter can be applied in the bending state.

articleTitle: Multilayered Resonator Enhanced Rydberg Atomic Receiver for HF Band Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: We demonstrated a new scheme of Rydberg atomic receiver tailored for high frequency (HF) band sensing with a deep-subwavelength resonator. The proposed multilayered split-ring resonator (MSRR) is constructed in a five-layered printed circuit board, providing significantly enhanced electric filed to greatly boost the sensitivity of the atomic receiver. In the measurement, we characterize the relationship between the AC-stark shift and input power. Furthermore, the sensitivity of the whole system is presented by utilizing off-resonant Rydberg atomic heterodyne technique. With the MSRR, the sensitivity can reach 4.3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{V}/\text{cm}\sqrt{\mathrm{H}\mathrm{z}}$</tex>, whereas it is only 240.8 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[\mu\mathrm{V}/\text{cm}\sqrt{\mathrm{H}\mathrm{z}}$</tex> without the MSRR. The measured results affirm the substantial sensitivity enhancement achieved by MSRR.

articleTitle: Research on Temporal and Spatial Characteristics of 50/60Hz Electromagnetic Background Based on CSES Satellite Observation
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Power Line Emission (PLE) generated by ground power systems has been receiving close attention in recent years. To enhance the precision in identifying and researching the PLE phenomenon in the topside ionosphere, the investigation of the electromagnetic background without PLE is necessary. The Extremely Low Frequency (ELF) electric field data of the China Seismo-Electromagnetic Satellite (CSES) during the three years (2019–2021) have been used to study the background at 50/60Hz. A statistical study was conducted on the differences in the impact of geomagnetic activity and lightning on the background in different regions and at different times. By analyzing the temporal and spatial distribution characteristics of the background, it is found that the geomagnetic activity may not affect the 50/60Hz electromagnetic background in the top ionosphere. The seasonal changes in areas with high lightning occurrence are very obvious at night, while in areas with less lightning, there is almost no seasonal change. Therefore, it is believed that the 50/60Hz electromagnetic background at night may be mainly affected by the proton whistler waves from lightning activities.

articleTitle: A Grid Mapping Algorithm Utilizing Limited Bandwidth Millimeter-Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a grid map construction algorithm that utilizes limited bandwidth millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar to achieve high-precision environmental perception and mapping. We first employ mmWave radar to capture environmental data. By configuring the radar bandwidth, the radar's resolution is leveraged to update the grid map. Combining the Bresenham algorithm, we have achieved rapid and accurate modeling of the environment, resulting in the final grid map construction outcome. Subsequently, the angle of arrival (AOA) distribution in the environment is statistically analyzed and fitted, demonstrating the proposed method's effectiveness. Finally, a comparison with a baseline map reconstructed using LiDAR is performed. The algorithm's perception and reconstruction capabilities are evaluated using root mean square error (RMSE), Jaccard similarity, and code execution time.

articleTitle: Measurement of Millimeter Wave Transmission Characteristics Based on Battlefield Smoke Interference Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In response to the impact of copper powder and smoke interference on millimeter wave transmission characteristics, four band tests were conducted using the same smoke agent equivalent battlefield interference environment, including K-band (24GHz), Ka band (34.5GHz), V-band (61GHz), and F-band (94GHz), to obtain millimeter wave radar echoes and analyze them. The experimental results indicate that: The interference of smoke on millimeter wave transmission has randomness, and as the concentration of smoke increases, the interference ability will gradually become stronger; As the carrier frequency increases, the wavelength gradually shortens and the anti-interference ability gradually improves; Relatively speaking, the interference ability of copper powder on millimeter wave transmission is stronger than that of fine smoke aerosols, but far inferior to that of foil cloud clusters.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Pulse Coupling Characteristics of Key Aircraft Components
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Electromagnetic pulse (EMP) poses a significant threat to aircraft. Understanding the coupling characteristics between EMP and aircraft is crucial for designing protective measures. This paper analyzes the characteristics of EMP in both time and frequency domains and explores their interaction mechanisms with aircraft. A testing method is proposed using a mobile EMP simulator to irradiate key components of the aircraft directionally. Experiments were conducted on a test aircraft, and the results indicate the following: 1)The maximum difference in time-domain shielding effectiveness is 3.3 dB under different irradiation peak values and polarization modes, suggesting that shielding effectiveness is largely independent of EMP irradiation intensity and polarization. 2)Aircraft materials perform better at shielding EMP below a certain frequency. 3)There is no significant positive correlation between the peak induced current in cables and EMP irradiation intensity. Specifically, under horizontal polarization, the peak induced current in cables is significantly lower than under vertical polarization. Additionally, under the same polarization conditions, the peak induced current in System 1 cables is higher than in System 2 cables. 4)The frequency spectrum of induced current in System 1 cables shows two significant peaks, while System 2 cables exhibit repeated oscillations with stable peaks at four specific frequencies. 5) The voltage waveform coupled by a certain system's antenna consistently shows a rising edge and overall damped oscillation with rapid attenuation, with energy concentrated in specific frequency bands. These findings aid in assessing aircraft EMP protection capabilities and provide crucial data for the electromagnetic protection design of aircraft.

articleTitle: Effect of Rough Sea Surface on Electromagnetic Wave Propagation in Evaporation Duct Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Atmospheric duct is a unique condition at sea that enables over-the-horizon detection by radio equipment. However, the ocean waves caused by sea breezes on the ocean surface significantly diminish this effect. In this paper, the influence of a rough sea surface on the propagation of electromagnetic (EM) waves is analyzed using the parabolic equation (PE) model. The analysis considers the rough sea surface model with and without accounting for the wave shadowing effect. Firstly, the study employs the Shadowed model, which considers the effect of shadowing, along with the Ament model, which neglects the effect of shadowing. These models are used to analyze the impact of grazing angle and wind speed (WS) on the roughness reduction factor and the Fresnel reflection coefficient of smooth surfaces. Secondly, the measured meteorological gradient data obtained from a research vessel in the South China Sea are utilized to analyse the effects of smooth sea surface and two types of rough sea surface on the one-way propagation loss under different WS conditions. The results show that as the WS increases, the influence of a rough sea surface on EM wave propagation within the evaporation duct becomes more pronounced, which will cause higher propagation loss. The rough sea surface on the propagation loss up to an increase of nearly 27.39 dB compared to a smooth sea surface.

articleTitle: A method for simulating SAR images based on scattering of ray tracing
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This study uses a ray tracing method to simulate urban Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images. These images are based on 3D models of buildings, the ground, vegetation, and small scatterers, obtained using a scattering of ray tracing algorithm. The ray tracing algorithm calculates the scattering paths and the power received by the SAR sensor, generating SAR simulation images. The results show that, despite the limitations of the scattering algorithm, the simulated SAR images closely match the actual scenes. All features present in the real images are reproduced in the simulated images; the shapes of buildings and vegetation are particularly clear. However, differences do exist, and these are also discussed.

articleTitle: Microwave AoD Design on the TFE of an OLED Display for 5G and B5G Cellular Phones
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a leading and practical microwave (mcw) antenna-on-display (AoD) design on the thin-film encapsulation (TFE) of an organic light-emitting diode (OLED) display for cellular phones of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5^{\text{th}}$</tex> generation mobile communications (5G) and beyond 5G (B5G) so that popular licensed FR1 mcw bands n77 and n78 in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3^{\text{rd}}$</tex> generation partnership project (3GPP) can be supported for better user experience in wireless communications and stronger product competitiveness. Besides, due to the on-TFE design, numerous advantages, e.g., thinner display modules, lower manufacturing complexity and costs, higher compatibility with touch sensors, and higher visual performance, can be attained as well.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Vivaldi Antenna with Resistive Loading
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the requirements of antenna size and operating bandwidth for time-domain through-wall radar system, an ultra-wideband Vivaldi antenna with resistive loading is proposed. The traditional Vivaldi antenna is slotted to form a loop radiating structure, and resistive loading is applied to the loop to expand the lower limit of the operating frequency band. Multi-stage feedline matching is used to optimize the impedance matching of the antenna. Simulation results show that the antenna has a bandwidth of 0.4-6 GHz (S11 < -10 dB) and a maximum gain of 7 dB. The proposed antenna has lateral dimensions approximately 0.3 times the wavelength at the lowest operating frequency. This antenna features lightweight, low profile, and ultra-wideband, making it suitable for time-domain through-wall radar system.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Wideband Patch Antenna Array for RF Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A circularly polarized broadband patch array antenna is proposed in this paper. The stacked structure well extends the antenna bandwidth. A <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2^{\ast}2$</tex> antenna subarray is designed using sequential rotation feed technique and it is translated and expanded to get a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4^{\ast}4$</tex> antenna array. The paper also derives the phase excitation of the array antenna with rotation fed structure when the antenna beam scans at different angles. The simulation results show that the designed antenna has large gain and little axial ratio even at large scanning angles. The antenna shows good performance in large scanning angles and it can be applied in radio frequency communication.

articleTitle: Physics-Informed Neural Networks with Hard Constraints for Electromagnetic Scattering Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel approach to solving two-dimensional electromagnetic scattering problem using physical-informed neural networks (PINN) enhanced with hard constraints. The proposed method is implemented under the partial differential equations (PDEs) framework, which demonstrates superior accuracy over traditional PINN structure compared to conventional numerical methods.

articleTitle: A New Dual-Band Phase Shift Metasurface for Wide-Angle Scanning of a Dual-Band Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents an implementation of a dual-band wide-angle scanning antenna array based on a new dual-band phase shift metasurface (PGM). The PGM consists of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3^{\ast}12$</tex> metasurface elements. Each element is capable of independent phase shift between -200° and 50° at 3.5 GHz and 6 GHz while keeping high transmittance (the average transmission amplitude is over 80<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>). The PGM is loaded above a dual-band antenna array for enhancing the wide-angle scanning performance. It is shown that the scanning rang of the antenna array has be extended from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 43^{\circ}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 60^{\circ}$</tex> at 3.5 GHz and from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 47^{\circ}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 60^{\circ}$</tex> at 6 GHz.

articleTitle: An Observational Data-Driven Analysis Model for Atmospheric Refraction Effects in Radar Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: For ground-based radars, the troposphere and ionosphere are the main sources of measurement errors. Currently, with the increasing demands for target tracking in many engineering applications of radar systems, accurately assessing the impact of atmospheric refraction effects on radar systems has become increasingly important. Based on GNSS and meteorological observation data, we have developed an observational data-driven analysis model for atmospheric refraction effects in radar systems, this model can realistically reproduce the variation characteristics of radar systems at different locations and frequencies in the three dimensions of elevation angle, azimuth angle, and distance.

articleTitle: Research on Electromagnetic Scattering of Leafless Trees and Targets Based on High Frequency Scattering Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The shooting and bouncing rays (SBR) method is widely used in the calculation of composite electromagnetic (EM) scattering between electrically a large target and backgrounds. This paper focuses on the scene of leafless trees and a typical target in late winter. The SBR is used to calculate the composite scattering radar cross sections (RCS) of the target and the leafless trees. This paper establishes the composite EM scattering model of leafless multi-tree and target, and studies the influence of leafless trees on the target. The simulation results show that two leafless trees with a height of about 7m cannot make a good shielding effect on the target.

articleTitle: Influence of Natural Magnetic Field on the Propagation Characteristics of Different Modes of LF One-Hop Sky Waves in the Day-Night Transition Area
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The study of the propagation characteristics of low-frequency (LF) sky waves in the anisotropic Earth-ionosphere waveguide is of great value for the improvement of the accuracy of navigation and timing systems. In this paper, we focus on the one-hop sky-wave propagation characteristics in the day-night transition area in the anisotropic Earth-ionosphere waveguide under the influence of natural magnetic field. The finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is utilized to construct a day-night mixed field, and the propagation delay and field strength of a one-hop sky waves are obtained using the fast Fourier transform and inverse fast Fourier transform (FFT/IFFT) spectral-division technique. And the propagation characteristics in the models of day-to-night variation and night-to-day variation under different directions of the natural magnetic field are analyzed, respectively. The numerical results show that the magnetic field in the horizontal direction has the greatest effect on the wave propagation delay and field strength in the nighttime area of the day-to-night path and in the daytime area of the night-to-day path, compared with the magnetic field in the vertical direction and 45° direction.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Tunable Terahertz Metamaterials Absorber Based on Vanadium Dioxide
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A terahertz ultra-wideband absorption tunable metamaterial was designed. The ultra-wideband absorber was designed using vanadium dioxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), a phase change material, to dynamically adjust the absorption of the metamaterial by changing the conductivity of the VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. While the conductivity of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> increases from 200 S/m to 2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>S/m, the absorption rate can be adjusted between 3.1% and 100%.When the conductivity increases to 2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>S/m, the absorption bandwidth of the metamaterial reaches 5.12 THz, which has the effect of ultrawideband absorption, and the ultra-wideband absorption performance is significantly improved. Due to the quadruple rotational symmetry of the structural element, the absorption performance of the metamaterial is not sensitive to the polarization angle of the incident electromagnetic wave, and it has good incident angle stability.

articleTitle: Analysis of Wet Delay Error of 1km Measurement Path by Ground-based Microwave Radiometer Interval Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper analyzes the measurement deviation of the path wet delay of a target 500km high relative to the radar when the ground-based microwave radiometer is 1km away from the radar. Without considering the influence of equipment system error, this paper uses the historical sounding data of the Global Telecommunications System (GTS) from 2011 to 2021 as the data source to extract the historical sounding data of GTS in the South China Sea subtropical region. Taking the historical sounding data of January, April, July and October as the representative of the four seasons in the South China Sea subtropical region, the brightness temperatures corresponding to elevation angles of 15°, 30°, 45° and 60° were calculated. The brightness temperature calculated by the simulated sounding data of South China Sea subtropical region is taken as the observation value of the ground-based microwave radiometer, and the brightness temperature is brought into the Marco technology to obtain the oblique path wet delay observed by the ground-based microwave radiometer 1km away from the radar. Then, when the ground-based microwave radiometer is 1 km away from the radar, the measurement deviation of the wet delay of the oblique path caused by the detection target at a height of 500 km and different elevation angles is obtained. The simulation results are shown in the table below. The results show that in the South China Sea subtropical region, when the ground-based microwave radiometer is 1 km away from the radar and the detection target is 500 km high, the root mean square error of the wet delay deviation of the oblique path measured at the detection elevation angles of 30°, 45° and 60° are all sub-millimeters. The RMSE is of the order of millimeters in July at an elevation angle of 15°, and of the order of sub-millimeters in January, April and October. This measurement error is negligible when the measurement accuracy of the equipment is in the order of centimeters, and cannot be ignored when the measurement accuracy of the equipment is in the order of millimeters.

articleTitle: Doppler Signature Analysis and Separation of Mixed O/X-Mode in HF Hybrid Sky-Surface Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The High-frequency hybrid sky-surface wave radar (HSSWR) working with frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) has great potential for large-scale monitoring targets and ocean environment. HF signal propagating through the ionosphere split into the ordinary (O) and extraordinary (X) waves due to the influence of the geomagnetic field. In this paper, the computational formula of the Doppler signatures is derived in the case of a mixed O/X-mode signal model and analyze the results in Range-Doppler spectrum. It is shown that the Doppler components cannot be separated using matched filtering. The fractional Fourier transform (FRFT) for separating two O/X mode Doppler components is proposed according to the derived Doppler signature expression. The simulation results illustrate that the proposed scheme is an effective solution for O/X mode Doppler separation.

articleTitle: A Two-Port Dipole Antenna with Enhanced Isolation for Radiation Pattern Diversity Application Using Commonly Differentially Hybrid-Fed Method
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A two-port dipole antenna with enhanced isolation and radiation pattern diversity ability is designed. First, the first-and second-order modes are analyzed and manipulated to support radiation pattern diversity applications. Then the commonly differentially hybrid-fed (CDHF) architecture is investigated, showing the ability to realize high isolation and radiation pattern diversity. Finally, a two-port dipole antenna is designed utilizing the CDHF method. The isolation exceeds more than 35 dB in the total operating bands. Additionally, broadside and conical radiation patterns can be achieved when Port 1 and Port 2 are exited respectively.

articleTitle: Improved Coupled Markov Chain for Three-Dimensional Spatial Modelling of Inhomogeneous Evaporation Duct
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: As the atmospheric environment in different oceanic regions is inhomogeneous, this inhomogeneous property has an important impact on radar detection systems and mobile communication systems. However, for inhomogeneous evaporation duct data within the range of low altitude regions at sea are limited, the traditional Markov process is difficult to achieve accurate modelling of inhomogeneous evaporation duct in full space, and the traditional radar sea clutter inversion of inhomogeneous profiles is not able to achieve the inversion of inhomogeneous evaporation duct profiles in full space. Therefore, this paper firstly proposes an improved coupled Markov chain to achieve full-space modelling of inhomogeneous evaporation ducts. Tropospheric evaporation duct have different classes and corresponding spatial structural features. In this paper, we will provide a comprehensive introduction to evaporation duct in terms of their characteristics and classification, formation mechanism, etc., followed by an introduction to the parabolic equation model commonly used in the study of radio wave propagation problems. The experimental results show that our proposed improved coupled Markov chain takes into account the effect of the spatial transformation of the evaporation duct on the spatial modelling, can able to model the whole space based on the limited observations of the evaporation duct, and reduces the evaporation duct altitude errors by 1.5 m and 3.3 m compared to those of the two-dimensional Markov chain and linear interpolation methods.

articleTitle: Prediction of Ionospheric TEC Based on ESOA-BP Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The global total electron content (TEC) of the ionosphere is an important characteristic parameter of the ionosphere, and the realization of ionospheric TEC forecasts is of great value in space science research, as well as in engineering applications such as satellite navigation, ground-based radar, and SAR. This paper applies an improved BP based on Enhanced Seagull Optimization Algorithm (ESOA) to forecast global ionospheric total electron content (TEC) maps with up to 24 hr. The ESOA-BP model is trained and evaluated using Center for Orbit Determination in Europe (CODE) global TEC maps from 2018 to 2022. An analysis of the effectiveness of forecasting solar activity in high and low years, as well as during periods of geomagnetic storms, shows that the correlation coefficient from model TEC concerning the CODE TEC are 0.96 and 0.94 in low solar activity years and high solar activity years, and TEC forecast errors increase during the onset of magnetic storms compared to periods of no storm.

articleTitle: A 76-81 GHz Microstrip Comb-Line Array Antenna with High Sidelobe Suppression and Wide Beam for Automotive Radar Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband microstrip comb-line antenna array is presented for short-range automotive radar sensors. The impedance bandwidth of the antenna covers the whole commonly used frequency band of automotive radar sensors (76–81 GHz). The antenna is a 1×20 antenna array with a wide beamwidth and low sidelobe level. The antenna radiating elements are placed side-by-side, which results in the antenna being able to realize the effect of high gain. Simulation results show that the antenna has a 16% (68.6-81.5GHz) impedance bandwidth and a gain up to 14.5 dBi, half power beamwidth wider than 107°. It reach the lowest sidelobe level of -18.8 dB at 80 GHz.

articleTitle: Analysis on Power Transmission Efficiency in Quasi-Optical Reflector Antenna System in MM - Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The quasi-optical reflector antenna is widely applied in millimeter-wave radiometers, the leakage and thermal loss of which are important for the calibration accuracy. In this work, the authors investigates the power transmission efficiency of a typical quasi-optical reflector antenna. The analysis includes the power leakage due to the spill over at 89 GHz, and the ohm loss of reflector of specific polarization state at 54,89,118GHz. The overall results gives an intuitive sight of the quasi-optical antenna performance for radiometer applications.

articleTitle: An Optimized Method for Electromagnetic Inverse Scattering Imaging Based on GAN
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Electromagnetic Inverse scattering problem (ISP) is aimed at recontructing shapes or retrieving electromagnetic parameters of scatterers from the scattering fields. Synthetic aperture radar methods, such as Delay-and-Sum (DAS) or Delay-Multiply-and-Sum (DMAS) are often used to solve such problems. However, the imaging results are not satisfying usually. Forthermore, these methods are associated with heavy computational cost, and consequently, they are often time-consuming. In this paper, a deep learning method named pix2pix based on conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) is applied to enhance the quarlity of imaging and reduce the time cost. The simulation results show that the proposed method can provide a new solution for the difficult ISPs.

articleTitle: Ka-Band 3-dB Quadrature Hybrid on 75μm GaAs Substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A wideband 3-dB quadrature hybrid is designed based on the stacked microstrip coupled structure, allowing tighter coupling realizable on 75μm GaAs substrates. The proposed structure can be easily integrated with typical two-metal-layer and thin-substrate GaAs fabrication processes. The simulation result shows the designed hybrid able to operate at 25–55 GHz and provide good port symmetry

articleTitle: A Plane Wave Synthesis Method Based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper a genetic algorithm (GA) is proposed that can be used to optimally reduce the number of plane wave generator (PWG) sources after the number of sources has been reduced by nearly a quarter, and the performance of the generated plane waves can reach an amplitude fluctuation of 3 dB and a phase fluctuation of 10° in most of the regions. The methods are verified by computer simulation.

articleTitle: The Propagation Characteristics of Low-Frequency Electromagnetic Wave Cross Air-Sea
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Seawater has good electrical conductivity and electromagnetic wave attenuation greatly in seawater. The long-distance information transmission based on electromagnetic wave in seawater has always been a problem of concern to everyone. The cross air-sea lateral wave propagation mode can realize efficient long-range information transmission, but the spatial distribution of cross air-sea lateral wave field and the impedance characteristics of transmitting antenna are complex. Based on low-frequency Propagation theory, the characteristics of Lateral wave propagation and impedance of transmitting antenna are analyzed to provide theoretical support for the application of lateral wave in space.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal Prediction of Global Atmospheric Duct Height Across Latitudes Based on ERA5 Data
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Accurate prediction of global atmospheric duct heights is important for a variety of purposes, including communications, navigation, meteorological forecasting and the military. However, the global atmospheric duct height data is wide-ranging and costly for overall spatiotemporal prediction. In addition, the traditional convolutional neural network (CNN) and recurrent neural network (RNN) have some limitations and cannot extract spatial and temporal features efficiently at the same time. In this paper, an efficient spatiotemporal prediction network for global atmospheric duct heights combining 3D convolutional neural network and Transformer is proposed based on ERA5 reanalysis data. Considering the spatial heterogeneity of atmospheric duct distribution latitude, the global data are divided into three latitude regions of low, middle and high latitude for spatiotemporal prediction respectively, and the prediction results are fused to finally obtain the spatiotemporal prediction results of the global atmospheric duct height. The experimental results show that compared with the overall prediction method, the deep spatiotemporal prediction model with cross-latitude fusion proposed in this study has a significant improvement in speed and accuracy, and outperforms other existing networks.

articleTitle: Impact of Sparse Sampling on Multi-Beam Pattern Measurement of Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The multi-beam pattern of phased arrays can be efficiently measured by synthesizing element patterns retrieved in arrays. In this paper, the effect of sparse sampling and interpolation strategies on the multi-beam pattern measurement is further investigated in simulations. The reconstruction errors of multiple beams are examined in terms of beam peak and whole beam pattern for different samnling spacings.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Miniaturized Reconfigurable FSS Design with High Selectivity
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a kind of band-pass frequency selective surface(FSS) with improved out-of-band rejection is proposed by using interdigital capacitor cascade structure. The proposed band-pass reconfigurable FSS can be used for hybrid radome, and its filtering characteristics of “high transmittance in band and strong stealth out of band” will improve the communication performance of the antenna system. the simulation results show that the FSS in 2-2.5GHz transmittance is greater than 70%, X band suppression characteristic is greater than 10dB, reconstruction, Ku band and below, the suppression characteristic is greater than 10dB, realize in TE and TE wide Angle polarization wave incidence, low frequency passband and resistance band can be switchable at the same time, with high frequency ultra-wideband harmonic suppression effect.

articleTitle: A High-Gain Planar Electronically Beam Scanning Antenna in Ku-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Modern communication systems have a strong demand for antennas with high gain, low cost, and beam scanning capabilities. This paper presents the design of a high-gain electronically scanned planar array antenna. Compared to the parallel-fed method of traditional electronically scanned arrays, this array employs a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) series-fed network, which simplifies the fed network complexity and reduces the length of the transmission line, thereby decreasing transmission loss. The array consists of 256 elements, formed by 16 series-fed sub-arrays with high radiation efficiency. Each sub-array integrates a 2-bit digital phase shifter, enabling one-dimensional beam scanning. Simulation results confirm that the array achieves a maximum realized gain of 23.5 dBi at 12 GHz, with a maximum radiation efficiency of 45.9%, and a beam scanning range of ±60° in the H-plane.

articleTitle: A K-D Tree Ray Tracing Acceleration Algorithm for Calculating Electromagnetic Scattering Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to solve the efficiency problem of electromagnetic scattering characteristics calculation of complex targets, this paper uses k-dimensional (K-d) tree to accelerate the ray tracing process of bouncing ray method. By optimizing the node splitting plane, the intersection calculation of rays and triangular face elements is reduced, thereby improving the efficiency of ray tracing. Through experimental verification of complex models, the results show that the proposed algorithm has high efficiency. The time domain shooting and bouncing ray (TDSBR) method combined with physical optics and geometric optics can handle multiple reflections and scattering of electromagnetic waves on the target surface. When dealing with complex targets, it can better simulate the propagation path of electromagnetic waves and provide more accurate results.

articleTitle: Remote Sensing Image Anti-Interference Matching Algorithm Based on Deep Hashing
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With its efficient storage and computing capabilities, deep hashing algorithms have been widely used in tasks such as remote sensing image matching. However, while this algorithm is convenient and fast, it is easily affected by noise and other interferences, which significantly reduces the remote sensing matching performance of the algorithm. To address the aforementioned shortcomings, we propose a remote sensing image anti-interference matching algorithm based on deep hashing. Guided by class representative hash codes, the algorithm trains the deep hashing network by constructing adversarial samples with sufficient interference capability to enhance its anti-interference ability. Compared to traditional anti-interference algorithms, the algorithm proposed in this paper is more targeted and effective in the field of remote sensing image hashing. The experimental results show that the network trained using the algorithm proposed in this paper can still make correct judgments when facing interfering remote sensing images and has good anti-interference ability.

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Decoupling of 1×4 DRAs Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This article presents a machine learning assisted decoupling method to decouple 1×4 dielectric resonator antennas with uniform radiation patterns, namely radiation pattern decoupling (RPD). Metallic vias and metal strips are used as decoupling structures. Gaussian process model and parallel Bayesian optimization method is used for optimization. A new cost function is designed to evaluate the effect of radiation pattern similarity. To verify the design idea, a prototype was fabricated and measured. The measured overlapping 10-dB impedance bandwidth is 6.4%. All radiation patterns can be found to radiate along the zenith directions, which verifies the RPD effects.

articleTitle: A Novel Circularly-Polarized Asymmetric Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna Using the Cross-Spiral Slot Feeding
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel circularly-polarized asymmetric magneto-electric dipole antenna (AMEDA). The antenna achieves the circular polarization through two mechanisms: firstly, an asymmetric magneto-electric dipole with four rotational hexagonal parasitic patches; secondly, the cross-spiral slot and sequential rotation microstrip feeding structure are adopted. The 3dB axial ratio and impedance common bandwidth of the proposed CPMEDA is from 31.28 to 32.96 GHz with the peak gain of 9 dBic.

articleTitle: A Broadband Dual-Polarized Dipole Filtering Antenna Based on Parasitic Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A wideband dual-polarized loop dipole antenna that can function in the 5G frequency band's Sub-6GHz is proposed in this paper. The two radiation nulls produced in this paper are primarily produced by electromagnetic cross-coupling technology. Loading the leaf-shaped structure on the loop dipole arm introduces higher frequency radiation zeros. Below the loop dipole arm, the parasitic ring loading can produce radiation zeros at a lower frequency. The filtering dipole antenna's quality of stopband suppression is increased by the loading of the parasitic ring and leaf-shaped structure. A square parasitic structure is loaded above the dipole arm to create a new resonance mode and increase the dipole antenna's impedance matching bandwidth. According to simulation results, the antenna has a wide 65.4% impedance bandwidth (|S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| is less than -10 dB between 2.77 and 5.46 GHz). The 1.5-2.15 GHz and 6–7 GHz frequency bands, respectively, have excellent out-of-band rejection levels of 23.2 dB and 20.6 dB, and the antenna's port-to-port isolation reaches 31 dB.

articleTitle: The Novel Method of Solving Eigenmodes of the Open Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The perfect match layer(PML) is introduced for the open waveguide eigenmodes finite element method(FEM) solving. Compared to the conventional method, The PML introduction make the open waveguide eigenmodes FEM solving effienciently and accurately. The method is employed to compute the transmission constant charateristics as well. The results show that the novel method results is consistent with the theoretic solution.

articleTitle: A Self-Decoupling Method for Antenna Arrays Using High-Coupling Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this work, a self-decoupling method is proposed for multi-antenna systems by suppressing coupling modes identified through characteristic mode analysis. Antennas are modified to break high-coupling modes while preserving radiating modes, thereby enhancing isolation. The proposed method has been validated through an example of two metasurface (MTS) antennas placed side by side. Effective suppression of high-coupling modes was achieved by etching slots on the MTS, resulting in an isolation improvement of over 10 dB between the two antennas without the need for additional decoupling structures. The proposed decoupling method is applicable for various antenna systems.

articleTitle: Analogue of Tunable Polarization Independent Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Based on Graphene-Integrated Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A planar metamaterial (MM) capable of exhibiting independently tunable electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) effect is proposed and investigated. The near field coupling between the bright resonator of the metallic cross and the dark resonator of the graphene square ring gives rise to the transparency window. The EIT effect is insensitive to the polarization direction due to the symmetric geometry. By tuning the Fermi energy of graphene layer, the EIT effect can be dynamically controlled. Furthermore, the polarization-insensitive slow wave effect can be realized with the group delay up to 5.0 ps. This work may provide possible method for terahertz filters, slow wave devices and modulators.

articleTitle: Positioning Correction for TDOA system in Atmospheric Duct by Using Ray Tracing
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With the development of passive detection system, the time difference error of targets caused by atmospheric duct has become more and more obvious, which seriously affects the positioning accuracy of TDOA system. Based on the ray tracing algorithm, aimed at the radiowave signal path characteristics in atmospheric duct, a refraction correction model for TDOA is proposed. The simulation results show that the time delay difference error caused by duct basically remained around 140ns and the positioning error can reach to about 8km in the range of 200km~800km, and the technique in this paper can significantly improve the positioning accuracy of the passive TDOA system for over-the-horizon targets.

articleTitle: Adjustable Axial Ratio Circular Polarization Decoupling Suspended Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes an adjustable axial ratio(AR) circularly polarized (CP) decoupling suspended surface(DSS). While the DSS introduces a new coupling path, its rotatability provides additional degrees of freedom compared to the array antenna decoupling surface (ADS) to adjust the coupling path. This work has achieved both homo-polarization and heteropolarization hybrid decoupling for a Ka-band dual CP antenna array, with an element center-to-center spacing of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.365\lambda$</tex>. Furthermore, the adjustable AR of the DSS is advantageous for applications in large-scale array scanning and fixed beam scanning satellite communication.

articleTitle: RIS-Aided Communication Network Deployment Strategy Based on BP Model
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) represent a promising technological advancement capable of establishing a smart radio environment through the utilization of reconfigurable passive elements. This paper examines a RIS-assisted multiuser multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) downlink communication system and introduces a blockage probability (BP) model aimed at optimizing the deployment strategy of RIS. Initially, we develop a block network model and subsequently align it with the actual wireless communication environment by adjusting the probabilities of random events and the blockage threshold. We then formulate an optimization problem designed to maximize the system sumrate by jointly optimizing the active beamforming at the base station (BS) and the passive beamforming of the RIS elements. Simulation results indicate that, in comparison to deploying RIS near the BS or the users, our proposed deployment strategy can achieve higher control freedom and system sumrate.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Filter Method Based on Multi-Input Cascaded Correlation for Low-Frequency Weak Magnetic Signal Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An adaptive filter method based on multi-input cascaded correlation for low-frequency weak magnetic signal extraction is proposed, which is used to suppress broadband background electromagnetic noise and enhance the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of low-frequency narrowband target signals. The algorithm principle and implementation of the method are analyzed. The results show that the signal extraction effect of the method is verified. Compared with the adaptive filter method based on dual-input correlation, the multi-input cascaded correlation method can improve enhancement of the SNR for weak magnetic signals.

articleTitle: FEM Study on Electromagnetic Pulse Propagation in Ionosphere
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The propagation characteristics of nuclear electromagnetic pulse (NEMP) in ionosphere is studied by using the Finite Element Method (FEM). The location-varying electron density, collision frequency, and dispersive permittivity of the ionosphere are introduced into the time-domain and frequency-domain FEM. The transmission coefficient, waveform, and time delay of the electromagnetic pulse (EMP) is analyzed. This work may provide theoretical foundation for the space-based nuclear explosion detection.

articleTitle: A Novel Design of Angle Stable Frequency Selective Surfaces Using Characteristic Modes Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An angle-stable frequency selective surface (FSS) with polarization insensitivity is designed using characteristic modes analysis (CMA) in this paper. By observing the mode behavior, the characteristic modes are classified into dominant modes and higher-order modes that affect the angle stability under oblique incidences In addition, the lumped elements are loaded guided by TCM in order to eliminate high-order modes, thus achieving the angle stability. The proposed structure achieves great angle stability via full-wave simulation.

articleTitle: A Metallized Tapered Slot Antenna for Ultrawideband Application
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a metallized tapered slot antenna (TSA) for ultrawideband application which takes advatanges in manufacturability and reliability is presented. The presented all-metal TSA is composed of aluminium alloy and ferrite rodes. Compared to the conventional the printed TSAs, this design has high structual strength and is easy-to-fabricate, features good ultrawideband(UWB) radiation performance, and the impedance bandwith of 3:1 is obtained.

articleTitle: Large-Area Complex Terrain Radio Wave Propagation Loss Prediction Using Bidirectional Three-Dimensional Parabolic Equations
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the parabolic approximation of Helmholtz equation, a three-dimensional (3-D) vector parabolic equation (PE) technique for predicting propagation loss in large region irregular terrain is proposed. The split-step Fourier transform method (SSFT) is used to solve the three-dimensional vector parabolic equation and in order to analysis the backward propagation, a bi-directional parabolic equation model is established. In addition, the absorption boundary conditions and the impedance boundary conditions of the obstacle surface are also studied. Two examples were simulated using the proposed method, one of which is a large-scale real terrain, verifying the accuracy of the method.

articleTitle: Study on Multi-Mode Propagation Characteristics of High-Power High-Frequency Heating Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: During the ionospheric heating process, high-power high-frequency heating waves can excite artificial (electron density) field-aligned irregularities at the height of the ionospheric F layer under certain conditions. At the same time, due to the field-aligned scattering effect of field-aligned irregularities on electromagnetic waves, in addition to conventional reflection, part of the high-frequency heating waves will be scattered, and even scattered multiple times during their uplink and downlink propagation. Using ray-tracing technology, according to the scattering propagation characteristics of electromagnetic waves on field-aligned irregularities, a high-frequency heating propagation model based on field-aligned scattering was established. The propagation path of the high-frequency heating wave was calculated using the model simulation. The results showed that the multi-mode propagation mode of the heating wave on the field-aligned irregularities makes the ground reception effect diverse. The established propagation model and simulation analysis results lay the foundation for studying the energy dissipation mechanism of high-power high-frequency heating waves and evaluating their impact range.

articleTitle: Gate Recurrent Unit to Accelerate Radar Cross Section Calculations for Electrically Large-sized Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Calculating the Radar Cross Section (RCS) of an electrically large-sized target is an important step in EMC design. In this process, an open-source ship scaling model was selected as the target for low RCS optimization and design. A dataset was established to train a Gate Recurrent Unit (GRU) to perform low RCS optimization and design for this electrically large-sized target. The simulated annealing method was chosen to update the physical model of the ship scaling model during the low RCS optimal design process. The physical model and corresponding RCS values were accumulated during the updating process to establish a dataset. During the low RCS optimization and design process of this electric large-size target, a multilayer GRU neural network is used to learn the dataset of the target object over time. This allows the trained neural network to calculate the RCS of the target object instead of relying on traditional electromagnetic simulation computation. The multilayer GRU neural network's properties are used to decrease computational requirements and increase speed.

articleTitle: Design of a Broadband Slant Polarized Cavity Backed Microstrip-Fed Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The design of a broadband slant polarized cavity backed microstrip-fed antenna for X/Ku-band applications is presented. The proposed antenna consists of a metallic cylinder cavity, a metallic dipole and a microstrip feed line connecting with the inner conductor of a connector. The metallic cylinder cavity is partially notched on the cavity wall to enhance the bandwidth and improve the radiation performance. It is shown that the slant polarized cavity backed antenna has a bandwidth ratio over 3: 1 for Voltage Standing Wave Ratio less than 3 and realized gains ranging from 4.4 dBi to 8.3 dBi. Coverage angles with x-polarized and y-polarized gains higher than 0 dBi are over 60° in both the vertical and horizontal plane.

articleTitle: A Visual Tool for Faraday Rotation Calculation and Brightness Temperature Simulation of Spaceborne Microwave Radiometer
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Microwave radiometer is the main payload for passive microwave remote sensing in space. In order to analyze its observational capabilities, a visual tool, MR Simulator, is developed in python. This tool can fast calculate Faraday rotation of the ionosphere and simulate brightness temperature observed by spaceborne microwave radiometer. It is useful for radiometer data pre-processing and retrieval of environmental parameters.

articleTitle: A Low Loss Broadband Circularly Polarized Magnetic and Electric Dipole Antenna with High Power Capacity and Better Axial Ratio
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A S-band low loss broadband circularly polarized magnetic and electric dipole antenna with high power capacity and better axial ratio was designed. The antenna is composed of an electric dipole, a magnetic dipole, a feeding balun, and a metal floor. The electric dipole uses a bow-tie dipole, the magnetic dipole uses a folded dipole, and the feeding balun uses a metal coaxial line with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda/4$</tex> V-shaped groove. The electric dipole and the magnetic dipole are symmetrically distributed in a cross shape. The electric dipole is parallel to the metal floor, and the magnetic dipole is perpendicular to the metal floor. Through theoretical analysis and electromagnetic simulation, the results show that the relative bandwidth (VSWR <2) at the center frequency of 3.14 GHz reaches 31°/0, the 3dB axial ratio bandwidth reaches 10°/0, the gain at 3 GHz reaches 6.53 dBi, and the axial ratio of the maximum radiation direction is 0.65 dB.

articleTitle: Experimental Research on Pseudo Carrier-Domain Interference Suppression of FM-Based Passive Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Frequency modulation (FM) -based passive radar is characterized by the wide distribution of transmitters and rich signal resources. The experiment shows that the detection results of different FM signals on the same target can form a strong complementary effect, and the reasonable use of it for multi-frequency detection fusion will be able to significantly improve the system's detection stability of target. However, many signals in the FM frequency band have partial spectrum overlapping with each other, and this kind of adjacent frequency interference will greatly affect the detection performance. To address this problem, we investigate a pseudo carrier-domain processing method inspired by carrier-domain clutter suppression for OFDM signals. The method performs spatial projection at every frequency point of the surveillance FM signals, which is capable of significantly suppressing the adjacent frequency interference after adaptive clutter cancellation and enhancing the target detection performance of the interfered signals. It in turn will help to expand the selectable frequency range of the FM-based passive radar. The experimental data verifies the effectiveness of this treatment.

articleTitle: Optimized Analyses of Gain Enhancement with Metasurface Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the fractional area, which is the ratio of the area of metal surrounded to the substrate area for one cell, of the metamaterial cells is studied to find the relation between the gain enhancement and the fractional area, where the distance away from patch antenna is λ0/2. Two cases of the split ring resonator are compared, one is that the structure and the relative size are kept while increases the cell number by increasing the fractional area, and the other is kept the fractional area but with different metal area and structure for two different cells of the same resonances. We find the gain doesn't always increase with the cell number, it will decrease when the fractional area is up to a certain degree; and the smaller cells, the higher gain enhancement.

articleTitle: A Broadband Planar Reflectarray Antenna Employing Tightly Coupled Slot Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel broadband planar reflectarray antenna is proposed. The reflectarray element consists of a rectangular patch embedded with a pair of symmetrical inverted L-shaped slots, and the phase shift of the element is achieved by adjusting the length of the slots. The array bandwidth is significantly extended by introducing the tightly coupled effect through connecting adjacent elements. Based on the proposed elements, a square aperture reflectarray antenna with 450 elements is designed. Simulation results demonstrate that the presented reflectarray antenna realizes a stable radiation pattern, low cross-polarization, reasonable gain and aperture efficiency in a wide frequency band from 3 to 6 GHz. The 1 dB and 1.5 dB gain bandwidth of 22.9% and 44.4%, respectively, are also obtained. With its broadband performance as well as single-layer aperture, the proposed reflectarray antenna is a promising candidate for various wireless applications.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Spatial Spectral Estimation for Direction Finding Based on the L-Shaped Time Modulation Array
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A new two-dimensional spatial spectral estimation direction finding method based on L-shaped array and time modulation theory is proposed. The main principle of this method is to generate a harmonic component of the incident signal by modulating the RF switch under the L-shaped array, recover the array manifold vector from the harmonic component using Fourier analysis, and finally use the MUSIC spatial spectrum estimation algorithm to solve the direction information from the array manifold vector, thus completing the direction finding. Nu-merical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, which is characterized by high accuracy compared with other 2D direction finding algorithms.

articleTitle: Estimating the Signal-to-Noise Ratio from the Power Delay Profile in a Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The time domain response in a reverberation chamber (RC) can provide information which is not available in the frequency domain. We show that the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) can be estimated from the power delay profile (PDP) in an RC. Since the PDP of the impulse response decays exponentially in an RC, the peak-to-noise ratio (PNR) can be identified easily. The relationship between the SNR and the PNR of the PDP is derived and verified experimentally.

articleTitle: A Hybrid EMI Filter for CM EMI Suppression in DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) is an unavoidable issue in power electronic equipment since it may threaten the reliability of the system. Passive EMI filter is the most commonly used method for EMI suppression. However, with the demand of high-power density, the bulky passive EMI filter can no longer satisfy the requirement. Hybrid EMI filter is an alternative choice to reduce the weight and volume of the passive EMI filter and has received widespread attention. In this paper, a hybrid EMI filter for suppressing the common mode (CM) EMI in DC-DC converter is proposed. The feasibility of the proposed HEF is verified by simulation with a boost converter and the CM EMI can be effectively suppressed with the proposed hybrid EMI filter.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Dual Circular Polarization Antenna Element for K/Ka Band
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized dual-polarized antenna unit is proposed. By adding dielectric material to the septum circular polarizer, the antenna size is reduced by 38.6%, with dimensions of 6.2mm×7.2mm×40mm. A wedge-shaped structure and a parallel-coupled microstrip bandpass filter effectively address the degradation in isolation between the two ports due to size reduction. The antenna demonstrates good impedance matching and isolation performance of no less than 33dB in the K-band (18.9-21.6GHz) and Ka-band (29.4-31.7GHz). Due to its reduced size, the antenna can be effectively used as a unit in dual-band co-aperture phased array antennas, achieving sidelobe-free beam scanning effects in azimuth and elevation directions up to ±35° with a unit spacing of 6.2mm.

articleTitle: RCS Simulation of Partly Coated Electrically Large Target with SBR Method
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this study, radar cross section of electrically large target partly coated with radar absorbing materials has been simulated and analyzed by using shooting and bouncing ray method. First, the simulation results are validated by comparing with multilevel fast multipole method for electrically small objects. Then the radar cross section of electrically large target is calculated and evaluated in three conditions: perfect electric conductor, partly coated and fully coated. The results indicate that part coating plays an equivalent role in a certain range of angles compared with the full coating, which provides a way to reduce cost of coated stealth plane.

articleTitle: Propagation Characteristics of Low-Frequency Electromagnetic Waves Across Waved Seafloor
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to enhance the capability of submarine communication based on low-frequency electromagnetic waves, the propagation characteristics of low-frequency electromagnetic waves near the seafloor with a parallel Shift Operator Finite Difference Time Domain (SO-FDTD) method is presented. The numerical results indicate that the waved shape of seafloor does not alter the propagation path of the field components, which is to propagate into the seabed firstly, then go through the seabed, finally go back to the sea again. When the electromagnetic wave propagating through the waved region of seabed, a phenomenon of amplitude oscillation is observed. However, when the wave propagating away from the seabed into the sea, the propagation direction of electromagnetic wave rapidly reverts normal to the interface of seabed.

articleTitle: Analytical Calculation Method of the Far Field of an Arbitrarily Polarized Dipole Above a Double-Layer Metal Meshes
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of far-field calculation of electric dipole above double-layer metal meshes, a fast and effective analytical method is given.
