Firstly, considering the reflection coefficient of double-layer metal meshes under plane wave irradiation, the far-field calculation of arbitrary polarization dipole above double-layer or single-layer metal mesh structure is realized combined with the rapid calculation scheme of dipole radiation above uniform layered half space. The research results can provide a fast and effective means for the far-field analysis of dipoles above different metal mesh structures.

articleTitle: An Equinoctial Asymmetry Index Model of Ionospheric Scintillation Occurrences Over Chinese Low Latitude Region
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: By analyzing the observations of UHF-band scintillations recorded at the Haikou station (geographic 20.0°N, 110°E) of the low latitude region in China from 2010 to 2017, we found that the scintillation occurrences are greater in the vernal equinox than in the autumn equinox during the seven years but 2011. Based on the monthly occurrences of ionospheric scintillations and the relationship between season and solar activity, an equinoctial asymmetry index empirical model of scintillation occurrences is firstly established over Chinese low latitude region, which could accurately describe the seasonal asymmetry variation characteristics of the scintillation occurrences, and it has an important application value.

articleTitle: An FDTD Method on Nonuniform Grids for Electromagnetic Analysis in Debye dispersive Media
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces a dispersive FDTD method on nonuniform grids to deal with Debye dispersive media, termed as dispersive NU-FDTD method. Compared to the dispersive FDTD method with uniform grids, the proposed method has the advantages of high efficiency and flexibility. The research results demonstrate that the accuracy of the proposed method is similar to that of the dispersive FDTD method with fine uniform grids, and the computational efficiency is further improved.

articleTitle: Cancellation Quality Assessment with Spectrum Segmentation for Speech Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The spectrum segmentation method is proposed for the interference cancellation quality assessment, which not only integrates the spectrum distribution characteristic of speech and interference, but also introduces the statistical optimization model for calibrating the assessment coefficient. Hence, there will be a remarkable improvement of SINR estimation accuracy and real-time performance of speech signals under various common interference. Implementation in hardware and numerical experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance of proposed method under the AM pattern. It is ideal for the closed-loop interference cancellation of speech communication.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based UNet for Global Ionospheric Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Vertical Total Electron Content (VTEC) in the ionosphere is a crucial parameter for describing dynamic changes. Due to limitations in observational techniques, real-time global distribution of ionospheric VTEC is challenging to obtain. Therefore, short-term forecasting of VTEC holds significant theoretical and practical importance. In this study, we utilize global ionospheric VTEC data and employ aU-Net network to capture the spatiotemporal characteristics of global VTEC, predicting the distribution for the next 24 hours. We analyze and evaluate the U-Net model and three other models in 2015 year and 2020 year. Under varying ionospheric activity conditions, the forecasting accuracy of the U-Net network is notably superior to the other three models. In 2015, its root mean square error (RMSE) is 4.045 TECU, and in 2020, it is 1.519 TECU.

articleTitle: Recent Developments of Transparent Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: As the need to integrate various wireless communication systems into mobile devices, Antenna-on-Display (AoD) technology is considered one of the key solutions to address the challenge of limited antenna space. AoD design avoids pattern obstruction of image displays using structures such as metal mesh or conductive films, while maintaining electromagnetic characteristics similar to those of non-transparent antennas, showing broad prospects in various practical applications. This paper reviews some recent advances in transparent antennas and compares various design schemes for transparent antennas based on metal mesh. The approaches for transparent antenna design based on metal mesh are classified and described briefly, such as leaky-wave antennas, artificial magnetic conductor (AMC), linear array antennas, and coplanar vivaldi antennas. The corresponding operating mechanisms and performance are discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Design of MIMO Imaging System by Millimeter Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper a MIMO imaging radar system with 12 transmitting antennas and 16 receiving antennas is designed for scenarios such as concealed objects penetrating imaging and nondestructive detection. The designed MIMO radar system has 12 transmit antennas and 16 receive antennas, forming a non-redundant linear array with 192 virtual antenna elements. The mmWave radar system constructs a signal model of an ideal point target, and uses the actual echo data of the corner reflector to estimate and compensate the amplitude and phase deviations of 192 channels. The MIMO radar system extends the antenna array, and shortens the imaging scanning time, which has great potential in the field of penetrating imaging such as security inspection and nondestructive detection.

articleTitle: Research on Passive Radar Array Detection Technology Based on Satellite Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This article explores the target detection technology based on satellite external radiation source radar system. The system uses satellites as radiation sources and ground radar to receive target reflections or scattered echoes. A target detection method based on receiving array is proposed, and its basic principles and preliminary design ideas are explained.

articleTitle: Revisiting Sub-Structure Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The energy-based sub-structure characteristic mode analysis (CMA) process is reviewed. From the process, the physical picture of sub-structure CMA and the physical feature of sub-structure characteristic modes (CMs) are revealed. The physical picture and feature clarify the fact that: the working of every sub-structure CM needs a driving field which acts on the active sub-structure of the objective electromagnetic (EM) system only, but does not act on the passive sub-structure of the objective EM system. This fact exposes the applicable range of sub-structure CMA: strictly speaking, the sub-structure CMA is not suitable for some EM systems, such as some aperture-fed antennas and the external-field-illuminated scatterers; the usually used microstrip-antenna-oriented sub-structure CMA is approximately correct, when the antenna is excited by probe and the probe is directly connected to the patch. Some numerical experiments are demonstrated for testing the above conclusions.

articleTitle: A High-Linearity Wideband Power Amplifier Based on Dynamic Bias
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a high-linearity wideband Ku-band power amplifier chip is designed based on the GaAs 0.15 um process, and the linearity of the amplifier is improved by using diode linearization bias. A stable network design has been added to the input and interstage matching to improve stability. Feedback is introduced to extend the bandwidth of the amplifier. In the 12–17 GHz frequency range, the power gain is greater than 19 dB, the P1dB is greater than 23 dBm, and the peak power added efficiency is 34%.

articleTitle: A Super Wide Bandwidth Mesh Antenna Featuring Omnidirectional Radiation Characteristic
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Modern wireless communication and broadcasting systems need miniature wideband antennas to improve their transmission capacity. In this paper, an omnidirectional mesh antenna with super wide bandwidth is proposed. The antenna utilizes a conical monopole structure loaded with a capacitive ring and shorting pillars to radiate omnidirectionally in its bandwidth. Simulation results show the antenna's VSWR is less than 2.5 from 70 MHz to 2000 MHz while its height is 0.0687 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex> at 70 MHz.

articleTitle: Research on the Optimal Design of Polarization Conversion Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Polarization, as a fundamental characteristic of electromagnetic waves, is the locus of the tip of the electric filed at a given point as a function of time. The linear-to-circular polarization (LCP) conversion and cross polarization (CP) conversion, as two main branches of polarization manipulations, have been widely used in various fields, such as antenna designs, microwave communications, and anti-interference technologies.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Field Enhancement Resonator Integrated with a Local Oscillator Port for a Rydberg Atomic Superheterodyne Receiver
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Rydberg atom-based receivers employing atomic superheterodyne techniques exhibit outstanding performance in sensing sensitivity, making them significant in various fields such as communications, microwave quantum technology, aerospace, medicine, and meteorology. This technique requires additional local oscillator (LO) signal. However, antennas that provide LO signals in the MHz frequency range are often quite large, lacking integration and portability in practical applications. Therefore, we propose a miniaturized local oscillator structure integrated with a field enhancement resonator to achieve high-sensitivity electric field measurement. The LO signal is fed into a square spiral resonator by a coplanar waveguide-fed monopole antenna. We investigate the three-dimensional positioning of the oscillator structure and the effects of structural parameters on the performance of the field enhancement resonator. Ultimately, we achieve optimal integration of the local oscillator and resonator for electric field enhancement in Rydberg atom-based electric field measurement.

articleTitle: Simulation of Offshore Magnetic Dipoles and Electric Dipoles Based on Ocean Wave Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To study the impact of wave randomness on offshore antenna radiation characteristics, the ocean waves are geometrically modeled from the ocean spectrum using the wave equation, and the magnetic dipole and electric dipole antennas are jointly simulated with the ocean waves by the HFSS software, respectively. The input impedance and radiation patterns are analyzed at different positions, depths, and angles of inclination of the antennas. Simulation results show that at low frequencies, the real part of impedance is very small with the best radiation pattern uniformity. As frequency increases, the real part of impedance grows and the radiation pattern worsens, with electric dipole antenna showing higher directivity than magnetic dipole antennas.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Dual-Channel LP-to-CP Conversion Transmitarray with Independent Beam Control: (Invited)
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A design method of a two-channel multiplexing transmissive Linear-to-Circular polarization converter (PC) with independent controllability is reported in this paper. In order to verify the feasibility of the design concept, sixteen kinds of anisotropic converter unit cells with linear polarization (LP) receiving and circular polarization (CP) transmitting are proposed. The Linear-to-Circular PC is enabled by introducing a length difference of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{\mathrm{g}}/4$</tex> between the two parts of microstrip lines of the unit cell, which makes the transmission phase difference between the plane wave of transverse electric mode and transverse magnetic mode is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^{\circ}$</tex>. Based on the hybrid phase compensation strategy of propagation phase (PP) and geometric phase (GP), 16 kinds of cells are creatively designed, and the proposed idea is verified by forming an array. The simulation results show that the peak gain of dual CP beam is greater than 25.3 dBic, and the overlapping bandwidth of 3-dB axial ratio (AR) and 3-dB gain bandwidth is greater than 20%. The proposed transmissive Linear-to-Circular PC has the advantages of two-channel multiplexing and independent beam control, and is expected to play an important role in wireless and satellite systems.

articleTitle: Radio Environment Electrical Parameter Calibration for Ray Tracing Channel Simulation Using Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Integration of Ray Tracing (RT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) represents a transformative approach that has received significant attention in 6G communications. The electrical parameters of materials in environment are crucial for the accuracy and reliability of RT channel simulations, and these material characteristics require precise calibration based on measurements. Conventional electrical parameters calibration methods are based on global optimization algorithms that iterate over pre-configured materials. These methods are computationally intensive and struggle to provide a sufficiently detailed description of the electrical characteristics of environment. In this paper, we propose a neural network-based method for electrical parameters calibration. The results demonstrate that the simulated channel shows high accuracy after calibration with a root mean square error less than 2.5 dB.

articleTitle: Novel Filtering Method of Metasurface Antennas Based on Characteristic Mode Analysis for 5G Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this manuscript, two ±45° dual-polarized filtering metasurface-based antennas with high-suppression and wide-stopband features for 5G millimeter-wave applications are respectively presented, which are both composed of a 2×2 uniformly distributed square metasurface structure and a cross slot to excite ±45° polarizations. Benefiting from the characteristic mode analysis (CMA), it can be found that the metasurface structure can provide an inherent upper radiation null to design filtering antennas. Furtherly, by loading stubs and etching slots on the metasurface, several radiation nulls can be generated, which can realize one high-suppression filtering antenna with an out-of-band suppression level about 30dB. Next, by rotating the metasurface structure and stubs with 45°, the positions between the metasurface and feeding slot are changed, thus less CMA modes radiating at broadside direction are excited in the upper stopband, resulting in a wide stopband feature and the stop suppression range is about 2.15f0 (where f0 is the center frequency). Finally, for the fabrication of Antenna B, the ground is enlarged and the defect ground structure (DGS) is adopted to weaken the influence by the large-full ground.

articleTitle: Polarization Insensitive Multiband Electromagnetically Induced transparency -Like Metamaterials*
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we studied a sandwich metamaterial consisting of a dielectric substrate and a front and back metal structure with rotational symmetry. The transmission of the structure was calculated by finite-integral time-domain(FITD) method. The result was shown that the structure has multi-band electromagnetically induced transparency(EIT) -like effect. Through the comparative study of the electric field distribution and the transmission of part of the structure, it was found that the two bright modes are coupled to the dark mode realized the multi-band EIT in the structure. The results of the structure have potential applications in refractive index sensing, multi-frequency filter and microwave communication.

articleTitle: Characterization of ELF Noise in the Ionosphere
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we select the measurement data of the electric field instrument onboard the China Seismo-Electromagnetic Satellite (CSES) in 2022 and analyze the electric field strength of the electromagnetic wave within the Extremely Low Frequency (ELF; 3∼300Hz) band, and find that there is not only the 50Hz or its harmonic signals but also 25Hz or its harmonic signals in the ionosphere at the altitude of the satellite orbit. The comprehensive analysis of the CSES multi-orbit probe data and the comparison of the electric field strength varied with the geographic location show that the above characteristics of ELF electromagnetic waves mainly appear in the middle and low latitude regions.

articleTitle: Study on the Characteristics of Composite Electromagnetic Scattering from Actual Terrain Surfaces with Multiple Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To address the need for radar echo data collection and feature extraction of targets in real-world environments, this study utilizes the four-component model proposed by Wang and Schmugge to simulate the dielectric constant of soil and applies the Digital Elevation Model (DEM) to represent the undulations of actual terrain surfaces. Employing the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method, we investigate the composite electromagnetic scattering characteristics of actual terrain with multiple targets, and derive the angular distribution curves of the composite scattering coefficient. The results indicate that the composite scattering coefficient oscillates with the scattering angle, exhibiting scattering enhancement in the specular reflection direction. It decreases with an increasing incident angle and increases with higher incident wave frequencies, greater soil moisture content, a larger number of targets. This study offers significant theoretical and practical insights into understanding the electromagnetic scattering behavior of targets in complex terrains and optimizing electromagnetic wave detection systems, particularly for target detection and identification in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: A High-Efficient Dual-Band Reflective Linear-to- Circular Polarization Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a dual-band reflective linear-to-circular (LTC) polarization converter based on metasurface. The metasurface element is consist of the ground, rectangular and symmetrical notched ring-shaped patches. The element can realize both left-hand circularly polarization (LHCP) wave at 9.04-10.82 GHz and right-hand circularly polarization (RHCP) wave at 11.78-20.89 GHz. The simulation results show a high efficiency of conversion (EOC) (more than 99.5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) across the entire frequency band.

articleTitle: Neural Network-Based Single-Station Ionospheric TEC Prediction at High Latitude
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Total electron content (TEC) is one of the most important ionospheric parameters since the satellite era reflecting significant characteristic of ionosphere which has practical importance for its effects on radio propagation to earth. In this paper, a deep learning-based TEC prediction model at high latitude station is proposed, and a long short-term memory (LSTM) network is used to realize the short-term prediction of TEC at high-latitude station (79.9°N, 85.9°W). The short-term prediction performance of the BP neural network and the LSTM neural network for ionospheric TEC has been made comparison with the TEC measurements from 2010 to 2023. The results show that the root mean-square error (RMSE) of the LSTM model for TEC prediction in the next hour is less than 1.5 TECU, and the accuracy is 13% higher than that of the BP neural network at the optimal number of iterations.

articleTitle: Attenuation Characteristics of Laser Fuzes in Low-Visibility Dust Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To address the issue of multiple scattering in the propagation of laser fuzes in low-visibility dusty environments, an experiment was conducted to measure the transmittance of laser in such conditions. The corresponding attenuation coefficient was derived based on the Beer-Lambert law. The results indicate that in low-visibility conditions, laser energy attenuates more severely in a dusty environment, with the attenuation coefficient decreasing exponentially as visibility decreases. For instance, at a visibility of 50m, the attenuation coefficient is 192dB/km, and at a visibility of 100m, it is 85dB/km. The experimental results were compared with independent scattering Mie theory calculations and Monte Carlo simulations that consider multiple scattering effects. The findings show significant discrepancies between the experimentally measured attenuation coefficients and Mie theory predictions under low-visibility conditions, whereas the differences with Monte Carlo simulation results, which account for multiple scattering and dust particle shape factors, are smaller. However, the Monte Carlo results are still lower than the experimental measurements in low-visibility conditions. The study concludes that when dust visibility is below approximately 200m, laser transmission simulations must consider multiple scattering and other influencing factors.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Aircraft Detection with DVB-S-Based Forward Scattering Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: DVB-S signals have a significant advantage as a source of opportunistic illumination for radar systems due to their global coverage and large signal bandwidth. This paper investigates the potential application of forward scattering radar based on DVB-S signal for aircraft target detection. First, we introduce the satellite signal forward-scattering radar system and its signal processing method, followed by a simulation of the time-frequency characteristics as an aircraft crosses the baseline. Next, we construct a Ku-band satellite signal-receiving system capable of effectively capturing DVB-S signals. Finally, an experiment is conducted that successfully detects an aircraft crossing the baseline, and the resulting time-frequency representation of the aircraft shows a distinctive ‘double-V’ shape, confirming the accuracy of the simulation results.

articleTitle: Research on Radar Clutter Generation Methods Based on Pre-Simulation of Dynamic Scenes
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Radar clutter simulation is crucial for validating the detection performance of radar systems in complex environments. Traditional clutter simulation methods struggle to adapt to the dynamic changes in environments. This paper presents a radar clutter signal generation method based on pre-simulation of dynamic scenes. By utilizing a Digital Elevation Model (DEM), a surface cover model, and the proposed spherical sampling method, we pre-calculate and generate a database of discretized clutter model parameters for predetermined flight paths. During the generation of simulated clutter, interpolation techniques are employed to achieve fast and accurate simulation of radar clutter signals in dynamic scenes. Experimental results demonstrate that this method can accurately simulate radar clutter in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Tunable Graphene-Based Terahertz Cross Polarization Converter via an External Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we use graphene to design a broadband reflective cross polarization converter by applying external static magnetic field. The polarization converter can realize cross polarization conversion in the frequency range from 3.62 THz to 5.47 THz (the relative bandwidth is 40.7 %), and its polarization conversion ratio is greater than 90 %. The cross-polarization converter is capable of achieving broadband, efficiently polarization conversion, and is tuned dynamically by varying the magnetic field.

articleTitle: Study on Rain Attenuation Based on Different Raindrop Size Distributions
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The specific attenuation model introduced in Rec. ITU-R P.838-3 has been widely used for the rain attenuation prediction. Comparisons of measurements around the world reveals that the different raindrop size distributions cause the estimates using the prediction model in Rec. ITU-R P.838-3 could not agree the rainfall attenuations in all cases. In this paper, a rain attenuation estimation method is proposed for generally applied rain drop size distributions as complementary approaches to Rec. ITU-R P.838-3. This method both could be applied to the frequencies between 1–1000 GHz.

articleTitle: Double α -κ - μ Distribution: A New Model Characterizing Signal Fading in Non-Linear Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The existing channel models have limitations in accurately describing the statistical properties of electromagnetic wave signals with non-linear propagation effects in line-of-sight cascading channel environments. In this paper, we proposed a general double <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha-\kappa-\mu$</tex> model to capture these fading characteristics more precisely. Specifically, the exact expressions for the probability density function, cumulative distribution function and higher order moments based on signal-to-noise ratio are derived. The Monte Carlo simulation is conducted to validate the effectiveness of the newly proposed double <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha-\kappa-\mu$</tex> distribution. The simulation results show that the stability of the cascaded channel signals improves with higher values of the parameters <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha, \kappa$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>. Furthermore, Our proposed double <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha-\kappa-\mu$</tex> distribution is highly versatile, allowing for the inclusion of many popular product distributions, such as double <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha-\mu$</tex>, double <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\kappa-\mu$</tex>, double Nakagami- <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex>, double Weibull, double Rayleigh, and double Rician distributions.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized Broadband Log-Periodic Antenna Design for UAV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An eight-port dual-polarized broadband log-periodic antenna design for UAV applications is proposed in this paper. The antenna consists of eight log-periodic antenna elements. To achieve dual linear polarizations and omni-direction radiations, the four horizontally polarized antennas are arranged in a symmetric structure on a horizontal substrate. Another four vertically polarized antennas are inserted through slots on the horizontal substrate. The results show that the antenna achieves a -10 dB impedance bandwidth from 2 GHz to 18GH, with a maximum gain of 7.8 dBi. The antenna can be potentially used for drone-to-drone communication.

articleTitle: A Miniaturization Harmonic Radar Tag for Insect Tracking Application
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Harmonic radar is a special radar system that has been used in insect tracking in recent years due to its excellent anti-clutter capability. Generally, a harmonic radar consists of a radar transceiver and a specially designed harmonic tag. However, tag tend to become entangled with vegetation in insect tracking experiments. This paper proposes a low-loss and miniaturized passive tag design method. We introduce a foldable structure in antenna design to achieve better tag miniaturization under unified frequency operation. The results using both simulated and real data demonstrate that remarkable improvements in size of tags, gain of tags, and echo signal strengthens of tags within our proposed method on the passive tag. The effectiveness of the method is verified by the results of harmonic radar illuminate tag.

articleTitle: Research on Wellbore Correction Charts for Array Laterolog in Small Boreholes Based on Numerical Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Resistivity logging data play a crucial role in the qualitative delineation of oil and gas layers and the calculation of oil saturation. However, in practical operations, the resistivity variation curves are easily affected by borehole environmental factors, which in turn impacts their accuracy. Existing research lacks studies on the response characteristics of small borehole array laterolog tools and their correction charts for borehole effects. This paper optimizes the design of a small borehole array laterolog tool (featuring four detection depth curves) as the research subject. Through numerical modeling and finite element method simulations, we investigate the impact of boreholes and create environmental correction charts. Simulation results show that an increase in borehole diameter significantly reduces the response values of RLA1 to RLA3, while excessively high mud resistivity leads to severe distortion of the resistivity curves. For the correction charts corresponding to RLA1-RLA4, when the ratio of apparent resistivity to mud resistivity is greater than 1, the correction coefficient increases with borehole diameter. However, RLA1 and RLA2 are more significantly affected than RLA3 and RLA4. This study uses forward modeling to enhance the response analysis of small borehole array laterolog tools under various borehole conditions, filling a gap in the numerical theoretical research foundation in this field and providing important guidance for the future development of logging technology.

articleTitle: The Influence of Deformation Amplitude on the Characteristics of VIRC*
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The mechanical stirring reverberation chamber has the disadvantages of high price and small available test space. A vibrating intrinsic reverberation chamber (VIRC) made of shielding cloth can solve these problems. However, the design of deformation amplitude of such a VIRC is a key factor. At present, the deformation amplitude of a VIRC can only be determined by empirical method, which lacks theoretical basis and is not enough to guide the construction of a VIRC. In this paper, a method for calculating the deformation amplitude of a VIRC based on volume disturbance is proposed. A VIRC with a geometric size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1.5}\mathbf{m}\times \mathbf{1.3}\mathbf{m}\times \mathbf{1}\mathbf{m}$</tex> was developed, and the spatial electric field uniformity of the VIRC was tested. The results show that the spatially uniform reverberation chamber environment can be obtained when the deformation amplitude is 20cm. When the deformation amplitude reaches 50cm, the uniformity of the VIRC becomes better, and the maximum standard deviation of the space electric field is less than 2.5dB, which meets the uniformity tolerance requirements, and can be used for electromagnetic compatibility testing.

articleTitle: Maximum Likelihood DOA Estimation Method Based on Matrix Completion in Non-Uniform Noise Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: For the estimation of the direction of reach in non-uniform noise environment, the method is proposed by applying Matrix Completion theory (Matrix Completion, MC) combined with the Improved Monarch Butterfly Optimization algorithm based ML (ML-IMBO) method, In this paper, a matrix completion based ML-IMBO (MML-IMBO) estimation method for maximum likelihood DOA under heterogeneous noise environment is proposed. Experimental simulation results show that the proposed MML-IMBO algorithm can effectively suppress the influence of non-uniform noise and has good performance in DOA estimation.

articleTitle: A 77 GHz 5-bit T-type Passive Phase Shifter with Amplitude Consistency Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A 5-bit T-type passive phase shifter with amplitude consistency compensation technique is proposed for automotive radar at 77GHz. The amplitude compensation switches are introduced to make the amplitude of the phase shifter closer between phase-shifting state and non-phase-shifting state. The phase shifter is fabricated in a 65nm CMOS technology, and the measured results demonstrate excellent performance, achieving a maximum root-mean-square (RMS) amplitude error (Max RMS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dB</inf>) of 0.7 dB and a maximum root-mean-square phase error (Max RMS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">phase</inf>) of 5.4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup>within 76–81 GHz.

articleTitle: An Integrated Metasurface Antenna with Reconfigurable Scattering Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel metasurface antenna with reconfigurable scattering performance is proposed based on the metasurface cell. This antenna uses the method of integrating metasurface and conventional antenna by introducing the coaxial feeding structure into the metasurface cell. The metal patch serves as both the metasurface cell and the radiation patch of the antenna. Meanwhile, a PIN diode is introduced into the microstrip branches of the metasurface antenna to control the reflection phase. Ultimately, stable radiation performance and reconfigurable scattering performance are achieved simultaneously.

articleTitle: Shared Aperture K- and Ka-Band Antenna Array for Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The design of a shared aperture dual-band and dualpolarized antenna array is presented for the K- and Ka-band satellite communications. The antenna operating at either band shares similar geometries, consisting of four small square patches fed by two orthogonally deployed inverted-F shaped antennas (IFAs) and an L-shaped metal strip to enhance inter-port isolation. By optimizing the geometrical sizes, two types of antenna elements are adjusted to operate in the K- and Ka-band, respectively. A novel topology for intersectional arranging of low-band and highband antenna elements is proposed, using a nested configuration of triangular and rectangular layouts. The proposed antenna array, verified through simulations, can generate dual orthogonal linearly polarized waves over 18.6-21.1 GHz and 25.5-32.5 GHz, with inter-band isolations better than 17 dB and 15 dB, respectively. The typical realized gain is 13.2 dBi at 19 GHz and 16.2 dBi at 29 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: On the Total Reflectivity Estimation of Microwave Calibration Target in Middle Frequency Range
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: For the applications of radiometer calibration, the microwave calibration target is a significant device which provides with an accurate reference brightness temperature. The total reflectivity, as an important indicator, has to be determined by measurements. In this work, the remaining issue in the mono-static measurements is to be numerically investigated, which is the compensation factor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{g}$</tex> in the frequency range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\lambda} < \boldsymbol{p} < \mathbf{4}\boldsymbol{\lambda}$</tex> It is compared, through investigations in cases of plane-wave and large-size illumination, between the easily obtainable one and actual value. In the preliminary results, a relatively acceptable agreement can be observed. Which is helpful for practical measurements.

articleTitle: Multi-Band Electromagnetically Induced Transparency-Like Metamaterials*
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a double layer metamaterial structure in the microwave band is studied. The transmission spectrum of the structure is analyzed by the finite-integration time-domain (FITD) method. The results show that the structure can produce multi-band Electromagnetically induced transparency(EIT)-like effect. To further investigate the physical mechanism of the multi-band EIT-like generation of the structure, the electric field and surface current distribution are analyzed at the resonant frequencies. The results show that the multi-band EIT is mainly generated by multiple bright modes coupled to multiple dark modes. In order to explore the potential application of the structure, the change of transmission spectrum was analyzed by changing the environmental permittivity. The structure has potential applications in refractive index sensing, microwave communication and multi-frequency filtering.

articleTitle: Analyzing And Modeling Outdoor Gaussian Man-made Radio Noise Based on Different Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The outdoor Gaussian man-made radio noise exerts a considerable impact on the requisite performance of radio communication receivers. However, in the wake of technological advancement, the outdoor man-made radio noise environment is prone to alteration, and the applicability of the existing models of outdoor Gaussian man-made radio noise may change. Therefore, the aim of this paper is to analyze the outdoor Gaussian man-made radio noise figure data measured by International Telecommunication Union (ITU) in urban, residential, and rural environments over nearly 15 years, and to compare these with the calculated values from the ITU model. Through analyzing the changes in the man-made radio noise environment in recent years, the paper ultimately provides corrected fitting coefficients based on this data.

articleTitle: Research on Evaporation Duct Prediction Model Based on the GRU Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The evaporation duct is a kind of atmospheric duct phenomenon, which has an important influence on the efficiency of electromagnetic systems such as radar or radio communication systems. The traditional evaporation duct model depends heavily on the sensitivity and accuracy of the model's parameters. Therefore, we used a data-driven Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) algorithm, which can predict meteorological elements more easily, quickly and accurately. In this paper, the parameter sensitivity analysis of the classical evaporation duct model, such as P-J model and NPS model, was carried out. Then, the ERA5 reanalysis data provided by the European Center and a single station radiosonde data from 2020 to 2021 were adopted to predict the evaporation duct height by the Gated Recurrent Unit algorithm, which was compared with other machine learning algorithms (such as the Bayes and the SVR). The experimental results show that the NPS model is more stable than the P-J model, and the Gated Recurrent Unit algorithm may have the best prediction accuracy among the other machine learning algorithms.

articleTitle: Research on Determinisitic Channel Capacity of MIMO System Based on Ray-Tracing Model in complex Indoor Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the channel capacity is investigated as a crucial metric for evaluating the transmission capability of channel information, which is essential for the design and assessment of communication system performance. A deterministic channel model based on the reverse ray tracing method has been employed to establish a multi-input multi-output (MIMO) system in an indoor scenario. The multipath information of rays in the MIMO system under a deterministic channel was accurately calculated through the algorithm. The channel matrix was constructed using the data output by the algorithm, and the channel capacities of different MIMO systems in indoor scenarios were computed based on the MIMO system channel capacity formula. To verify the significance of MIMO systems in enhancing channel capacity, the channel capacities of single-input single-output (SISO), multi-input single-output (MISO), and MIMO systems, as well as MIMO systems with different numbers of antennas, were compared at different frequency points while keeping the horizontal distance of the transceiver antennas constant. Cumulative distribution function (CDF) graphs of each system were plotted, and the average capacity of each system was calculated. The results confirmed that MIMO systems can significantly improve the channel capacity of the system, and the average channel capacity increases with the order of the MIMO system. Additionally, various factors affecting the channel capacity of MIMO systems under deterministic channels, including frequency, line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) propagation environments, and the number of antennas, were thoroughly discussed. The performance of MIMO systems was analyzed in terms of the singular values of the H matrix, the condition number of the channel matrix, and the correlation coefficients between antennas in the R normalized autocorrelation matrix, with the simulation results being explained and discussed.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Off-Diagonal Butterfly-Based Direct Solver for Computing Far-Field Radiation of Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A hierarchical off-diagonal butterfly-based (HODBF) direct solver for calculating antenna array radiation problems has been proposed, which can be used for direct solving of antenna array radiation problems. Numerical examples demonstrate its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Modeling of Magnetoelectric Laminate Composite Using 2D-FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Magnetoelectric (ME) laminate composites exhibit stronger magnetoelectric effect than other ME composites, which can be used in many fields such as sensor, resonator and antenna. Based on the established multiphysics field coupling equations, a two-dimension Finite-Difference Time-Domain (2-D FDTD) model is proposed to analyze the resonance performance of ME laminate composites. The linear constitutive relationship is applied to describe piezoelectric and magnetostrictive effects in ME composites. The simulation result shows that the proposed FDTD model can analyze the transverse and longitudinal stresses and be used to predict the resonance frequency of ME laminate composites in different directions, which gives more generalized analysis than bulk acoustic wave FDTD model.

articleTitle: Ku-Band Low-Profile Dual-Circularly Polarized Planar Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this letter, a dual circularly polarized planar reflectarray antenna suitable for Ku-band satellite communication was proposed. The array adopts a single layer metasurface structure, and the unit cells are primarily composed of hexagonal metal splitted rings with different sizes. By synthesizing Berry phase and Dynamic phase, the independent control of left-hand circularly polarized (LHCP) and right-hand circularly polarized (RHCP) double beams is realized. The bandwidth of the designed cells is 28% (10.5 GHz - 14 GHz) with a reflection coefficient amplitude greater than -1dB. When a left-handed circularly polarized wave at the center frequency (11.725 GHz) excites the array, the beam direction of the antenna is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{\varphi},\boldsymbol{\theta}) =(\mathbf{90}^{\circ},-\mathbf{20}^{\circ }))$</tex>, the maximum gain reaches 27.7 dB, the aperture efficiency is 48.3%, and the 1 dB gain bandwidth is 37% (11 GHz to 16 GHz). When a Reft-handed circularly polarized wave excites the array, the above performance parameters are (90°, 20°),27.8 dB, 49.5% and 34%, respectively.

articleTitle: Fast Calibration of Beam Pointing Directions Based on Principal Component Analysis for Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The actual beam pointing directions of a phased array antenna can be different from the designed ones, which may cause serious consequences in radar applications. Conventional calibration methods require measurements of nearly all angles, which is very time-consuming. This paper introduces a fast calibration method based on Principal Component Analysis (PCA), which only requires measurements at partial angles. The PCA extracts characteristics of beam pointing direction errors at those measured angles and predicts the actual beam pointing directions at all required angles. Experiments show that, the standard deviation of the discrepancies between the predicted and actual beam pointing directions is approximately 0.053° when only 1/10 of the angles are measured. Hence, the proposed fast calibration method is valid.

articleTitle: Design of a High-Gain Transmit-Reflect-Array Antenna for Bidirectional Beams Exhibiting Orthogonal Polarization Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A high-gain transmit-reflect-array (TRA) antenna with bidirectional beams and orthogonal polarization attributes is presented in this paper. The antenna features an arrow-shaped amplitude-phase modulated (APM) unit, which can switch between transmission and reflection characteristics by adjusting the angle of the arrow. Additionally, the polarization attributes of the transmitted and reflected electromagnetic waves are orthogonal. Utilizing this APM unit, a sparse array approach is employed to design the TRA antenna, integrating both transmitted and reflected units on the same phase-shifting surface to achieve bidirectional beams. The measured results align well with simulation outcomes. The transmitted beam is y-polarized while pointing at 0°, achieving a peak gain of 24.1 dBi with a relative 1-dB gain bandwidth of 16.2% at 30 GHz. On the other hand, the reflected beam is x-polarized while pointing at 170°, attaining a peak gain of 24.0 dBi with a relative 1-dB gain bandwidth of 13.1% at 30 GHz.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Propagation Loss Model for Urban Environment with Raytracing Method
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A hybrid propagation loss model is proposed to cope with the typical urban propagation scenario where the propagation is affected by the buildings and building entries. The statistic method and ray tracing method are both applied in the proposed model, which makes it possess a higher accuracy and practicality compared to the single application of each method. It is believed that the hybrid propagation loss model would be available to expand for future communication systems in mmWave or even THz.

articleTitle: Design of High-gain Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna Using Split Ring Metasurface for Near-field Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Antipodal Vivaldi antenna have been widely used in many fields including near-field measurement due to its low profile and ultra-wideband characteristics. However, it faces the challenge of low gain, as well as patterns distortion. In this paper, a high-gain antipodal Vivaldi antenna based on split ring metasurface (MS) is proposed. By introducing the metasurface composed of split ring elements on the antenna aperture, the gain and radiation stability of the antenna are improved. The simulation results show that at 6-18GHz, the return loss of the designed antenna is below -10 dB and the maximum gain reached 11.5 dBi. Moreover, in the whole frequency band, the 3-dB beam width of the antenna is stable and the radiation pattern is undistorted. Finally, the designed antenna is fabricated and measured, and the measured results are in good agreement with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Effect of Displacement Error of Dielectric Rod Antenna Used in Phased Array Radar on Radiation Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The effect of displacement errors of dielectric rod antenna arrays on radiation performance is analyzed in this paper. For dielectric rod antenna arrays, there will be horizontal and vertical displacement errors during the assembly process, which will interfere with the radiation pattern of the antenna array. Displacement changes based on Gaussian random errors are added to the antenna array in order to more effectively describe the displacement errors present in the antenna array. The analysis of the displacement error on the performance of the antenna array helps to evaluate the actual performance of the radar and provides a reference for the improvement of the antenna element assembly process.

articleTitle: Design of the Unit Cell Based on Liquid Crystal for A Beam Scanning Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the unit cell of the beam scanning reflectarray is proposed. The unit cell is based on the liquid crystal (LC), which consists of two dielectric substrate layers and an LC layer. In the simulation, when the relative permittivity of the LC ranges from 2.5 to 3.0, the tunable reflection phase range of the proposed unit cell reaches about 300° at 11 GHz. To verify the proposed unit cell, the reflectarray consisting of 10×10 LC-based unit cells is designed and simulated. The simulated first sidelobe level (SLL) is less than -14 dB at 11.4 GHz. And the max gain is 19.27 dB in the working band.

articleTitle: Design of an Inband Millimeter Wave Full Duplex Circularly Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposed an inband millimeter wave full duplex circularly polarized antenna. Multilayer structure and metasurface are employed. Left hand circularly polarization (LHCP) and right hand circularly polarization (RHCP) can be realized by exciting different ports. Slots and strip metal patches are used to improve isolation between ports. The simulated impedance bandwidth is 17%, ranging from 24.08GHz to 28.62GHz. The 3dB axial ratio bandwidth ranges from 25.72GHz to 28.69GHz. Isolation in the operate band is greater than 19.31dB, the maximum isolation is 39.55dB at 26GHz. The maximum gain at 26GHz is 8.60dB.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Metal-Frame MIMO Antenna Based on Mode Control for 5G Smartphones
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This work presents a 5G broadband MIMO antenna array applied to the metal frame of smartphones. Based on the mode regulation, the ratio of fundamental mode and high mode frequencies is reduced to achieve 3.3-6.0 GHz broadband coverage. At the same time, two low frequency antenna units are designed for multiplexing with decoupled structure, which can cover PCS(1850- 1990 MHz), UMTS(1920-2170 MHz), LTE2300(2300-2400 MHz) and LTE2500 frequency band (25000–2690 MHz), respectively. The low frequency antennas not only participate in radiation, but also act as a decoupled structure for 5G broadband antennas to improve space utilization. Experiment results show that the designed MIMO antenna array has good performance in the operating band of 3.3-6.0 GHz with ECC less than 0.04 and efficiency up to 80%.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility Analysis for the Provisional Communication Network Planning of Radio Telescope Site
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper conducts an electromagnetic compatibility analysis for the provisional communication network planning in the construction area of a radio telescope site, aiming to achieve both network coverage and minimize the received interference power on sensitive equipment. In order to achieve the above goal, objective functions for two different tasks are designed, and the genetic algorithm is adopted to optimize the two objective functions. The results show that the minimum received interference power is -101dBm, which represents a reduction of approximately 40dB compared to the maximum received interference power, significantly enhancing the electromagnetic compatibility between communication base stations and sensitive equipment. It shows that the proposed method can be applied to the electromagnetic compatibility design during the construction and operation phases of radio telescopes.

articleTitle: Amplitude-Phase Measurements of Near-Field Scattering of Vortex Electromagnetic Wave by Regular Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the amplitude-phase distribution measurements of the scattering near field of vortex electromagnetic wave is conducted in a microwave anechoic chamber environment by utilizing a robotic system for automated testing and analysis of antenna near-field characteristics. The reliability of the measurement data is verified by comparison with the simulation results produced by the FEKO software. The effects of beam parameters, the polarization of vortex waves and the position of the receiving field are analyzed based on the measurement results. The results demonstrate that the near-field amplitude of the target irradiated by the vortex beam is contingent upon the irradiated target's shape and the beam's parameters. This work may provide a foundation for the further utilization of the near-field scattering characteristics to obtain more information about the radar target.

articleTitle: Feasibility Analysis of Using Evaporation Duct for Communication in the South China Sea
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Evaporation duct is a phenomenon that almost always exists across the global oceans, facilitating electromagnetic waves to propagate beyond the horizon and enabling over-the-horizon communication. This paper presents a simulation-based analysis of the feasibility of utilizing evaporation duct for communication in the South China Sea. Initially, atmospheric refractivity profiles and evaporation duct heights were derived from meteorological observation data obtained from gradient towers in the South China Sea. Subsequently, the parabolic equation (PE) model was employed to simulate the propagation characteristics of electromagnetic waves under these specific evaporation duct conditions. This simulation provided insights into the variation of propagation losses with distance and transmission frequency, ultimately identifying the optimal communication frequency for achieving long-range communication. Furthermore, a simulation of the communication link system was conducted, with the receiver's signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) being assessed across different time periods. The feasibility of using the evaporation duct for communication was analyzed. The results indicate that under these evaporation duct conditions, 89.58 percent of SNR surpassed the threshold of 40 dB, indicating the potential for effective communication.

articleTitle: The Investigation of EM Scattering and SAR Image Simulation of Maritime Ship Formation
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to effectively simulate the SAR images of composite scenes of maritime ship formation, this paper combines the Two-scale subdivision Shooting and bouncing Ray method (TSBR) with the two-scale model (TSM) of sea surface to establish an electromagnetic (EM) scattering model for maritime ship formations. This method uses the large-sized facet to fit the geometric profiles of ship target and sea surface, while utilizing fine ray tubes formed by the small-sized facet for ray tracing. Moreover, it considers the complex coupled scattering paths between the sea surface and ship formation, improving computational accuracy while ensuring efficiency. Finally, the EM scattering calculation model is further combined with the SAR imaging system to simulate the SAR echo signals of the maritime ship formations. Then the Range Doppler (RD) imaging method is used to obtain the SAR image of maritime ship formation. Our work will to some extent alleviate the problem of insufficient measured ship SAR images, and provide the data support for the ship detection and recognition in the complex maritime environment.

articleTitle: A Wideband Dual Circularly-Polarized Metal Cavity Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel wideband dual circularly polarised metal cavity antenna array is proposed. The radiating element consists of a tilted slot on the narrow wall of the ridged waveguide and a bending slot at the bottom of the L-shaped wall. RHCP and LHCP antenna arrays have the same waveguide structure and the difference is in the orientation of the slots. The impedance bandwidth of the antenna at the operating frequency is about 15% (9.0GHz~10.5GHz), and the axial ratio bandwidth is about 20% (8.8GHz~10.8GHz). The antenna has the characteristics of high efficiency, simple structure and wide band.

articleTitle: A Spaceborne Phased Array Antenna with High Gain Narrow Beam and Wide Coverage
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of high complexity, high cost, and high power consumption in traditional multi beam phased array antenna, a spaceborne phased array antenna with the same aperture is designed to achieve both narrow beam with high antenna gain and wide coverage. The implementation scheme of this phased array antenna is relatively simple. The phased array antenna adopts a full array to form a fast and agile scanning narrow beam with high antenna gain, ensuring high transmission rate communication to key areas under the satellite. Additionally, through three sub arrays of the phased array antenna, three wide beams with relatively high antenna gain are formed, which can simultaneously increase the wide coverage of specific areas under the satellite.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation for the Detection of Underground Pipelines Using GPR
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: As a non-destructive technique, ground penetrating radar (GPR) is extensively used for detecting underground pipelines. To find out the distribution of underground pipelines and avoid the damage for them. In this paper, the underground pipelines with different materials were simulated using gprMax, i.e., concrete, copper, iron, and PVC pipelines. Peplinski's semiempirical soil was taken into account to ensure that the soil environment more closely real conditions. In order to get clearer and highlight echo signals, the average method was used. A discussion about different kinds of pipelines B-scan profile to analyze the electromagnetic properties of the microwave propagation in underground media. At last, a comparative analysis was conducted on the B-scan images of the four-pipeline model under uniform soil and simulated soil conditions to evaluate the impact of different soil conditions on the echo signals. Through analyzing the electromagnetic characteristics of underground pipelines to verify the advantages of ground penetrating radar in the measurement of underground pipelines.

articleTitle: Design of Zero-Backtracking Antenna Array with Wide-angle Low-RCS Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a zero-backtracking antenna array with wide-angle low radar cross section (RCS) performance. Building upon the directional backtracking characteristics of the traditional Van Atta antenna array, this design achieves phase cancellation of reflected echoes from adjacent antenna elements by adjusting the transmission line phases. This reduces the scattered echo and lowers the backward RCS of the antenna array. Simulation results demonstrate that, compared to a metal plate of the same size, the antenna array achieves a reduction of 17 dB in RCS at the 0° incident angle, 20 dB at 10°, 6 dB at 40°, and 10 dB at 70°, effectively reducing RCS for incident waves within a wide-angle.

articleTitle: HF Communication Simulation Modeling from Qingdao, China to Tromsø, Norway
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper uses the ionospheric models IRI2016 and NRLMSISE-00, along with the ray tracing method, to simulate the high frequency (HF) signal communication effects between Qingdao, China (36.04°N, 120.2°E), and Tromsø, Norway (69.65°N, 18.95°E). The results show that HF signal communication technology can satisfy the communication requirements over a distance of 6,700 km between China and the polar region. However, HF signal communication in the polar region experiences severe multipath effects, leading to significant signal attenuation. This study is conducted in conjunction with propagation engineering technical issues, employing a specific ionospheric model, and demonstrates the application of three-dimensional ray tracing in certain propagation engineering scenarios.

articleTitle: Analysis of the propagation distance and delay of GNSS sea-scattered signals in tropospheric ducts
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To facilitate the analysis of the propagation characteristics of Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) sea-scattered signals in tropospheric ducts, it is necessary to implement the mutual conversion of the propagation distance and delay. For different constellation orbits and elevation angles of GNSS satellites, a suite of simulations on the variations in the code delays of the sea-scattered signals relative to the direct signals and the specularly reflected signals with the horizontal distance from the scattering point on the sea surface to the receiving antenna are made in this paper. The results indicate that the impacts of the Pseudo Random Noise (PRN) code rates on the code delays are more significant than those of the orbit altitudes, and the code delays are taken as the minimum values in the case of specular reflection. Furthermore, when the elevation angle is extremely low, its variation with the horizontal distance between the satellite and the receiving antenna cannot be neglected.

articleTitle: A Range-Doppler Map Simulation Method Based on Near-Field Electromagnetic Scattering Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a range Doppler simulation method based on near-field electromagnetic scattering algorithm is proposed for radar and target intersection scenarios. Firstly, the near-field physical optical (PO) expression under antenna beam irradiation is given, and the closed expression is obtained based on the local far-field approximation method. The near field physical diffraction theory (PTD) is further introduced to improve the simulation accuracy. Then, based on the expression of near-field scattered electric field, the calculation process of distance Doppler graph is derived in detail. Finally, the numerical results show the accuracy and efficiency of this method in calculating velocity and distance information.

articleTitle: Propagation Model of Very Low Frequency Waves in the Ionosphere
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the finite-difference time-domain method with inhomogeneous grid and GPU parallel computing, this paper establishes the propagation model of very low frequency (VLF) waves in the ionosphere. The model can flexibly modify ionospheric parameters and simulate the propagation of VLF waves under different ionospheric conditions. This model provides theoretical support for the wide application of VLF waves in the ionosphere and the understanding of the mechanism of the whistler wave in the ionosphere.

articleTitle: An Improved Architecture of Polarimetric Phased Array Radars for Enhanced Transmitting Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Alternately transmitting and simultaneously receiving (ATSR) and simultaneously transmitting and simultaneously receiving (STSR) are the two most commonly used polarization modes for polarimetric phased array radars (PPAR). Conventional array architectures are designed strictly according to these two modes, which limits the full utilization of the hardware resources. This paper proposes an improved architecture of PPAR, which exhibits enhanced transmitting performance with more economical structures. Although the amount of active components is equal to the conventional ATSR architecture, both ATSR and STSR polarization modes can be flexibly supported. The results of simulation experiments proved that compared to the conventional ones the proposed architecture has advantages in the cross-polarization suppression for the ATSR mode and the cost reduction for the STSR mode.

articleTitle: Prediction of Northern Polar ionospheric scintillation Using the Random Forest and LSTM Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Ionospheric scintillation is one of the most important space weather phenomena in the polar ionosphere, which is clo sely related to people's lives, especially to the widely used satellite navigation and positioning system with unavoidable impacts, so the prediction of ionospheric scintillation needs to be addressed. Nowadays, a network of multiple Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receivers has been established in the Arctic, and the sc intillation index data provided by the GNSS receivers make the prediction of northern polar ionospheric scintillation possible. To predict the polar scintillation events, we developed a new deep le arning method. Based on the 2011–2016 dataset from the Eureka station (79.99°N,274.09°E), by using a random forest approach to regressively analyze the physical covariates that characterize the solar-terrestrial environment, we evaluate the correlation of 24 different parameters with the phase scintillation index (σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">φ</inf>), filter out the five covariates with the highest correlation as inputs to the long-short time memory (LSTM) algorithm, and make a prediction of σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">φ</inf> one hour in advance. The results show that the model can accurately predict polar ionospheric scintillation, demonstrating that the deep learning method has a wide range of prospects in the field of predicting polar scintillation.

articleTitle: Target Detection Method Based on Accurate Prediction of Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to explore how to construct an inversion system based on the characteristics of the target when the target has a disturbance to the background electromagnetic, the target characteristics are inverted. In this paper, a target detection method based on detecting electromagnetic disturbances in steady-state space is proposed, a target detection method based on Babinet and Fresnel zone theory is proposed, and a weak electromagnetic disturbance signal enhancement method based on differential cancellation is used to enhance the upper-air signal fluctuation. The space electromagnetic field disturbance based on the Beidou satellite signal as the external radiation source is simulated and analyzed, and the target is judged to appear and locate the target according to the fluctuation received by the ground station.

Author Keywords: The Babine and Fresnel Zone Principle

articleTitle: Design of the 1-Bit Unit Cell for A Dual-Polarized Broadband Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A broadband dual-polarized 1-bit unit cell for beam scanning reflectarray is proposed. The unit cell includes elements in two orthogonal polarization directions. Each element is composed of a pair of tightly coupled dipoles and a pair of phase delay lines. RF switches are loaded on the delay lines to alter the unit cell's reflection phase. Simulations demonstrate that the unit cell can achieve 1-bit phase shift from 4 to 6 GHz. To verify the beam scanning capability, the radiation pattern of a reflectarray that includes 11×13 unit cells is calculated. The results indicate that this design can achieve ±30° beam scanning from 4 to 6 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of SSPP Based 3D X-Band Frequency-Selective Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this work, a class of spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) based X-band spatial bandpass filters are designed. In these designed 3D frequency-selective structures, a spatial wave coupling structure is specially designed to implement spatial wave to filter coupling. By combining the high-pass substrate-integrated waveguides with the SSPPs which possesses low-pass characteristics, the spatial bandpass filter is achieved. Two X-band spatial FSS prototypes are designed, and simulation results show that both designs have good filtering characteristics and angle stability.

articleTitle: Research on Tungsten Heating Layer in Phase Change Switch
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> - W has been widely used in device heating layers due to its low electrical resistivity and high mechanical strength. This article prepared <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex>-W films by selecting the thickness and annealing temperature of W films. At the same time, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex>-W thin film is used in the indirectly heating phase change switch as the heating layer. The insertion loss of this phase change switch at 1-20 GHz is less than 0.75 dB, and the isolation degree is greater than 22 dB, and the on-off resistance ratio of the switch is greater than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>. These are indicating that this switch has good performance.

articleTitle: Dual Band Low Profile Circular-Polarized Shared Aperture Phased Array for Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a low-profile, shared aperture antenna suitable for low Earth orbit satellite communication, operating in the dual-frequency bands of left-hand circular polarization (LHCP) at 21 to 22 GHz and right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) at 25 to 27 GHz. The dual cross-band isolations are better than 20dB and 25dB. The dualband shared aperture array is arranged in an equidistant square pattern. The total profile is only 0.762mm, about 0.06 high-frequency wavelengths. A wide-angle scanning of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 60^{\mathrm{o}}$</tex> is obtained in both operating bands, and the axial ratio is always below 3dB during scanning.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Wideband Filtering Reflecting Surfaces for 6G Radio Environment Manipulation
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes dual-polarized wideband filtering reflecting surfaces for 6G radio environment manipulation. The proposed reflecting element is composed of the basic filtering element and the true-time-delay line. The wideband filtering characteristic is synthesized and designed according to desired performance. A reflecting surface with 12×12 elements is realized for a deflection angle of 40°. Within the operating bandwidth of 70.1%, the average efficiencies for simulations and measurements are 82.5% and 77.4%. The dual-polarized reflecting element and reflecting surface are further obtained, where simulated average efficiencies for x and y polarizations in the overlapped 66.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> bandwidth are 91.7% and 92.5%.

articleTitle: Transition Structure from Substrate Integrated Fin-Line (SIFL) to Microstrip Line
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a multilayer structure based on substrate integrated fin-line (SIFL), featuring designs for both microstrip-to- unilateral fin-line transitions and microstrip-to-antipodal fin-line transitions. The substrate integrated configuration overcomes the limitations of conventional fin-line transition structures that require installation within waveguides. Compared to traditional fin-line transitions, this approach offers advantages such as lower cost, easier fabrication, and improved integration with other electronic components. Through simulation and experimental validation, it is demonstrated that the insertion loss is less than 1.5 dB within the 8 GHz to 10 GHz frequency range, with test results closely aligning with the design curves.

articleTitle: A Planar Dual-Band Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a planar dual-band antenna is presented. At 2 GHz, the antenna operates as a half-wavelength dipole. At 3.5 GHz, the E-dipole in full-wavelength mode and the M -dipole in slot mode work together to form a magneto-electric (ME) dipole. The measured impedance bandwidth of the antenna are 1.93~2.07 GHz (7%) and 3.2~4.08 GHz (23.6%).

articleTitle: A Novel Low Profile Stacked Microstrip Wideband Antenna Using F-Shaped Slot
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel low profile antenna operating at a very high-frequency (VHF) band is presented in this communication. The antenna is composed of three-layer microstrip patch with F-shaped slot. Compared to the traditional VHF band antenna, this antenna has an extremely low profile of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{0.015\lambda}$</tex> at its lowest operating frequency. Simulated results show that its operating bandwidth ranges from 30 to 350 MHz with the voltages standing wave ratio (VSWR) less than 3 and the gain over -25dBi. The proposed antenna is a viable candidate for VHF communications.

articleTitle: Unidirectional Small Antenna Design Using Optimal Currents Based on Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A method for designing unidirectional electrically small antenna is proposed by analyzing the achievable directivity using characteristic modes. By examining the optimal currents of the achievable directivity within the design space, the fundamental antenna structure can be established.
