Structural parameters are then optimized to achieve the antenna with high gain, a high front-to-back ratio, and good impedance matching. The proposed method is validated through the simulated design of a unidirectional electrically small antenna with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{ka}=\mathbf{0.7}$</tex>, achieving a gain that closely approaches the achievable gain of the initial design space, along with a good FTBR. This method provides valuable design guidance for configuring high-performance unidirectional antennas within constrained spaces.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Multi-Target DRFM System Based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With the development of electronic warfare in modern combat, Digital Radio Frequency Memory (DRFM) technology has assumed an increasingly important role due to its ability to interfere with enemy radar and protect friendly forces from being tracked. This paper proposes a DRFM design based on Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) technology and the AD9361 agile RF transceiver. This simulator achieves multi-target echo simulation through multi-stage delay and applies Doppler shift and amplitude scaling to the outputs.

articleTitle: Beam Scanning Antenna Based on Radiation-Type Intelligent Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Intelligent metasurfaces have attracted remarkable attention in wireless communication and radar due to their ability to manipulate electromagnetic wave in real time. However, both reflective and transmissive intelligent metasurfaces require an additional feed source, resulting in a relatively high profile and lower efficiency. Therefore, reducing the profile, improving efficiency, and ensuring real-time modulation over the meta-surface are of utmost significance. A radiation-type intelligent metasurface for dynamic beam scanning is proposed in this paper. A pair of PIN diodes is integrated on the element to achieve 1-bit phase manipulating, while power dividers are integrated on the metasurface to form a microstrip network to stimulate the radiation layer. The simulation results elucidate that the radiation-type intelligent metasurface can achieve real-time beam manipulation within the range of ±45°, with an aperture effi-ciency exceeding 20% and an extremely low profile. The novelty of this study lies in the elimination of the external feed required by traditional intelligent metasurfaces. This framework offers significant advantages in terms of low profile, high efficiency, and cost-effectiveness.

articleTitle: Study on Composite Electromagnetic Scattering from Polar Surface with Buried Target by the Method of Moments
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To address the requirements for target detection, identification and imaging in polar environments, based on the digital elevation model to simulate the realistic polar surface undulation, the frozen soil mixing dielectric constant formula was chosen to calculate the dielectric constant of the medium below the polar surface, and the method of moments was applied to study the composite electromagnetic scattering between the polar surface and the buried equilateral triangular cross-section columns when the incident wave was a conical wave, and the curves of the composite scattering coefficients varied with the scattering angle were obtained, the Influences of incident angle, incident wave frequency, polar soil type and soil temperature on the composite scattering coefficient are discussed.

articleTitle: A Physics-Informed Transformer for Atmospheric Ducting Propagation Loss Forecast
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Atmospheric ducting is an atmospheric refraction effect on electromagnetic waves formed under specific weather conditions. Accurate forecasting of its propagation loss is of great importance in modern communication and radar systems. Traditional forecast methods face challenges due to the complexity of physical model inference and the incompleteness of empirical data, often resulting in low precision. This paper proposes a physics-informed Transformer method for forecasting propagation loss, utilizing the Helmholtz equation to forecast the propagation loss of atmospheric ducting. This method combines the advantages of physics-informed approaches with the efficiency of the Transformer architecture. By incorporating physics-informed conditions of atmospheric ducting propagation, the proposed method significantly improves forecast accuracy and efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to the current state-of-the-art methods, our approach significantly enhances forecast performance under various atmospheric conditions. Performance metrics such as RMSE and training loss validate its effectiveness and application potential in forecasting atmospheric ducting propagation loss, providing a valuable reference for improving communication and navigation systems based on atmospheric ducting conditions.

articleTitle: Enhancing OAM Radio Waves Through Directional Antenna Arrays: A Practical Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) of radio wave has been considered as a promising technique to greatly improve the transmission rate in communication systems. The most common method to generate the OAM radio wave is to use an antenna array. However, a detailed analysis of the effect of the antenna type, number of elements, and frequency on OAM radio waves with directional antenna array are not given. In this paper, we investigate these effects on the beam angle, beam width, and maximum gain for the OAM wave, with the mathematical model generated by a circular directional antenna array.

articleTitle: Optimization Method of Low Sidelobe Multi-Beam Leaky Wave Antennas Using Discrete Dipole Approximation
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This article proposes a discrete dipole approximation (DDA) for optimizing multi-beam leaky wave antennas. The radiation pattern of typical leaky wave antennas can be accurately represented by the proposed DDA. On the basis, the optimization method based on particle swarm optimization (PSO) is also employed to work in conjunction with DDA to optimize the antenna pattern. As a proof of concept, dual-beam antenna and three-beam antenna can be obtained quickly and accurately by the proposed method. More importantly, satisfactory antenna sidelobe performance less than -15dB is obtained at the operating frequency of 5.8 GHz.

articleTitle: Application of Mode Filtering in Near-Field Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper briefly introduces the theory of planar near-field measurement and applies cylindrical mode filtering to correct errors in planar near-field measurements. This method decomposes the far-field pattern obtained from planar near-field measurements into cylindrical wave modes. By exploiting the spatial constraint relationship between the cylindrical wave spectrum and the tested antenna, scattering components are filtered out. Finally, the processed far-field pattern is obtained through cylindrical wave spectrum to far-field transformation. By measuring a horn antenna, the algorithmically processed directional pattern is compared with the pattern from simulation software. The results indicate that the algorithm effectively reduces the impact of scattering errors on the far-field pattern.

articleTitle: Design of Transparent Antenna Based on Uniform Metal Mesh
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With the rapid development of mobile communication equipment, visible optically transparent antennas have attracted widespread attention due to their superior concealment, high integration and characteristics of easy commonality. However, traditional optically transparent antennas designed by transparent conductive material film are facing contradiction between optical transmittance and radiation performance. In this paper, two transparent antennas based on uniform metal mesh (UMM) are proposed: “T-shaped” antenna and “question mark”-shaped antenna, both of which are fed by coplanar waveguide structures. The antennas are designed to operate in the (1559–1610) MHz band. The transparent UMM film is fabricated by orthogonally distributed thin silver wires with the width of 20 μm and the period of 300 μm. While the optical transmittance (OT) of the T-shaped antenna using UMM reaches 82.6%, the gain of the T-shaped antenna using UMM has improved from -2.42 dBi to 0.62 dBi, compared to that of the T-shaped antenna by indium-tin-oxide (ITO) film. The OT of “Question mark”-shaped antenna using UMM reaches 91.8%, which is a significant improvement. The antenna design and optimization method based on UMM above can effectively improve the realized gain and radiation efficiency of optically transparent antennas without affecting optical transparency, which has certain academic value and engineering significance.

articleTitle: A Multiband Circularly Polarized Antenna for Satellite Navigation System
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This letter presents a multiband circularly polarized antenna for the satellite navigation system. The main features of this antenna are the following: four layers of stacked patches to achieve multiband operation and compactness; one metal structure; and one radome. The radome can ensure aerodynamic shape and the antenna is fixed on the aircraft through the metal worktop. Simulation results show that the proposed antenna exhibits excellent performance. Details of design considerations and simulation results are presented.

articleTitle: Study on Radar Reflectivity of Rain Clouds Based on Rayleigh Approximation
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Accurate calculation of radar reflectivity for rain clouds is crucial for meteorological observation and weather forecasting. This study delves into the radar reflectivity of various types of rain clouds using the Rayleigh approximation method. Utilizing experimental data from the last century, we calculate and analyze the radar reflectivity for high-level clouds, maritime cumulus, nimbostratus, stratus, orographic clouds, continental cumulus, cumulonimbus, and congestus clouds. The radar reflectivity is primarily determined by two key parameters: the number density and the radius of the particles in the cloud. The results indicate that the radar reflectivity of different types of clouds, from low to high, is as follows: high-level clouds, maritime cumulus, nimbostratus, stratus, orographic clouds, stratocumulus, continental cumulus, congestus clouds, and cumulonimbus.

articleTitle: Dynamic Semi-Passive RIS-Assisted URLLC Communication with Finite Blocklength
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Distinct from the conventional paradigms of fully passive and fully active RIS configurations, a novel semi-passive RIS composed of partially active reflecting elements and passive elements which can leverage combined advantages is proposed in this paper, Specifically, we investigate a semi-passive RIS assisted URLLC system from the energy efficient maximization perspective. In addition, efficient alternating optimization, successive convex approximation, and successive refinement algorithms are developed to jointly optimizing the transmit precoding matrices and dynamic RIS beamforming matrix. Numerical analysis shows that the proposed RIS system significantly outperforms traditional RIS and non-RIS systems. Moreover, semi-passive RIS with only few active elements can achieve superior energy efficiency compared to passive RIS even with infinite blocklength. This highlights the potential of semi-passive RIS to reduce latency, enhance reliability, and improve energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Design of E-Band Common Aperture Dual Polarization Terminal Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a co-aperture terminal antenna works in the E band is proposed. The antenna is composed of substrate integrated wave-guide(SIW) cavity antenna and printed dipole antenna. The public bandwidth of the antenna array reaches 13.3%. The maximum gains of vertical and horizontal polarizations are 9.89dB and 10.38dB, with the scanning angle from -40° to 40° for vertical polarization and the scanning angle from -52 ° to 52 ° for horizontal polarization with gain deterioration less than 3 dB.

articleTitle: Research on the Integrated Prediction Method of Sea Clutter Characteristic Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Accurate prediction of sea clutter characteristic parameters can help to improve the detection performance of radar on sea targets. However, the existing methods predict each characteristic parameter independently, which brings a lot of difficulties in practical application. In this paper, based on the measured clutter data under different radar operating conditions and marine environmental parameters, a parameter prediction model of sea clutter characteristics is established by using residual networks starting from the description of multi-source measurement parameters. The network model proposed in this paper enables holistic prediction of clutter characteristic parameters. Based on the experimental results of the measured data, it can be seen that the method proposed in this paper has a high prediction accuracy, a wide range of application, and a more convenient use process.

articleTitle: A Broadband Metasurface Absorber Design with Surface Impedance of Resistive Ink
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A broadband metasurface absorber design loaded with surface impedance of resistive ink is proposed. This design consists of three dielectric substrate, one depletion layer and two depletion-free layers. The three dielectric substrates are composed of polyimide, FR4 and an air dielectric substrate, respectively. The depletion layer comprises a surface impedance resistive ink. The depletion-free layer I is constituted by a combination of rectangular, ring and arrow-shaped metal patterns. The second depletion-free layer is a metallic ground plane. The measurement results demonstrate that the relative absorption bandwidth is 91.25% in the frequency range of 3.51 GHz-9.40 GHz. The measurement results are in accordance with the simulation results. Finally, a comparison is made between the radar cross-section (RCS) of the proposed absorber and that of a metal plate of equivalent dimensions. It is observed that the designed absorber is capable of reducing the RCS, thereby offering a promising solution for stealth applications.

articleTitle: Design of a Wavelength-Scale and Dual-Frequency Anechoic Chamber
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Anechoic chambers played a decisive role in fields of microwave imaging, RCS reduction, radiation and scattering measurement and so on. Facing with the dilemma of high cost and huge construction site, traditional anechoic chambers can hardly be promoted and applied in practical engineering scenarios. In this work, wavelength-scale anechoic chamber working at dual-frequency was specially designed, simulated and fabricated with the help of the spatially arranged absorbing surface. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed dualfrequency anechoic chamber, the voltage standing wave ratios were experimental estimated which are comply with the simulation results. The proposed design and fabrication methodologies are simple and robust, we foresee the promotion and extensive use of the miniaturized anechoic chambers both in scientific research and practical engineering.

articleTitle: Rapid Optimal Deployment Algorithm for UAV Cooperative Positioning Sites
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A rapid deployment optimization algorithm that balances deployment time and positioning accuracy for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is proposed. In addition to the existing constraints on communication distance and safety distance in the optimization function, a constraint on UAV formation adjustment time is introduced. For the nonconvex region optimization problem, the initialization process of the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is improved by incorporating the Delaunay triangulation method. Simulation results demonstrate that the formation optimization effectiveness can be enhanced by over 40% in nonconvex regions, while the required time for UAV deployment is reduced by more than 65%.

articleTitle: A Compact Base Station Antenna Array With High Isolation in New U6G Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The 3GPP RAN Plenary has started the standardization of frequency band 6425–7125 MHz(U6G) as a new IMT licensed frequency band[1] and International Telecommunication Union(ITU) will be carried forward in the final acts of World Radiocommunication Conference 2023(WRC-23)[2]. In this paper, a compact 3×4 base station antenna array with high isolation and improved radiation patterns operating in 6.425-7.125GHz frequency band is proposed. The proposed array consists of twelve miniature dual-polarized antenna elements, which are designed for pressure casting of mass manufacturing. The horizontal spacing between 1×3 subarrays is 0.36λ(λ is the wavelength of the electromagnetic wave at 6.775GHz in the free space) and the vertical spacing between the antenna in the same subarray is 0.65λ. High isolation of above 20dB is achieved successfully by deploying a partial reflective decoupling layer (PRDL) and special metal strips in the array. Kinds of electromagnetic couplings in the array are effectively decreased by the two decoupling methods and improved radiation patterns are obtained. The simulated results show that the compact array with high isolation and improved radiation patterns becomes the candidate of the base station antenna array operating in the brand new 6.425-7.125GHz frequency band.

articleTitle: An Equivalent Dual-Channel Detection Method and Simulation Analysis for Radio Proximity Fuzes Based on Doppler Sharpening Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to improve the height-finding accuracy of radio proximity fuzes in complex ground environments and reduce the issue of premature detonation caused by reflections from tall buildings, this paper proposes an equivalent dual-channel detection method based on Doppler sharpening technology. This method splits a wide-beam antenna into a dual-channel detection mode with wide and narrow beams. By utilizing Doppler frequency to distinguish between building reflections and the ballistic flight speed, the method effectively prevents premature detonation due to false detection. Simulation experiments that model the process of a projectile skimming over rooftops validate the feasibility of this algorithm in avoiding premature detonation on rooftops and ensuring proper detonation upon ground impact.

articleTitle: Extremely High Sensitivity Contactless Measurement Technology of Passive Intermodulation in Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Passive intermodulation (PIM) is an un-negligible issue in satellite antennas and communication systems, which also has an adverse impact on future 6G communications. High sensitivity measurement is essential for evaluating the PIM performance of microwave components. Novel contactless PIM measurement method is proposed. All components of the measurement system that pass through high-power signals are designed to be contactless using gap waveguide technology, and the residual PIM of the measurement system can be significantly reduced. As a result, the PIM measuring sensitivity would be improved to an extremely high level. A Ku-band contactless PIM measurement system is successfully implemented, and 3rd order residual PIM of less than -140dBm@2×100W under temperature cycling conditions is achieved.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-Target Motion Detection and Tracking Algorithms Based on One-Dimensional Array Antenna Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces an algorithm that applies multi-speed information weighting to the spatial power matrix of signals. Based on the radar data cube, a velocity information weighting matrix and a target signal power matrix are constructed. By performing a point-wise subtraction between the elements of these two matrices and subsequently applying a threshold filtering, a motion target signal power matrix is derived, enabling the identification and separation of moving and stationary targets.

articleTitle: Enhancing Antenna Radiation Gain with an Improved Half-Fisheye Lens
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An improved half-fisheye lens (HFL) is designed for high-gain lens antennas applications. To control the profile height of the lens and reduce its refractive index, the HFL is axially compressed, and its refractive index distribution modified. Additionally, to achieve plane wave emission under practical feeding conditions and relieve the impedance mismatch at the interface between the HFL and free space, a transition layer with a specific shape and refractive index distribution is designed at the interface. When feeding with a standard horn antenna, the improved HFL achieves a radiation gain improvement of 1.8 dB compared to the conventional HFL, while reducing the maximum refractive index from 2 to 1.6.

articleTitle: A Wideband Dual-Polarized Quad-Ridged Horn Antenna with Stable Beam-Width
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Reflector antennas face practical requirements such as wider working bandwidth and multi-polarization. When the traditional ridged horn is used as the feeder, the beam-width of the ridged horn is sharply narrowed with the working frequency increase, which leads to a decrease in the reflector system's gain. To solve this problem, a broadband quad-ridged horn antenna with a stable beam-width is designed in this paper. By optimizing the profile of the ridge curve and horn shell curve simultaneously, the designed horn achieves a basically unchanged -10 dB beam-width in the 2~6 GHz with dual-polarization.

articleTitle: Marine Environment RCS Prediction Model Based on Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The simulation of electromagnetic scattering from the random rough sea surface has a wide range of applications in the study of remote sensing instrument parameter design, ocean parameter inversion, and composite electromagnetic scattering. By introducing the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method, a method based on Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) is proposed to obtain the radar cross-section (RCS) of targets on the random rough sea surface. This method involves training a GAN model to learn the complex nonlinear relationship between the input sea surface roughness and radar scattering cross-section, thereby achieving high-precision prediction in HH polarization mode. Experimental results show that compared with the FDTD method, the proposed deep learning model not only ensures the accuracy of HH polarization radar scattering cross-section prediction but also significantly reduces computational time.

articleTitle: A 11GHz Conformal Phased Array Antenna for Curved Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a 11 GHz Conformal Phased Array Antenna is presented for curved surfaces, which has 1-bit reconfigurable radiation units, digital phase shifters, and feeding network with a low profile (0.07λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>at 11 GHz). The 1-bit reconfigurable unit utilizes symmetric geometries and PIN diodes to realize stable 180<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup>phase change, The digital phase shifter provides 8 phase coding states and together with the unit form 16 phase coding states. The antenna operates between 10.7 and 11.4 GHz, and the array contains 8×1 elements with each of which being individually addressable. By changing the state of the diodes, the antenna can achieve ±30<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup>beam scanning without sparsity, and the gain fluctuations are less than 1dB. The antenna provides conformal beam-scanning capability with low cost, which applies to vehicle-mounted or airborne application scenarios.

articleTitle: Wideband and wide Beam Scanning Array Design by Adjusting E-Coupling and H-Coupling Resonance
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A new wideband and wide beam scanning array is designed by using a new decoupling method. The beam width of the array element and inter-element isolation of the linear array can be improved simultaneously. By installing a ground-connect stub, a magnetic dipole is introduced to generate horizontal direction radiation to broaden the antenna beam width. Moreover, the ground-connect stub facilitates an E-coupling and H-coupling resonance between array elements. Thus the high isolation of the array can be achieved. Finally, the beam scanning capability of the eight-element linear array can be enhanced correspondingly. It is a potential method for phased array designing.

articleTitle: Target State Tracking in Semi-Passive RIS-Aided ISAC Wireless Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a target state tracking algorithm for semi-passive reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) aided Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems. It enables simultaneous data transmission and location sensing using shared resources. Specifically, echo signals can be received by deploying low-cost RF chains on certain RIS elements, and measurement information about the state of the target can be obtained at the RIS side by analyzing the echo signals. Moreover, considering the nonlinearity of the equations of measurement information and vehicle motion, the extended Kalman filter (EKF) and a novel RIS phase-shift design scheme are proposed for tracking the target state with guaranteed accuracy and reduced computational complexity. Numerical simulations validate the efficacy of the proposed design and prediction scheme.

articleTitle: Study on LF Insulated Dipole Antenna in Seawater
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A LF insulated dipole antenna for underwater wireless information transmission is proposed. The propagation characteristics of EM waves in seawater is analyzed. The insulation layer of the antenna is designed to mitigate effects caused by the big conductivity of the seawater. The radiation characteristic and return loss of the antenna with a matching network are given. The effects of the radius and relative permittivity of the insulation layer on the radiation property are discussed. This work may provide guidelines for the development of effective underwater communication systems.

articleTitle: Computer Vision-Based Channel Prediction for Vehicular Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Integration of communication and artificial intelli-gence is an important part of future evolution of 6G. As an important research field of artificial intelligence, computer vision also has broad cross-application prospects in wireless channel prediction due to its special advantages such as not occupying spectrum resources. In this paper, we first carry out channel sounding and environment sensing campaigns, and simultaneously acquire channel and image data. Then, we propose a channel characteristics prediction model based on computer vision, which can realize prediction of typical channel characteristics such as path loss, K-factor and root-mean-square delay spread. Finally, based on measured data, we validate the performance of model. The results demonstrate that proposed model can accurately predict the above three characteristic parameters with root mean square error less than 3 dB.

articleTitle: Graphene-Based Magnetically Tunable Wideband Terahertz Absorber
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a broadband THz tunable absorber based on graphene via static magnetic field bias (SBMF), exhibiting an outstanding absorption of more than 90% in the frequency range from 1.49 THz to 2.41 THz (i.e., the relative bandwidth is 47%). The operating frequency band of the absorber can be dynamically tuned by adjusting the magnitude of the SBMF. Moreover, the absorber has excellent properties of insensitive polarization. Due to its sub-wavelength structure, small volume, tunable and broadband characteristics, the absorber can meet the requirements of miniaturization and integration.

articleTitle: Tri-band Dual-polarization Wide-angle Scanning Shared Aperture Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel tri-band dual polarized shared-aperture array antenna is proposed in this paper. The C-band antenna adopts the double-layer microstrip patch, and it operates at 3.9 GHz. The folded microstrip dipole is designed as an L-band antenna, with the L1-band antenna operating at 1.69 GHz and the L2-band antenna operating at 1.29 GHz. Based on the miniaturization design of antenna cell, the array achieves wide-angle scanning of ± 60°.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Propagation Characteristics of P-Band Narrow Pulse in Coal Seams
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to study the change rule of attenuation during the penetration of P-band narrow pulse into coal samples, a time-domain test scheme based on P-band narrow pulse is proposed. The time-domain narrow pulse test of coal seam media with thickness of 20,35,50,80,100 cm is carried out by using an antenna with frequency band of 300 MHz to 1GHz. The receiving antenna is directly connected to the oscilloscope to store the received signals. The received signal data were processed by intercepting time window, background cancellation, wavelet denoising, and analyzing the changes of positive and negative peaks in the signals, and the transmission characteristics of narrow pulses passing through different thickness coal seams and the relative dielectric constant of coal samples are obtained. This conclusion has certain guiding significance for studying the transmission characteristics of P-band electromagnetic wave in coal and life detection in underground.

articleTitle: Analysis of Reflection Height Descent in Ionospheric Heating Experiments
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Using the high-power heating and diagnostic equipment of the European Incoherent Scatter Scientific Association (EISCAT), we conducted ionospheric heating experiments on September 13, 2010, ionic line enhancement characteristics observed using VHF radar. The study found that as the heating process progresses, the altitude of the ion line enhancement phenomenon gradually decreases. Through analysis of electron density and electron temperature, we propose that the underlying physical mechanism of this phenomenon may be the enhancement of diffusion transport processes. Specifically, electron diffusion drift alters the electron density near the reflection altitude, causing a step-like decrease in altitude. This result is not due to an increase in electron temperature affecting the electron recombination rate.

articleTitle: Classification Method of Echo and Interference Signal Support Vector Machine Based on Two-Dimensional Characteristic Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to improve the anti-jamming ability of FM fuze in electronic countermeasures, a support vector machine classification method for echo signal and jamming signal based on two-dimensional characteristic parameters was proposed. In this method, the actual target echo signal and the guided jamming signal of the frequency modulated fuze are taken as the research objects, and the time domain information entropy and frequency domain information entropy are used as the two-dimensional feature parameters, and the two signals are classified and identified by the support vector machine classification method. Through laboratory tests, it can be seen that the classification accuracy can reach more than 95%.

articleTitle: Long-Wave Antenna Technology and Development Trends for Remote Communication and Navigation
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Long-wave antennas are extensively employed in extra long-distance communications and navigation, ocean surveillance, and radio broadcasting, owing to their superior propagation characteristics at low frequencies. Long-wave signals, characterized by strong penetrating power and extended propagation ranges, are well-suited for remote communications and signal transmission in unique environments. As information and communication technologies continue to evolve, the design and optimization of long-wave antennas have emerged as a focal research area. This article systematically reviews the fundamental principles, common types, design methodologies, and recent research advancements of long-wave antennas, aiming to offer a comprehensive reference framework to facilitate further advancements and applications in long-wave antenna technology.

articleTitle: The Integrated Antenna with Frequency Selective Surface Radome
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With the development of modern communications, radio equipment on airborne platforms is becoming more numerous and complex. Low-profile omnidirectional antennas are widely used on airborne platforms, and loading FSS radome for antennas has become a research direction. This paper investigates the integrated design of omnidirectional antennas with frequency selective surface (FSS) radome while achieving low-profile characteristics. The integrated omnidirectional antenna consists of an FSS radome, a low-profile radiator, a gain enhancement structure and sixteen short-circuit pins. The miniaturization of the antenna through the use of a low-profile radiator. Metal FSS consists of an outer hexagonal ring and an inner hexagonal layer. The gain enhancement structure and the short-circuit pins address the radiation pattern degradation and impedance mismatching caused by the strong coupling of the FSS radome and the low-profile radiator in compact spaces. The integrated antenna can operate from 2.2GHz to 2.6GHz and has an omnidirectional radiation pattern. This paper innovatively investigates the low-profile integrated design of an omnidirectional antenna with FSS radome.

articleTitle: Fast Convergent FDA Transmit Beamforming Based on Interior Point Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This article proposes a dot-shaped transmit beam-forming algorithm by using interior point (IP) algorithm to design optimized frequency offset (FO). We compared the beam focusing performance of this scheme with linear FO, logarithmic (Log) FO, and genetic algorithm (GA) FO schemes, and provided the convergence process of the algorithm. The simulation results show that the algorithm converges quickly while ensuring good beam focusing effect. We extended it to two-dimensional planar array and further reduced the computational complexity of the algorithm by applying symmetric frequency offset on the array. The effectiveness of the algorithm was verified through numerical simulation

articleTitle: Short-Term Forecasting of Evaporation Ducts Based on GraphCastGFS
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Evaporation ducts have an important impact on the propagation of electromagnetic waves near the sea surface. The short-term forecasting of regional evaporation ducts has important practical significance for radar, communication, etc. The development of machine learning technology has resulted in a wide range of applications in the field of meteorological forecasting. Recently, the National Centers for Environmental Prediction (NCEP) released the GraphCast Global Forecast System (GraphCastGFS), which is a new meteorological forecasting product based on the machine learning algorithm GraphCast. This study carried out a 168 h short-term forecast for the northern part of the South China Sea (SCS), based on the GraphCastGFS forecasting product and the NAVSLaM model. Taking ERA5 data as the benchmark value, a root-mean-square error (RMSE) analysis of the evaporation duct height (EDH) forecast results based on GraphCastGFS, and those of GFS, was performed. The results showed that the RMSE of the EDH forecast result based on GraphCastGFS was 3.0 m, and that of GFS was 3.4 m. The short-term forecasting accuracy of evaporation ducts based on GraphCastGFS was found to be marginally better than that of GFS, and the rapid data generation speed of GraphCastGFS further suggests its substantial potential in the field of evaporation duct forecasting.

articleTitle: Satellite Communication Smartphone Circularly Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a circularly polarized antenna for smartphones, positioned at the top bezel of the device. The antenna exhibits a –6 dB impedance bandwidth ranging from 2.36 GHz to 2.76 GHz and 3 dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth from 2.11 GHz to 2.57 GHz, covering the S band of the BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) from 2483.5 MHz to 2500 MHz. The proposed circularly polarized antenna demonstrates excellent performance, providing an outstanding option for smartphone satellite communication antenna structures.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Pixel Antenna Design Method Based on Dominant Rank Pre-allocation NSGA-II
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With the continuous advancement of millimeter wave technology, antenna design is trending towards miniaturization and cost reduction. The second section of this article presents an improved NSGA-II algorithm with dominance rank pre-allocation for antenna optimization. The combination of this improved algorithm with the Internal Multi-Port Method (IMPM) enables rapid analysis and optimization of pixel antennas. Based on this method, a frequency-reconfigurable pixel antenna operating at 24.63GHz to 25.13GHz (K-band) and 29.26GHz to 31.88GHz (Ka-band) was designed in the third section of this paper. The gains of the antennas are 10.5dBi and 11.8dBi respectively, and the half-power beamwidths of both the E-plane and H-plane of the antennas are greater than 30°.

articleTitle: VGG16 and Morlet Wavelet-Based Anomaly Detection for Automotive Actuators
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for anomaly detection in automotive air conditioning actuator(AACA) based on acoustic feature extraction and deep learning. The Morlet wavelet transform is used to convert the acoustic signal sequence of the AACA into a time-frequency graph, extracting the transient features and spectral information of the signal. Then, the pretrained VGG16 model is employed to extract high-level image features from the time-frequency graph. Finally, the Support Vector Data Description (SVDD) classification algorithm is used for anomaly detection. The test results show that this method can effectively distinguish between normal and abnormal states of the automotive air conditioning actuator, achieving high detection accuracy and robustness. This provides a new solution for real-time monitoring and fault prediction of automotive air conditioning actuators.

articleTitle: Simulation of Space-Time Coding Metasurface By Field-Circuit Co-Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper develops a field-circuit co-simulation method to dynamically analyze the space-time coding metasurface arrays. The proposed co-simulation method is to combine discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) method based on Maxwell's equations with SPICE solver. The spacetime coding metasurface arrays are decomposed into two subsystems: one is electromagnetic structure part which is modelled by the DGTD method, and the other is circuit part including arbitrarily linear or nonlinear components which is solved by the SPICE solver. The electromagnetic and circuit parts are iteratively solved to achieve the transient response of the space-time coding metasurface arrays. Numerical examples are given to verify the proposed method, demonstrating the feasibility of field-circuit co-simulation for analysis and design of the space-time coding metasurface.

articleTitle: Solving the Impulse Response of a Typical High-order Filter by Differential-algebraic Equations
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Application of the Pantelides method on solving typical high-order filter's differential-algebraic equations (DAEs) is presented. The method is proved to be valid for transforming the unsolvable DAEs to a solvable form. The numerical calculation based on the transformed DAEs is taken. The comparison between the result with that of the Simulink shows the filter's impulse response is correct.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Hexagonal Ring Type Linear-to-Circular Polarization Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An ultra-wideband linear-to-circular(LTC) polarization converter(PC) is designed, featuring a hexagonal metal periodic array. The metal rings are placed diagonally, ensuring consistent reflection characteristics for both TE and TM polarized waves. Numerical simulations confirm that, under normal incidence, this converter effectively transforms incident linearly polarized waves into reflected circularly polarized waves within the 18.2-59.4 GHz band, relative axial ratio(AR) bandwidth of 106%), with an AR less than 3 dB. Furthermore, at the central operating frequency of 39 GHz, the LTC PC unit structure is compact, with dimensions of only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.52\lambda_{0}\times 0.52\lambda_{0}\times 0.13\lambda_{0}$</tex>. This miniaturized design significantly enhances its potential for application in integrated K, Ka, and U-band polarization conversion devices. Therefore, this converter provides robust support for achieving efficient and compact polarization conversion and is expected to play a crucial role in related fields.

articleTitle: Research on Electromagnetic Scattering Acceleration Algorithm Based on Coupling Region Division
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The shooting and bouncing rays method[1] (SBR) is a combination of physical optics method (PO) and geometric optics method (GO). Compared with low-frequency numerical method, SBR has a remarkable high speed. Therefore, many experts and scholars are using it to calculating the EM scattering from the target with large electrical size [2]–[4]. This article is based on the shooting and bouncing rays method and uses the coupling region division method to accelerate the scattering calculation of rough surface and target on it. The Radar Cross Section (RCS) results and calculation time before and after the improvement are provided to prove the feasibility of the coupling region division method.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of a 2.45 GHz Flexible Liquid Metal Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this letter, a flexible liquid metal antenna operating at 2.45 GHz with a dielectric substrate thickness of 50 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\mu m}$</tex> is proposed. The design utilizes liquid metal eutectic gallium-indium (EGaIn) as the antenna's conductive material, a flexible polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) material as the dielectric substrate, and a coplanar waveguide (CPW) to feed the antenna. The simulated results show that the antenna has a minimum bending radius of 10 mm in both directions when covering the 2.45 GHz ISM band using HFSS. Finally, the laboratory fabrication process and the bendability measurements of the antenna are described in detail.

articleTitle: Design of an Eight-Port UWB MIMO Antenna with Shared Radiator
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an eight-port UWB MIMO antenna with a shared radiator is proposed. The structure of the radiating unit of the proposed antenna is a planar polygon more closely resembling a circle due to the broadband effect of the circular patch. The ground plane of the antenna is optimized with a stepped structure mainly on both sides for good impedance matching. The ground planes are rotated 45 degrees to each other to reduce the coupling effect between the ports. The frequency range of the simulation is from 6.2 GHz to 45 GHz, and the isolation degree of S12 is mostly above 15 dB, while the rest of S13, S14, and S15 are mostly above 20 dB. The frequency band achieved by this antenna covers the X-band, Ku-band, K-band, and Ka-band and is suitable for satellite communication.

articleTitle: Design of High Isolation Electromagnetic Vector Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A high channel isolation electromagnetic vector antenna is proposed to meeting the needs of miniaturization (small footprint), multi-dimensional, and high-precision development in the acquisition of wide area ionospheric information. The electromagnetic vector antenna consists of three orthogonal electric dipoles and three orthogonal magnetic loops. The antenna body is made of aluminum and has six channels. Through extensive simulation calculations, the optimal structure of the proposed antenna is determined. The simulation results indicate that within the shortwave range of 3–30 MHz, the VSWR of the proposed antenna is less than 2.5, and the isolation between each channel is high. The measurement results show that the isolation between the channels of the proposed antenna is high and the VSWR<2.5 in the shortwave range of 3–30 MHz. The proposed antenna has the characteristics of high isolation and can be used for receiving multi-channel ionospheric incoming wave signals. It can provide basic, reliable and effective received data for multi-feature processing and parameter extraction such as polarization domain and spatial domain of incoming wave.

articleTitle: Analysis of Received Signal and Detection Performance of Passive Radar on Non-Stationary Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Passive radar on moving platform has significant advantages, however, its non-ideal motion introduces new problems. This paper first models the multi-channel received signal on a non-stationary platform. The time-varying Doppler frequency shift (DFS) and direction of arrival (DOA) of the echo caused by non-stationary motion are analyzed theoretically. Simulation results show that errors exist in the DFS and DOA of the target, and the integration gain decreases. Motion compensation is required for target detection and clutter suppression.

articleTitle: Experiment Research on Echo Characteristics of Pulsed Laser Fuze in Smoke
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a measurement method based on a smoke chamber is proposed to study the backscattering characteristics of pulsed laser fuze in smoke environment. Firstly, the smoke environment was created in a chamber by burning a known amount of smoke agent whose main chemical composition is red phosphorus. Then, a pulsed laser fuze and auxiliary equipments (visibility meters, lambert reflectors, etc) were arranged to collect echo signals. Finally, a statistical method was used to analyze echo characteristics of the pulsed laser fuze. The experimental results show that the laser fuze prototype used in this experiment does not even have the ability to distinguish a target with low reflectivity (5%) from the smoke environment which was created by burning 0.3g smoke agent, and it cannot discriminate a target with high reflectivity (99%) from the smoke environment when the mass of smoke agent is larger than 4g dues to the high smoke particles concentration. The method proposed in this article provides a new feasible means for the research on anti-interference effect evaluation for smoke of pulsed laser fuze.

articleTitle: Ultra-Low Profile Folding Transmission Array Based on the W Band
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Here we propose a design method for an ultra-low profile folding transmission array based on W band. The folded transmission array antenna designed in this paper has two kinds of metasurface(MS) array, and an open waveguide as feed. On this basis, the lower MS can efficiently convert the linear polarization incoming wave emitted by the feed into the cross-polarization reflection wave. The upper MS can realize full reflection of a specific linear polarization wave and full transmission of another linear polarization wave, while converting the transmitted linear polarization wave into a cross-polarization wave. Through reasonable design and ray tracking principle, the antenna can reflect the radiation electromagnetic waves on the upper and lower MS three times, and its profile can be reduced to 1/4 of the traditional transmission array. Simulation results show that the antenna has a 3dB gain bandwidth of 2 GHz from 77 to 79 GHz, a peak gain of 15.1dBi at 78GHz, cross-polarization averaging below-15dB and sub-valve averaging below 10dB. This design method aims to achieve low profile and high efficiency antenna solution, providing new ideas for W band array antennas requiring compact size and good performance.

articleTitle: Terrain Relative Navigation in the Permanently Shadowed Regions at the Lunar Poles with DEM Data and SIFT Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: China's Chang'e-7 mission (CE-7) plans to conduct in-suit measurements in permanently shadowed regions (PSRs) at lunar south pole. The poor lighting conditions near the lunar poles makes optical images insufficient for terrain-relative navigation (TRN). Digital elevation model (DEM) obtained by the lunar orbiter laser altimeter (LOLA) onboard the lunar reconnaissance orbiter (LRO) is suitable for TRN in PSR. By matching the real-time DEM data acquired by the laser imaging sensor on the flyer with the geocoded LOLA DEM data, the position of the mini-flyer can be estimated. In this paper, scale-invariant feature transform (SIFT) algorithm is used to acquire matched points, which can be used to calculate rotation and scaling matrix to determine the position and flying direction of the flyer. The images of the surface slopes derived from the LOLA DEM data with high resolution are taken as the real-time images from the mini-flyer, and the images with low resolutions are taken as the reference images. SIFT algorithm performs well under different resolutions and rotation angles. The results indicate that the matching error between reference images and real-time images is small, making it suitable for TRN in lunar PSR. This paper also conducts registration experiments between SAR images and DEM images. The results indicate that the registration performance between SAR images and DEM images is not as good as that of DEM images with different resolutions.

articleTitle: Wideband 3D Hexagonal Shaped MIMO Antenna System for Mmwave Vehicular Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a compact non-planar six ports 3D hexagonal shaped MIMO antenna array system for mmwave vehicular communication is presented. Identical six 1 x 4 antenna arrays are arranged in 3D hexagonal shaped to attain pattern diversity and focus beam in the desired direction. Each of the six arrays consists of four rectangular shaped elements which are truncated in the top middle with partial ground plane. The Rogers RT5880 substrate with permittivity 2.2 and thickness 0.254 mm is used. The dimensions of each single array is 15 X 26 X 0.254 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. All arrays of MIMO antenna system are operated in wideband frequency range from 24 GHz to 40 GHz. Good isolation is achieved among the array's configuration. The MIMO diversity parameters ECC, DG, CCI and MEG give well accepted values. This is a suitable 3D structure design for mmwave Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication and Internet of Things (IoT) communication systems.

articleTitle: A 77 GHz Millimeter-wave Radar Antenna with a Reflector Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a 77 GHz microstrip patch millimeter wave radar antenna is proposed for the problems of narrow bandwidth and low gain of a microstrip patch antenna, which can be applied to the anti-unmanned aerial vehicle(UAV) system to detect unmanned aircraft. This millimeter wave radar antenna mainly includes a radiating body structure, an air layer, and a reflector structure. The radiating element consists of eight 1*8 string-fed array antennas and dielectric substrates, and the string-fed line array is designed based on the Chebyshev array synthesis method. Based on the 8*8 array antenna, the antenna's gain is improved based on the reflector structure. After simulation, it is shown that the antenna gain at 77Ghz is 10.58dB the -10dB impedance bandwidth is 6.6GHz without increasing the reflector structure, and the -10dB impedance bandwidth of the antenna with increasing the reflector structure is 4.5GHz. The gain of the antenna at 77GHz is 13.27dB, which is an increase of 2.67dB year-on-year, with a certain degree of directionality and sufficient bandwidth.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband High-Gain Segmented Luneburg Lens Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a design of a spherical dielectric lens composed of several generalized Luneburg lenses with different focal lengths segmented together. The focal length of the outer layer of the segmented lens is small, and the focal length of the inner layer is large. Even if the feed radiation pattern is narrow, the radiation can still illuminate most of the segmented lens area. Compared to standard Luneburg lenses of the same size, the designed lens maintains higher aperture efficiency over a wide bandwidth. Assuming negligible insertion loss, the lens achieves aperture efficiencies ranging from 52% to 85% across the 6–12 GHz frequency band.

articleTitle: A Wideband W-Band Driver Amplifier with Capacitor Neutralization in 28-Nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband W-band driver amplifier fabricated in a 28-nm CMOS process for automotive radar, imaging, and high-frequency communications. The amplifier achieves a 3dB bandwidth of 70.9-96.9 GHz, with a relative bandwidth of 31%. A peak gain of 4.7 dB, and input/output 1dB compression points of -3.2 dBm and -1.3 dBm, respectively. It employs capacitor neutralization technology to mitigate parasitic effects and improve stability and bandwidth. The design consumes 20.1 mW at 0.9 V and occupies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.05}\ \mathbf{mm}^{2}$</tex>, The amplifier's optimized power output and 50-ohm matching make it suitable for W-band applications.

articleTitle: Radiation Mode Analysis of Negative Permeability Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The High Impedance Surface (HIS) or near-zero refractive index metamaterials are used extensively to enhance the antenna performance or radiate directly. However, the radiation characteristic of negative permeability metamaterial has not been focused. We verify the corresponding radiation mode by using the negative-permeability split-ring resonator (SRR), where the related radiation modes are the same as the resonant modes. And a modified rectangular waveguide is fed to the unit cells to indicate the radiation performance.

articleTitle: Analysis of Factors Affecting ELF Wave Intensity Induced by Natural Current Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on EISCAT experiment data, this article analyzes the experimental results of varying the power level of the heating system at different heating frequencies. The analysis reveals the variation of extremely low frequency (ELF) wave intensity with heating frequency and heating system power. Combined with theoretical analysis, it is observed that the variation of total energy absorbed by electrons per unit time in the ionospheric disturbance region exhibits similar characteristics to the variation of radiation wave intensity. This study not only offers a new perspective for understanding the mechanism of ELF wave generation but also provides valuable insights for optimizing ionospheric heating technology.

articleTitle: High-Speed and Low-Energy Phase Change Radio Frequency Switch Using GeTe/Sb Superlattice-Like Film
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Due to the comprehensive performance of the phase change radio frequency (RF) switch, it provides a novel and promising idea for the next generation of new microwave switch. This work reports for the first time that the directly heated phase change RF switch based on [(GeTe 5 nm/Sb 5 nm)]<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> superlattice-like phase change film has the advantage of high speed and low energy consumption. The insertion loss of the phase change RF switch based on [(GeTe 5 nm/Sb 5 nm]<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> superlattice-like is less than 0.9 dB and the isolation is greater than 18.6 dB up to 67 GHz. The total energy consumption of the switch can be as low as 964 nJ, and the switching ratio exceeds 4 orders of magnitude. This increases the prospect of RF switches based on phase change materials, which can be used as key components in future refactoring wireless and 6G communication systems.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Attention-Enhanced DenseNet in Logging Lithology Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Logging lithology identification is a key task in geological exploration, oil and gas development and groundwater resource management. Traditional methods rely on manual analysis, geological experience and rock sample analysis, which are not only time-consuming and laborious, but also susceptible to subjective judgment and data quality, resulting in uncertainty and limitations in the identification results. Currently, most lithology recognition methods use simpler machine learning algorithms and neural networks, with limited recognition accuracy, especially when dealing with complex logging data, which show poor accuracy and insufficient generalization ability, making it difficult to meet the demands of high precision and high efficiency. To address these challenges, we propose a logging lithology recognition method that combines DenseNet with Attention mechanism. The method realizes efficient feature reuse and mitigates the problem of gradient vanishing through dense connectivity, while the Attention mechanism is utilized to enhance the focus on key features and enhance the model's expressive ability and accuracy. The whole model effectively avoids the gradient vanishing problem while maintaining high accuracy and can focus on key features, thus improving the classification performance, which is especially suitable for processing complex high-dimensional data and tasks requiring fine feature recognition. Experimental results show that compared with other neural network models, the recognition accuracy of our method is 13.3% higher than that of the Transformer model and about 10.6% higher than that of the traditional convolutional neural network (CNN) model. This significant improvement not only demonstrates the superiority of combining DenseNet with the Attention mechanism, but also shows the strong potential of the method in parsing complex geologic data.

articleTitle: A Microwave/Millimeter-Wave Triple-Band Shared-Aperture Antenna with High Structure Reuse Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel microwave (MW)/millimetre-wave (MMW) triple-band shared-aperture antenna. It operates as a patch antenna and a transmitarray (TA) antenna in the MW (3.6 GHz) and MMW bands (26 GHz and 39 GHz), respectively. The two types of antennas are integrated efficiently through aperture reuse. To obtain an appropriate focal-to-diameter ratio (F/D) for the TA, a frequency selective surface (FSS) is designed to replace the ground plane of the patch antenna. Due to the band-pass characteristic of the FSS, it can be equivalent to a ground plane for the patch antenna and allows waves to pass through for the TA. The proposed antenna demonstrates good performance in all bands and a high structure reuse efficiency. It can be a promising candidate for 5G multi-band applications.

articleTitle: A Meta-surface Antenna for Satellites' X-band Data Transmission Subsystem Test
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel X-band antenna used for satellites' data transmission subsystem test. The working frequency band of the antenna is 8.00GHz-9.00GHz, which can cover data transmission subsystem's full frequency band. And the 3dB beam width is 80deg, the wide beam can support test application. In addition, the combination of meta-surface and microstrip make the antenna have both advantages, such as wide frequency band and low-profile.

articleTitle: A High- Isolation Quad-Channel Diplexer Based on Dual-Mode T-Shaped Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a high-isolation quad-channel diplexer is proposed with each path consisting of two folded dual-mode T -shaped resonators to reduce the circuit size and improve passband isolation. Due to the controllable transmission zero and resonant frequency of the T -type resonator, it can achieve quad controllable channels with good frequency selectivity in the receiving and transmitting channels. To confirm the feasibility of the theoretical design, we designed, fabricated, and measured prototypes of the diplexer. The measured results of the circuit are in good agreement with the simulation results.

articleTitle: A Study of the EM Scattering from the Sea Skimming Target at the Multi-Scale Sea Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper aims at simulating and analyzing the EM scattering from the sea skimming target at the multi-scale sea environment. The multi-scale sea surface model is set up considering the Bragg structure and the whitecap layers. The sea surface scattering is calculated by a modified Facet Based Small Slope Approximation method (FBSSA). The scattering from the target and the interactions between the target and the sea surface is calculated by the Physical Optics (PO) approximation method, the Equivalent Edge Current (EEC) method as well as the GO-PO method respectively. Finally, the simulations of the EM scattering from the sea skimming target at different sea states are made. The results show the backward EM scattering can get significantly intensified at the higher sea states.

articleTitle: Time Domain Transfer Impedance Measurement of Shielded Cables with Wavelet Denoising Method
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: For the transfer impedance measurement of shielded cables in time domain, the original results may be sensitive to the measurement noises, which is in general superimposed onto the original data. To remove the noisy signals, the wavelet denoising method is used for the high altitude electromagnetic pulse based measurement. To well deal with the noisy signals introduced in high altitude electromagnetic pulse tests, two applicaiton scenarios, i.e., indirect denoising and direct denoising, are considered for the transfer impedance of shielded cable. The denoised results have highlighted that the noisy signals are significantly shrunk for the indirect denoising, and the wavelet denoising method can preserve the essential features of the transfer impedance.

articleTitle: Macro Fibre Composite-Based Active Suppression of Low-Frequency and Broadband Applied in Thin-Walled Composite Beam
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With the development of aerospace technology, the low-frequency noise of aircraft wings has become an urgent issue, and low-frequency noise causes aircraft wing fatigue and even leads to aircraft damage. Since the noise environment of aircraft wings is in the low-frequency range of 5–300 Hz, the existing passive vibration isolation technology has poor adaptability to low frequency. Therefore, it is urgent to have a low-frequency active vibration suppression material suitable for thin-wall structure, which requires low frequency, high response, high sensitivity and broadband. Macro fibre composite (MFC) has the advantages of low frequency, flexibility and high sensitivity. Because of its excellent mechanical and electrical coupling properties, it can effectively suppress aircraft wing noise in low-frequency active vibration suppression devices. This work proposed an MFC-based selffeedback system for low-frequency and broadband applied in a thin-walled composite beam, in which MFCs were attached on the upper and lower surface. The above MFC acted as sensors for continuously sensing the vibration signals, and the other below MFC was utilized to generate inverse vibration to suppress vibration. Optimal vibration suppression is observed at the first-order resonant frequencies of aluminum, stainless steel, and carbon fibre substrates, with suppression rates of 98.00%, 89.90%, and 81.63%, respectively. Excellent broadband vibration suppression effects are also demonstrated at non-resonant frequencies within 100 Hz. Our proposed structure for low-frequency suppression could be further extended to other thin-walled materials, such as carbon fibre plate, epoxy plate, and steel plate, opening up a new avenue in low-frequency and broadband vibration suppression.

articleTitle: A Single Single-Pole-3-Throw RF Phase Change Switch Based on GeTe Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: As an important component in front-end devices, RF switches can not only control the signal on/off, but also configure different units to regulate the overall RF performance of the device. This work designed and investigated the Single-Pole-3-Throw (SP3T) phase-change switch based on GeTe as phase-change material, simulated the electromagnetism of the SP3T switch and prepared a physical switch for RF performance testing. The actual measured insertion loss of the SP3T switch in the 0–67 GHz band is less than 1.67 dB, and the isolation is more than 17.80 dB. The SP3T phase-change switch is characterized by an insertion loss of less than 1.67 dB and an isolation degree of more than 17.80 dB in the 0–67 GHz frequency band, and it has excellent RF performance and good potential market advantages compared with other RF switches.

articleTitle: Implementation and Comparison of Eye Diagram Measurements Based on Clustering Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the eye diagram parameters are measured and calculated by clustering algorithms. The eye diagram results are used as a dataset, and a comparison of the measurement results is carried out to verify the feasibility of the measurement method. Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) is robust to noise and outliers in data. It is chosen as an improved scheme of K-Means, which is more effective in dealing with fuzzy datasets. It has an advantage in terms of computational speed without reducing the accuracy of parameter extraction.

articleTitle: The Simulation of Plasma Sheath and ISAR Imaging of Hypersonic Target
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In recent years, the research on hypersonic flight target has been a hot topic, and it is inevitable to study and discuss the plasma sheath covering the surface of aircraft. The study on the transmission and scattering of electromagnetic waves in plasma sheath is helpful to understand the electromagnetic characteristics of plasma and solve the existing problems in related fields. In this paper, based on the RAM-C experiment of NASA hypersonic vehicle, a simplified model of blunt-cone aircraft is established with reference to the size parameters of its aircraft. In computational fluid dynamics software, the fluid in the outer space of blunt-cone aircraft is numerically calculated by discrete numerical method, and the flow field data of blunt-cone aircraft in the state of 50 km and 10 Mach are obtained. Then, the plasma sheath model covering the target is established by extracting relevant data. The radar cross section data of plasma sheath-coated targets are calculated by physical optics method, and the images of hypersonic target model from different perspectives are obtained by ISAR imaging method, and the electromagnetic scattering characteristics of plasma sheath are analyzed. The experimental results are in line with the theory and have certain reference value.

articleTitle: Dual-Port Phase Mode Antenna with Folded Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a wide-angle-scanning dual-port phase mode antenna with folded spoof surface plasmonic polaritons structure (SSPPs) is proposed. The antenna is constructed by two monopoles and a folded SSPPs. The serrate section uses centrally symmetric SSPPs structure to realize different dispersion characteristics between the upper and lower parts. By changing the phase difference between two ports, different modes can be excited in the serrate structure and achieve beam scanning. Simulated results validate that the proposed antenna can realize upper half space scanning under 3dB beam width in 5.7-6.7GHz.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Bandpass Filter Based on IPD-GaAs Technology with Mushroom-Substrate Integrated Waveguide Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces a millimeter-wave miniaturized filter using GaAs-Ipd(Integrated Passive Device) technology, applied in the 5G N258 band (24.25-27.5GHz). The filter integrates mushroom structures within the Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW). The introduction of mushroom structures into the SIW introduces resonant modes independent of the SIW, enabling effective tuning of resonant frequencies by adjusting the upper and lower dielectric thickness ratio, thereby reducing the filter size. In the SIW, coupling exists between the mushroom structures, allowing multiple mushroom structures to be reasonably loaded into the SIW cavity to achieve a single-cavity multi-mode effect. In this work, a filter with a Cascaded Triplet (CT) structure is designed by integrating three mushroom structures into a single SIW cavity. Simulation results demonstrate that the filter, with a size of 1.3×1.3mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, achieves an insertion loss (IL) of 1.4 dB at the center frequency. The out-of-band rejection exceeds 20 dB in the ranges of 14-21.6 GHz and 29.2-40 GHz, with a transmission zero at 30.44 GHz. The performance of the designed filter closely matches the synthesized results.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement of Pixelated Patch Antennas Based on Localized Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper employs a reinforcement learning algorithm to improve bandwidth for a pixelated patch antenna. Differing from traditional methods that depend on manual tuning and extensive computations, this approach autonomously discerns the relationships between numerically characterized pixelated patch antennas and their S-parameters. Specifically, the implementation of a double deep Q-network (DDQN) and prioritized experience replay allows the model to dynamically adjust learning processes based on a structured exploration of state and action spaces. In this case, pixelated patch antenna configurations are efficiently optimized for maximal bandwidth performance. The learning model systematically tests and refines antenna designs by iteratively adjusting the presence or absence of metal at each pixel, thereby achieving a significant bandwidth increase to 34%. This method not only optimizes the bandwidth efficiently but also suggests promising applications in complex antenna designs.

articleTitle: Isolation and Bandwidth Enhancement of 5G Millimeter-Wave Dual-Band MIMO Antenna Based on Metamaterial Wall
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An isolation- and bandwidth-enhanced 5G mmwave dual-band MIMO antenna is proposed. The proposed antenna composed of a 2×1 28/38GHz dual-band antenna and a metamaterial-based isolation wall. On the one hand, the isolation improvement is achieved by the dual-band bandstop characteristic of the isolation wall. On the other hand, after inserting the isolation wall, the input impedance in both low-and high-band is improved simultaneously. Simulated results illuminate that the isolations at low- and high-band are improved by 26dB and 39dB, respectively. Meanwhile, the operating bandwidths <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\vert \mathrm{S}_{11}\vert < -10\text{dB})$</tex> are largely increased from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$27. 7\sim 30.4\text{GHz}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$36. 1\sim 41.0\text{GHz}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$27. 0\sim 30.3 \text{GHz}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$35.2\sim 45.9\text{GHz}$</tex>, resulting in the bandwidth extensions of 24% and 108%, respectively. The proposed MIMO antenna has the advantages of high isolation, wideband and dual-band operation, which can be used for the 5G millimeter-wave wireless communication system.

articleTitle: Global Ionospheric ROTI Prediction Based on DeepONet
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This study extends our previous research published in IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing [1], which focused on predicting the Slant Total Electron Content (STEC) of the ionosphere using the Deep Operator Network (DeepONet) method. We now advance this work by implementing short-term forecasts of the Rate of Total Electron Content Index (ROTI), broadening the application of the DeepONet operator network in forecasting ionospheric irregularities. This work uses data from February 2023 for training and predicts the ROTI for March 1, 2023, achieving an average Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) accuracy of approximately 0.1 TECU/min. Additionally, the study found that the model's prediction deviations mainly occur near the equator and the poles. This investigation confirms DeepONet's capabilities for effectively forecasting ionospheric conditions, which could significantly improve the operational efficiency of global satellite navigation systems.

articleTitle: Effect of Rainfall on Plane Wave Phase Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: For high-frequency wireless satellite communication scenarios, rain attenuation seriously affects the reliability of the communication system. The phase distortion caused by electromagnetic waves passing through the rain area is an important part of studying rain attenuation. Therefore, this study gives a general process for calculating the spatial distribution of the phase shift rate of plane wave transmission in the rain field. By constructing a spatial rainfall field, the extinction cross section is obtained using the DDA algorithm. Combining the Weibull raindrop spectrum and the M-P raindrop spectrum, a 100GHz high-frequency electromagnetic wave is selected to conduct an example analysis of the spatial distribution of the phase shift rate of the receiving radar aperture. The results show that due to the uneven and random distribution of the rainfall rate in space and the uneven distribution of raindrop size under the same rainfall rate, the phase distribution on the receiving radar aperture plane is random and uneven. This study can support the design and operation of MIMO systems and other radio systems affected by the tropospheric environment.

articleTitle: Simulation Method of Ground Millimeter Wave Scattering Based on Encoded Meta-Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 14th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aiming at the demand of the environmental adaptability and reliability of millimeter wave proximity fuze for the simulation test system of near-field backscattering characteristics of various backgrounds, such as land, green vegetation, and road surfaces. A simulation method for millimeter wave scattering characteristics of complex ground background is proposed. The method can realize both the background equivalent simulation in the energy dimension and the dynamic scene simulation in the time dimension, which solves the technical defects of the traditional simulation method for the dynamic test scene simulation. The test results show that the maximum error and the root mean square error of the two background simulations of grass and concrete pavement are less than 3dB, which meets the demand of simulating the dynamic detection response characteristics of various background millimeter wave near-field and provides a concise and efficient testing method for the practical performance assessment of ground proximity fuze.
